latestRelease.notes:
# Agent

### Prelude

Released on: 2026-08-19

- Please refer to the [7.82.2 tag on integrations-core](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/AGENT_CHANGELOG.md#datadog-agent-version-7822) for the list of changes on the Core Checks

### New Features

- When `infrastructure_mode: end_user_device` is set, the `logon_duration` feature is now enabled automatically, so operators no longer need to set `logon_duration.enabled: true` separately. This setting can still be overridden explicitly in the configuration file if needed.

### Enhancement Notes

- The Agent's embedded Python has been upgraded from 3.13.14 to 3.13.15
- Agents are now built with Go `1.26.6`.

### Bug Fixes

- APM: Raise the messagepack decoder allocation limit for the span `meta_struct` field to 10MiB, so large `meta_struct` entries (as written by LLM Observability) are no longer rejected by the package-wide 500,000 element limit. Other span fields keep the lower limit.
- Disable GPU parallel collection by default to avoid triggering NVML concurrency bugs.
- gpu: fix concurrent calls to NVML GetFieldValues API, that could cause missing NVLink metrics.

### Other Notes

- gpu: GPU inventory payload and GPU tags are only emitted when GPU monitoring is enabled

# Datadog Cluster Agent

### Prelude

Released on: 2026-08-19 Pinned to datadog-agent v7.82.2: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/blob/main/CHANGELOG.rst#7822).

signals.title: IMDS lookups retry every 15s forever when IMDS is unreachable from a container
signals.text: ### Agent version 7.78.1 ### Bug Report On EC2 instances with `HttpPutResponseHopLimit: 1` and `HttpTokens: required`, IMDS is unreachable from the agent when it runs in a container. The hop limit drops the IMDSv2 token response before it reaches the container, and IMDSv1 is refused, so no code path can succeed. `cloud_hostinfo` retries anyway, every 15s, indefinitely. Each attempt blocks a collector slot for ~600ms waiting on a socket, so roughly 4% of the time a collector slot is occupied doing nothing that can ever succeed. Please back the IMDS lookup off to 60s after repeated failures. ### Reproduction Steps 1. Run the agent in a container on an EC2 instance with `HttpPutResponseHopLimit: 1` and `HttpTokens: required`. 2. `agent status collector` — `cloud_hostinfo` shows ~600ms average execution time, indefinitely. 3. From inside the container, `curl -X PUT http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token -H 'X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60'` hangs until timeout, while `curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id` returns 401 in under 10ms. ### Other environment details Seen on EKS Auto Mode, whose nodes default to those metadata options, but nothing here is specific to it — any container on a hop-limited instance should reproduce.

signals.title: add support so DDOT attaches grpc status code tags(rpc.grpc.status_code)
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? This PR adds support so DDOT attaches grpc status code tags(rpc.grpc.status_code). As described in this [ticket](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTELS-685), rpc.grpc.status_code tags were reported to be lost in trace metrics for the DDOT routing method and were showing up as N/A. Now, the grpc status codes are shown properly. The screenshot shows the behaviour after the changes. As well, this ticket adds support for rpc.response.status_code from the latest convention and to interpret it as a gRPC status code only if rpc.system.name is grpc. If rpc.system.name is grpc, it is able to interpret different rpc.response.status_code values: If rpc.system.name is jsonrpc, it is not able to interpret rpc.response.status_code values: Also, this ensures that jsonrpc systems are still able to interpret regular rpc.grpc.status_code values: ### Motivation ### Describe how you validated your changes Tested it locally by running the Otel collector with a sample app service to either pass rpc.response.status_code with an grpc rpc system, confirming it is interpreted as gRPC status code. With a non grpc rpc system, confirmed it is not interpreted. An then ran both systems passing rpc.response.status_code to confirm it shows up for both. ### Additional Notes

signals.title: [Logs Stateful Encoding] transport layer initial implementation
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Implements the "transport" layer of the new gRPC based "stateful encoding" logs protocol (https://github.com/DataDog/agent-payload/pull/443). This explicitly doesn't connect the change to existing pipeline/configuration or pattern extraction code to keep the PR a more reviewable size - follow up PRs will implement that. ### Motivation Partial implementation of experimental new logs protocol. ### Describe how you validated your changes We have tested the full feature end to end against a real Intake as well as in the Lading regression test setup. ### How to Review this PR This change is extracted from https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/43321 which has the full stateful encoding setup. This PR specifically extracts pkg/logs/sender/grpc (without hooking it up to config or integrating pattern extraction) to turn the transport layer into a more reviewable chunk. ./pkg/logs/sender/grpc/DESIGN.md is included to document how this code works. Github now includes file filters on the "Files changed" tab to ignore all the go.mod / go.sum changes: https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/46583/changes?file-filters%5B%5D=.work&file-filters%5B%5D=.yml&file-filters%5B%5D=.go&file-filters%5B%5D=.md#diff-cb098977d66de67165f77535af2410865dc732fbe747d1b90028348c1d9c517b ### Additional Notes Labels: no-changelog: this feature is not fully complete so no changelog is needed yet qa/done: The full feature has been tested via Lading regression tests as well as e2e tests

signals.title: add eviction configs
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Pick up NCM eviction configurations from the datadog.yaml. Use these values in the eviction function. Call the eviction function after we write to the db to ensure that we do not exceed memory constraints. Evictions are tracked under a new Datadog internal metric: `datadog.ncm.store.configs_evicted` ### Motivation ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes ### Local Validation That datadog.yaml is read correctly set `dev/dist/datadog.yaml`: ``` log_level: debug api_key: *** dd_url: 'https://dd.datad0g.com/' hostname: "sophie-local" process_config: process_collection: enabled: true network_devices: config_management: rollback: enabled: true store: min_configs_per_device: 2 max_configs_per_device: 24 max_raw_config_store_bytes: 2000000000 ``` run commands: ``` dda inv agent.build --build-exclude=systemd ./bin/agent/agent run -c ./bin/agent/dist/datadog.yaml ``` View debug logs: ### CML eviction e2e test Confirmed eviction order with simulation on CML - set low number of bytes for store config - change configuration of network device, expecting removal of configurations in alignment with eviction policy - check evicted uuids in logs, confirm that inventory_reported_at does not continue to update for evicted configs in orgstore ### QA flow in CML 1) Configure datadog.yaml file inside of CML yaml file for test case, import lab to CML 2) Make needed configuration changes for test case 3) Validate Boltdb state with the following steps: ssh into vm running agent in cml, display device_config.db in cml as base 64: `sudo base64 /opt/datadog-agent/run/ncm_config.db` copy and paste the db output into a .txt file in local computer convert to a bin file: `base64 -d ~/Documents/cml_boltdb.txt > ~/Documents/cml_boltdb.bin` explore file using ncm show: ``` cd ~/go/src/github.com/DataDog/ndm-tools/ncmshow ./ncmshow ~Documents/cml_boltdb.bin ``` ### Manual test cases 1) Set configuration to: min_configs_per_device: 1, max_configs_per_device: 24, max_raw_config_store_bytes: 8 Get BoltDB state: Change hostname Get BoltDB state: (Should see 2 configs per device, even though min configs is set to 1 it should get overridden to 2. signals.title: feat(serverless-init): add shared infrastructure for AWS MicroVM cloud service
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the shared Go infrastructure that AWS MicroVM cloud-service support depends on. This is the first in a stack of PRs that together deliver full MicroVM observability. ### Motivation The Datadog Agent's serverless-init supports multiple cloud platforms (Cloud Run, Container Apps, etc.) via a `CloudService` abstraction. AWS Lambda MicroVMs are a new deployment target where the Agent runs as an init process inside a Firecracker microVM. Each new platform requires small additions in a few central places before the platform-specific code can be wired in cleanly. This PR makes those additions in isolation so the platform-specific MicroVM PR is a clean diff: - **`pkg/metrics/metricsource.go`** — adds `MetricSourceAWSMicroVMEnhanced`, the metric source tag used on all MicroVM enhanced metrics. - **`pkg/serverless/env/env.go`** — adds `MicroVMImageARNEnvVar` (`AWS_LAMBDA_MICROVM_IMAGE_ARN`), the env var the platform injects with the image ARN. - **`pkg/serializer/internal/metrics/origin_mapping.go`** — maps the new MetricSource to its origin string so metrics are routed correctly in the serializer. - **`comp/dogstatsd/server/impl/default_serverless.go` + `enrich.go`** — threads MicroVM origin/tag enrichment through DogStatsD's serverless path. - **`comp/logs-library/processor/json_serverless_init.go`** — adds a JSON log encoder for structured serverless-init logs, needed for MicroVM's log pipeline. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New unit tests cover the origin mapping and DogStatsD enrichment paths. - All changes are additive; no existing behaviour is altered. Run the unit tests for the packages touched by this PR: ``` dda inv test --targets=./comp/dogstatsd/server/impl,./comp/logs-library/processor,./pkg/metrics,./pkg/serializer/internal/metrics,./pkg/serverless/env ``` ### Additional Notes **PR stack** (each PR bases on the one above): 1. **This PR** — shared infrastructure 2. `microvm-02-cloudservice-run` — `Run()` method on `CloudService` interface 3. `microvm-03-lifecycle-config-childhandle` — lifecycle package primitives 4. `microvm-04-lifecycle-forwarder` — HTTP pass-through proxy 5. `microvm-05-lifecycle-heartbeat` — periodic heartbeat metric 6. `microvm-06-lifecycle-server-wire` — lifecycle HTTP server 7. `microvm-07-microvm-service-wiring` — MicroVM `CloudService` + main wiring 8. `microvm-08-sigusr2-on-run` — SIGUSR2 on `/run` for PRNG reseeding

signals.title: [DO NOT MERGE] One-off e2e run with ADP enabled by default
signals.text: ## Summary Temporarily flips \`data_plane.enabled\` from \`false\` to \`true\` in the agent's compiled-in config default so that every e2e test in the full suite runs against ADP without requiring per-test changes or test duplication. The change is throwaway — close without merging once the CI run completes. This is the same config knob used by the AMP ADP test helpers (DADP-72, see [Slack thread](https://dd.slack.com/archives/C070PQKLLP5/p1783453441368899)). ## How to kick off the full e2e suite Trigger a new pipeline on this branch and set the CI variable: \`\`\` RUN_E2E_TESTS=on \`\`\` That variable hits the \`if_run_all_e2e_tests\` rule in \`.gitlab-ci.yml\` and flips all e2e jobs from manual to \`on_success\`. ## CI findings (ADP 1.5.1, branch jszwedko/run-ci-adp-enabled) ### Fixed in this PR - **Windows MSI \`status_command_infos\`**: All MSI test variants fail because \`agent_behaviour.go\` asserts the status output contains "DogStatsD". When ADP handles DSD, the \`DogStatsD\` status section is absent (the \`EnabledInternal()\` guard prevents registering the status provider). Fixed by accepting either "DogStatsD" or "Dogstatsd Metric Sample" (always present in the Aggregator section). ### Known pre-existing failures (ADP limitations, tracked in Saluki) - **\`TestReplayWithTagEnrichment\`** — ADP doesn't enrich replayed DSD packets with current tagger state. Tracked in Saluki. ### New failures requiring Saluki fixes - **Container DSD tests (ECS \`TestDogtstatsdUDP\`, \`TestDogtstatsdUDS\`; Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods)**: In container environments (ECS, K8s/Kind), fakeintake is configured as \`DD_ADDITIONAL_ENDPOINTS\` rather than \`dd_url\`. ADP doesn't appear to forward DogStatsD metrics to \`additional_endpoints\`, so no metrics arrive at fakeintake. In VM tests where fakeintake IS \`dd_url\` (primary endpoint), DSD forwarding works. This points to an \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding gap in ADP. - The Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods fail to become Ready — the workload pods mount \`/var/run/datadog/dsd.socket\` as a HostPath volume (type \`Socket\`). With ADP enabled, the core agent's DSD server doesn't start (so no socket is created); ADP must create it but apparently doesn't complete socket setup in time or at the expected path. - Root cause: ADP \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding — active Saluki config migration work (issues #2312–#2316) may be the upstream cause. ### Other failures under investigation - **Anomaly detection tests** — under investigation, may be ADP-independent - **GPU tests** — under investigation ## Test plan - No new tests. The goal is to observe which existing e2e tests break when ADP is the default. - \`new-e2e-amp-adp\` (existing) runs the AMP suite filtered to \`--run "ADP"\` tests; this PR covers the rest. **DO NOT MERGE** — this default flip must not land on \`main\`.

signals.title: Pedro.cordeiro/macos ec2 snapshot poc
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Introduces a shared pool of macOS EC2 Dedicated Hosts for the E2E test framework, so macOS test runs stop provisioning (and tearing down) a brand-new Dedicated Host + instance every time. - **Pool package** (`test/e2e-framework/resources/aws/ec2/pool`): discovers idle, tagged macOS EC2 instances and manages their lifecycle via lease records stored in S3, using conditional writes (ETag/If-Match) to arbitrate concurrent acquisition: - `Acquire` claims an idle instance from the pool (`AcquireIdleInstance`), or falls back to a per-developer local instance lookup/provisioning path (`LocalProvisionOptions`) outside CI. - Leases track `idle`/`in-use` status, owner, and `leased_at`, and are namespaced per owner to avoid collisions. - `RevertAndRelease` reverts an instance's root volume to the lease's baseline AMI and republishes it as `idle` on teardown; `RevertInPlace` re-reverts and re-publishes as `in-use` for local dev reuse. - `PublishInitialLease` registers a brand-new pool member's first lease out-of-band (used when auto-provisioning on a local cache miss). - **Provisioning wiring** (`test/e2e-framework/resources/aws/ec2/vm.go`): macOS VM creation now imports an existing pool member (pinning `HostID`/`SubnetID`/AMI via `pulumi.Import` + `IgnoreChanges`, and `RetainOnDelete` so Pulumi never destroys pooled instances) instead of always creating a fresh Dedicated Host. On a local cache miss, it provisions a new Dedicated Host/instance through ordinary Pulumi resources and registers it as a new pool member. - **Teardown wiring** (`test/e2e-framework/testing/e2e/suite.go`): `BaseSuite.releasePoolInstanceIfAny` reverts and releases the pool instance backing a suite's environment at teardown, replacing ad hoc destroy-based cleanup for macOS hosts. - **Bypass flag**: `E2E_MACOS_POOL_ENABLED` (default enabled) lets a run opt out of the pool entirely and fall back to the pre-existing per-run Dedicated Host provisioning; it's meant to be removed once the pool is validated and trusted as the default. - CI-run detection now checks the `CI` env var, so local runs consistently take the per-developer local-provisioning path. ### Motivation Every macOS E2E test run previously stood up a new AWS EC2 Dedicated Host that was used once and then torn down — but AWS bills Dedicated Host allocations in 24-hour minimum increments, so each single test run paid for a full day of macOS instance time. A shared pool of pre-baked, leasable hosts amortizes that 24h allocation across many runs via acquire/release against S3-backed lease state. See [WINA-2931](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2931). ### Describe how you validated your changes - Ran `TestMacosInstallScript` locally in CI-mode (`E2E_PIPELINE_ID` forced) and in local-provisioning mode against a live pool, confirming warm-import acquisition and correct root-volume revert/release on teardown. - Ran four simultaneous `TestMacosInstallScript` invocations against a 2-member pool to exercise acquire-retry contention: the two extra runs correctly queued and waited on `pool.Acquire`'s retry loop until a member was released, then all four passed. - Validated the `E2E_MACOS_POOL_ENABLED=false` bypass path falls back to the pre-existing per-run Dedicated Host provisioning unchanged. ### Additional Notes [WINA-2931]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2931?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: Fix DI proxy dropping when logs_enabled unset
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes the trace-agent Dynamic Instrumentation proxy so it only drops debugger data when the Logs product is explicitly disabled. Previously, an unset `logs_enabled` was treated the same as an explicit `false`, so DI snapshots were silently dropped. The proxy now forwards unless `logs_enabled` (or the deprecated `log_enabled`) is set to `false` and neither key enables logs, matching how the logs agent itself decides to start. ### Motivation Customers reported that DI snapshots were not reaching the intake even though they had not disabled the Logs product. `core.GetBool("logs_enabled")` returns `false` for both "unset" and "explicitly false", so the proxy dropped snapshots any time the setting was omitted. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests in `comp/trace/config/impl` cover the matrix: both keys unset, each key explicitly `false`, the override, and mixed configurations where one key enables logs while the other is `false`.

signals.title: fix(otel-metrics): skip spans with client-computed stats
signals.text: ## What Datadog tracing libraries can emit spans as OTLP while also computing APM stats client-side (CSS). Those spans carry `_dd.stats_computed` as a resource or span attribute. Before this PR, the DDOT connector did not inspect that marker. It converted the spans and recomputed hits, errors, and duration, double-counting stats the tracing library had already produced. After this PR, the connector treats `_dd.stats_computed` as a `ResourceSpans`-level signal. When the marker is truthy on the resource or any span it contains, every span in that `ResourceSpans` is excluded from the connector's concentrator. Other resources in the same OTLP batch remain eligible for Agent-computed stats. ## Why resource scope is correct - Client-side stats are enabled or disabled for the whole ddtrace client; there is no partial per-span enablement. - The ddtrace OTLP path emits `_dd.stats_computed` as a resource attribute. - The Agent and built-in collector processors preserve or copy the resource and its attributes when forwarding, batching, splitting, or regrouping trace data. One marked span is therefore sufficient evidence for its containing `ResourceSpans`, but not for other resources that happen to share the same `ptrace.Traces` payload. ## Changes - Detect `_dd.stats_computed` on both resource and span attributes. - Promote a span-level marker to its containing `ResourceSpans`. - Skip every span belonging to a client-computed resource while retaining unmarked resources. - Return before span indexing and top-level detection when the entire payload is client-computed. - Allocate the computed-resource set only when a marker is found. - Treat absent, empty, or `false` markers as not client-computed; other non-empty values enable the skip. ## Performance The same focused benchmark was run at the PR's base commit and current head on an Apple M4 Max with `GOMAXPROCS=1`. The payload contains 10 resources with 10 spans each. | Scenario | Before PR | After PR | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Client stats enabled | ~281.6 us/op | ~0.82 us/op | ~344x faster | | Client stats disabled | ~282.5 us/op | ~283.7 us/op | +0.4%, within benchmark noise | With client stats enabled, memory falls from 114,808 B/op to 712 B/op and allocations from 855 to 5. With client stats disabled, memory and allocations are unchanged at 114,808 B/op and 855 allocations/op. The added no-marker resource scan measures approximately 0.50 us per 100 spans with zero allocations. That is about 0.18% of the baseline conversion cost, or roughly 5 ns per span for this payload. ## Validation ```text bazel test //pkg/trace/otel/stats:stats_test bazel test //comp/otelcol/otlp/components/connector/datadogconnector:datadogconnector_test ``` Both targets pass. Tests cover marker parsing, resource-level markers, promotion of a span marker to its containing resource, and retaining unmarked resources in the same payload.

signals.title: [Backport 7.81.x]  Windows: don't let registry DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS fallback override explicit install args
signals.text: Backport 32353f859276f5283be48e7abe1a615891312a63 from #54125. ___ ### What does this PR do? Prevents a `getenv()` fallback (registry-derived `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS`, service-derived `DDAGENTUSER_NAME`) from silently overriding an explicit value passed via install args on a Fleet Automation install/upgrade. ### Motivation Follow-up to #53958, addressing a [review concern](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54081#discussion_r3642641460) that also applies to `main`. `getenv()`'s fallbacks for `AgentUserKeepRights` (registry) and `AgentUserName` (running service) don't know about raw install args (`ctx.WindowsArgs`), a separate path an operator/Fleet task can use to pass these properties explicitly. Since `msi.Cmd()` always places typed properties after raw args on the final command line regardless of option order, a stale fallback value would win over an explicit one, reversing the operator's intent. `AgentUserPassword` has no such fallback and isn't affected. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `TestArgsHaveProperty`: property present/absent/nil args, no false-positive prefix match, covers both `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS` and `DDAGENTUSER_NAME`. - New E2E suite `TestAgentKeepRightsFleetUpgrade` (`test/new-e2e/tests/installer/windows/agent_keep_rights_fleet_test.go`), driving the real Fleet Automation experiment lifecycle (`StartExperiment`/`PromoteExperiment`) against a stable baseline pinned to 7.81.0 (the first release with `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS`), registered in the `new-e2e-installer-windows` CI matrix: - `TestKeepRightsSurvivesFleetUpgrade` — regression test for #53958. - `TestKeepRightsExplicitArgWinsOnFleetUpgrade` — regression test for this PR, using `StartExperimentMSIArgs` to inject an explicit override at experiment time. Both E2E tests passed CI after two fixes to the tests themselves (a log-filename collision from calling `installPreviousAgentVersion()` twice, and pinning the stable baseline version since the pipeline's default "last stable" pointer predates the `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS` feature) — the underlying fix required no changes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [WP] Read OTel thread local context records (OTEP 4947)
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds support for reading span/trace IDs from native applications using the OpenTelemetry Thread Local Context Record format (OTel spec #4947) in the CWS eBPF security module. The implementation adds a new eBPF read path that: Discovers the OTel TLSDESC TLS variable offset (registered by user-space) Dereferences the TLS pointer to locate the OTel Thread Local Context Record This targets native applications using ELF TLSDESC (C, C++, Rust, Java/JNI, .NET/FFI, Python native extensions). ### Motivation The OpenTelemetry specification defines a standard mechanism for SDKs to publish thread-level trace context (trace ID, span ID) through ELF Thread Local Storage so that out-of-process readers like eBPF probes can correlate security events with distributed traces. Supporting this standard allows CWS to automatically pick up span context from any OTel-instrumented native application without requiring Datadog-specific instrumentation. ### Describe how you validated your changes * All modified Go packages (probe/erpc, probe/constantfetch, ebpf/probes, ptracer, probe) build cleanly * The C syscall tester compiles successfully with the new otel-span-open command * Added a functional test (TestOTelSpan) that: * Creates a __thread TLS variable in C, computes its offset from fsbase via arch_prctl(ARCH_GET_FS) * Registers the offset with eBPF via the new REGISTER_OTEL_TLS_OP eRPC operation * Fills an OTel Thread Local Context Record with a known trace ID and span ID in W3C byte order * Triggers an open() syscall and verifies the correct trace/span IDs appear in the captured security event ### Additional Notes

signals.title: fix(remoteagentregistry): canonicalize local metric help
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes Core Agent telemetry HELP text canonical when Remote Agent Registry (RAR) merges incoming Prometheus telemetry. The telemetry component records HELP text for metric families it creates in the normal `/telemetry` registry. When RAR receives a remote family with the same name, it uses that local HELP text when constructing the forwarded Prometheus descriptor. Remote-only families retain the remote agent's HELP text. ### Motivation Prometheus requires metric families that share a name to use identical HELP text. A remote agent can currently supply a different description for a metric also emitted by Core Agent, causing the combined telemetry gather to fail. The Core Agent definition is the authoritative local contract. This includes the Core Agent DogStatsD client byte counters added in #54381. The regression coverage verifies that Core Agent's `dogstatsd_client__bytes_sent` HELP wins over incompatible ADP text while retaining the ADP sample and authoritative `emitter` label. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/core/telemetry/impl:impl_test //comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl:impl_test --test_output=errors` - `git diff --check` - Independent spec-compliance and code-quality reviews. `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/telemetry/impl,./comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl --timeout=120` and `dda inv linter.go --targets=./comp/core/telemetry/impl,./comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl --timeout=120` were blocked before compilation by an internal dependency-mirror HTTP 403 for `github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/extension/healthcheckextension@v0.158.0`, which is in its mirror cooldown window. ### Additional Notes The canonical HELP catalog deliberately covers metrics created through the telemetry component's counter, gauge, and histogram factory APIs. It excludes `DefaultMetric` and opaque direct `RegisterCollector` registrations, which are not part of RAR's normal telemetry registry merge path.

signals.title: [ACTP] package and activate par-control
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Packages and activates split-mode PAR on Linux and Windows hosts: - installs `par-control` and process-manager definitions for it and the on-demand executor; - adds Agent package, installer, and Windows executable-resource wiring; - preserves a standard Unix service `PATH` for process-manager children; - adds fake-OPMS support plus Linux and Windows lifecycle/bootstrap E2E suites and CI jobs. Two details about how the definitions delegate to `dd-procmgrd`: - Windows has no console for a service to inherit, so the `par-control` definition redirects `stdout`/`stderr` to `<ETC_ROOT>/logs/par-control.log` instead of the binary managing its own log file. `dd-procmgrd` now creates a missing stdio parent directory rather than silently falling back to inherit on a fresh install. - The PAR definitions set `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR=${DD_CONF_DIR}/managed/datadog-agent/stable`, which `dd-procmgrd` expands from the supervising unit, so a stable or experiment unit selects the matching config tree. Hardcoding the rendered stable path would have made the control plane and executor read stable policies during an experiment while the core Agent read the experiment's. This matches what the DDOT definition already does. Windows keeps reading `fleet_policies_dir` from the registry, as `pkg/config/setup/config_windows.go` does, because there are no experiment services there. Docker and Kubernetes deployments remain monolithic. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages:packages_test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages/embedded:tmpl_test //pkg/procmgr/rust:dd-procmgrd_test` - `dda inv linter.go --module=test/new-e2e --targets=./tests/privateactionrunner` The installer test now pins the full `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR` value for both definitions; asserting only the key name would not catch a regression to a hardcoded path. Live Linux and Windows E2E execution is left to CI. _Stack 9 of 9; based on #54594._

signals.title: [ACTP] add par-control resolved configuration
signals.text: ## this is in draft again, i'm investigating reusing saluki ### What does this PR do? Adds configuration and identity bootstrap for `par-control`. The reason this is a big PR is because some config loading behavior had to be adapted from Go to Rust. `par-control` now resolves agent and PAR config in _mostly_ the same way as the Go config loader. On startup it runs the new Go `ensure-enrollment` command (#54870) to detect or perform enrollment, then loads the identity. Note that unlike in the Go config loader, unresolved `ENC[...]` secrets are rejected. We did not (yet) implement the Agent secret-backend protocol or FIPS configuration transforms to lower the scope of this work. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo test -p par-control` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo clippy -p par-control --all-targets -- -D warnings` _Stack 4 of 9; based on #54870 and followed by #54591._

signals.title: [ACTP] add par-control executor channel
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the authenticated local gRPC channel between `par-control` and the Go executor: - health and readiness checks; - workflow signing-key synchronization that keeps the executor alive while synchronization is in progress without counting it as an active action. The executor's idle tracking gains a distinct activity counter for this, so non-action work suppresses idle exit while `ActiveActions` still reports only running actions; - action dispatch and terminal outcomes; - Unix-socket and Windows named-pipe transports using the Agent IPC certificate; - message limits sized for large action payloads. This layer introduces the crate's generated-bindings module and the local transport helpers, since it is the first one that needs executor protos and mTLS. OPMS polling and orchestration remain in later layers. ### Validation Focused Go and Rust tests cover the protocol, key synchronization and idle interaction, transport, and message limits. Proto changes are Bazel-validated because Cargo and Bazel use separate generated bindings. - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test //pkg/privateactionrunner/executor:executor_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo test -p par-control` _Stack 5 of 9; based on #54590 and followed by #54592._

signals.title: [ACTP] add par-control OPMS client
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the authenticated OPMS client for `par-control`: - ES256 runner JWT signing; - task dequeue, heartbeat, and terminal publication; - runner health checks; - proxy, TLS, retry, and wire behavior matching the Go runner. Orchestration policy remains in the next layer. ### Validation Rust unit and HTTP/TLS contract tests cover request signing, payloads, pacing, proxying, and TLS behavior. Native TLS coverage runs on Linux and Windows. _Stack 6 of 9; based on #54591 and followed by #54593._
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: [ACTP] orchestrate par-control tasks
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the production `par-control` orchestration loop. It dequeues tasks with bounded concurrency, starts the executor on demand, synchronizes signing keys, dispatches actions, and publishes outcomes. Executor idle shutdown is self-owned by the Go executor rather than driven by `par-control` process-manager calls. Task heartbeats run from dequeue through cold start, execution, and terminal publication. Runner health checks are independent of task flow, and shutdown drains in-flight work without calling `dd-procmgrd` from the shutdown path. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo clippy --manifest-path pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` _Stack 7 of 9; based on #54592 and followed by #54594._

signals.title: [ACTP] wire split runner ownership
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the monolithic Go runner stand down when split mode is enabled on supported Linux and Windows host installations. Containers and unsupported platforms keep the monolithic runner because they do not yet launch the complete replacement topology. This preserves the invariant that exactly one runner polls OPMS without disabling the only available runner. ### Validation - `bazel test //comp/privateactionrunner/impl:impl_test` Tests cover Linux and Windows hosts, containers, and unsupported platforms. _Stack 8 of 9; based on #54593 and followed by #54529._

signals.title: [CWS-6628] Implement the unshare syscall event
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds a public `unshare` CWS event carrying the requested namespace flags, so detection rules can match the syscall itself rather than the name of the calling binary: ``` unshare.flags & CLONE_NEWNET > 0 unshare.flags & (CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET) > 0 && process.file.name != "docker" ``` New SECL surface: `unshare.flags` (bitmask, `Clone flags` constants) and `unshare.retval`. 12 `CLONE_*` constants are registered. ### Motivation Jira: [CWS-6628](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628) (also filed as [CWS-6778](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778) — duplicates). Requested by the detection guild. Recent Linux LPE exploits call `unshare` **directly** to create a new network namespace and thereby obtain `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. Today CWS can only catch this via `process.executable.name == "unshare"`, which misses every exploit that invokes the syscall from its own code. > [!NOTE] > The Jira description claims this complements an existing `setns` event. There is no `setns` instrumentation in CWS — `setns` appears only in the syscall-number tables used by the syscall-monitor event. This is CWS's first namespace-lifecycle event. Scope is unchanged; the ticket framing is just wrong. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `pkg/security/tests/unshare_test.go` with per-flag rules plus a combined `CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET` case (the actual exploit shape), asserting the exact raw bitmask and `retval`. The `syscall_tester` helper invokes `unshare(2)` **directly** rather than exec'ing `unshare(1)`, since catching direct syscall callers is the point. Verified locally: | Check | Result | |---|---| | eBPF C compiles — kprobe, fentry, syscall-wrapper | all 3 objects rebuilt; `tracepoint/"handle_sys_unshare_exit"` present | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/...` | 1420 passed | | `dda inv security-agent.build-functional-tests` | testsuite + `syscall_tester` build clean | | Codegen idempotent | re-ran generation, byte-identical output | | `dda inv linter.go` on secl, probe, serializers, ebpf | 0 issues | > [!IMPORTANT] > **KMT functional tests have not been run** — they need a real kernel. Since this modifies an event the mount resolver depends on, please run `TestUnshareEvent` **plus the mount, pivot_root and network suites** before merging. `syscall_tester.c:test_new_netns_exec` already calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, so this event will start firing inside existing network tests. ### Additional Notes <details> <summary>Why the public event reuses event ordinal 46, and why that matters</summary> `unshare` was already hooked, but narrowly: the hook bailed out unless `CLONE_NEWNS` was set, and the resulting `unshare_mntns` event was swallowed in userspace after registering the mount-namespace copy (`field:"-"`, never dispatched to rules). That internal event fires **once per cloned mount** — `hook_make_visible`, `hook_attach_mnt`, `hook___attach_mnt`, `hook_attach_recursive_mnt` and `hook_propagate_mnt` each call `handle_new_mount()` for a distinct mount, which tail-calls through to `dr_mount_stage_two_callback` → `send_event`. Correct for mount bookkeeping; wrong for detection, where a rule must fire once per syscall. So the two concerns are now separate event types: - **`EVENT_UNSHARE` (ordinal 46, reusing the old slot)** — public, per-syscall. Full process/cgroup/span context plus the raw flags bitmask, sent once from the exit hook. - **`EVENT_UNSHARE_MNTNS` (newly appended)** — internal, per-mount. Semantics unchanged, still consumed by `handleNewMount` and never dispatched to rules. Keeping the *public* event at ordinal 46 is load-bearing. `probe_ebpf.go` packs enabled events as `1 << (eventType - 1)` into a **`uint64`**, mirrored kernel-side in `helpers/events.h`. `PivotRootEventType` is ordinal 64 — the last representable bit, which is exactly why `LastEventType = PivotRootEventType`. A newly appended public type would be ordinal 69 and therefore permanently unreachable by `is_event_enabled()` and by `applyDefaultFilterPolicies()`. The internal event doesn't care, since internal events are never gated by that mask. </details> <details> <summary>Event volume</summary> Bounded by a single gate: **`is_event_enabled(EVENT_UNSHARE)`** — no event at all when no loaded rule references `unshare.*`. Every `unshare` call is reported once that gate opens, so all 12 exposed `CLONE_*` constants are matchable and the `flags` field carries the full raw bitmask. An earlier revision also filtered kernel-side on `CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID`. That was dropped in review: it silently made rules on the other exposed constants (`CLONE_NEWUTS`, `CLONE_NEWIPC`, `CLONE_NEWTIME`, …) unable to fire. Per-flag volume control belongs in `unshare` approvers, as a follow-up. `CLONE_NEWNS` is always *cached* regardless of the gate, because the mount resolver depends on that hook entry. </details> <details> <summary>Known gap and follow-ups</summary> - In `handle_new_mount` (`mount.h`), if the mount bookkeeping bails early it calls `pop_syscall()`, dropping the cache entry before the exit hook runs — so that particular `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` produces no public event. Narrow degraded path, mirrors existing behaviour, but a real coverage hole for `CLONE_NEWNS` specifically. - ebpfless/ptracer support deferred, as `setrlimit` did. - `setns` instrumentation (the join-side signal) not in scope. - Four existing events (ordinals 65–68: `SampleRefresh`, `SetSid`, `Nop`, `Socket`) are already unreachable by the `enabled_events` mask and silently stay that way. Widening it past 64 bits is separate, cross-cutting work worth filing. </details> [CWS-6628]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [CWS-6778]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: [procmgr] Windows spawn profiles foundation
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Introduces **Windows spawn profiles** in dd-procmgr so managed children can run under different security contexts: - **Privileged**: spawn as LocalSystem (supervisor primary token) - **AgentUser**: spawn as the agent service account (`ddagentuser`) Adds the Windows spawn stack (token logon, user profile load, supervision job, suspended `CreateProcessAsUserW`), a **privileged spawn catalog** that rejects unexpected command/args/env for privileged children, and **gRPC named-pipe caller authentication** (admin for mutating RPCs; agent-profile children may read but not Start/Stop other catalog entries). Separates **spawn credential resolution** from installer identity: - **`AgentAccount`**: who the Agent was installed as (registry, LSA, gMSA classification) - **`SpawnCredential`**: how `CreateProcessAsUserW` obtains its primary token (`InheritSupervisor` vs `Logon`) Privileged spawn verifies the duplicated supervisor token is LocalSystem before proceeding (guards console/dev fallback). Also refactors the daemon runtime into a **`Supervisor` event loop** plus `ProcessManager` handlers, and runs **dd-procmgr-service as LocalSystem** so agent-profile spawn can read the agent password from LSA. Includes **list/describe spawn identity** from [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568): `profile`, `user`, and `runtime_user` in the proto, API, and `dd-procmgr` CLI. **Stack context (PR 1):** | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | This PR | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI + list/describe (#53568) | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | **Explicitly deferred:** config gates (#54732), secret-backend cache invalidation (#54734), process-agent dual-mode (#54735), full `ReloadConfig` (#55080). RPC/CLI for reload stay in this PR but return `UNIMPLEMENTED` until #55080. ### Motivation Process-agent on Windows must run as LocalSystem; other agent children should stay on the agent user. Spawn profiles make that explicit and enforceable at spawn time, and are a prerequisite for moving process-agent supervision off legacy SCM in #54735. LocalSystem MSI lands here so agent-profile children (ADP, PAR, DDOT) can spawn without waiting for #54735. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Bazel/Cargo procmgr Rust unit tests (Linux + Windows CI), including `SpawnCredential` resolution tests and cfg(test) harness that duplicates the supervisor token on non-LocalSystem runners (no registry/LSA in unit tests) - Privileged spawn catalog and spawn-profile unit tests (`pkg/procmgr/rust/...`) - COAT package tests (`pkg/procmgr/coat/...`) - Windows new-e2e (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-runtimes/procmgr/`): - ADP running, restart, describe, and COAT telemetry - Spawn identity: procmgr service as LocalSystem, agent-profile children as installer user, userprofile env, admin Create pipe auth - Linux new-e2e: shared CLI tests plus DDOT running, restart, and describe (`procmgr_nix_test.go`) - PAR Windows E2E is unchanged on `main` (`par_procmgr_win_test.go`, not part of this diff) ### Additional Notes - **List/describe:** [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) was merged into this branch; release note ships here. - **Env expansion:** Restores optional `${VAR}` / `try_expand_env_vars` from [#54168](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54168) (lost during rebase). - **Fleet:** DDOT extension uninstall uses `ReloadOrRestartProcmgr()` (reload stub → SCM restart fallback). No process-agent dual-mode changes in this PR. - **ReloadConfig:** Proto and `dd-procmgr reload` remain for API compatibility; handler returns `UNIMPLEMENTED` until [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080). - **Windows DDOT E2E:** Reload-after-yaml tests removed from this PR (reload is deferred to #55080). Linux DDOT smoke tests remain. - **MSI:** After switching `dd-procmgr-service` to LocalSystem, restore **Manual** start type on upgrade so hosts left Disabled by older installers recover ([#55130](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55130) context). - **Shutdown:** `ShutdownBudget` is anchored to the SCM stop signal so ordered teardown shares the service control wait window. - **SpawnCredential:** Production registry/LSA/gMSA resolution is `#[cfg(not(test))]` so Bazel Clippy on `rust_test` targets does not treat it as dead code. - Supersedes the spawn portion of [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249).

signals.title: [procmgr] Config gates for processes.d auto-start
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds **config gates** to dd-procmgr so `processes.d` definitions can use `condition_config_any` to auto-start only when Agent config says they should. Implementation mirrors the Windows legacy SCM startup checks in `dependent_services_windows.go` and Agent config resolution: - YAML lookup via saphyr (case-insensitive keys, flattened dotted keys, merge keys, permissive parse fallback) - Go yaml.v2 parity for gate file loading: first document only in multi-doc streams; YAML 1.1 bool/int/float coercion on plain untagged scalars; quoted or explicitly tagged scalars use ParseBool only - Environment bindings (`DD_*`) with Agent precedence (ignore empty values, no trim before `ParseBool`, legacy `process_config.enabled` transforms) - Fleet policy merge - Derived `system_probe_config.enabled` (USM/NPM/security knobs, sk-tracer and discovery adjustments, end-user-device infrastructure mode overrides) - Windows: read `DD_*` overrides from the core Agent SCM `Environment` registry when not set in the procmgr process env Wires gate evaluation into `ManagedProcess` auto-start and on-failure restart paths (not config reload; that lands in #55080). **Stack context:** PR 2. Builds on [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) (`jose/procmgr-spawn-profiles`), which already includes list/describe ([#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568)). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI (includes #53568) | | 2 | This PR | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation Moving subservices (starting with process-agent) to dd-procmgr requires the supervisor to apply the same start/stop rules as the Agent today. Without config gates, a `processes.d` entry would always spawn when registered, which breaks parity with legacy SCM and fleet policy. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/` (env bindings, YAML load, system-probe derivations) - Integration tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate.rs` (process_config transforms, fleet/EUD overrides, multi-document YAML streams, Go yaml.v2 scalar parity) - `may_auto_start` / `condition_config_any` wiring tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/process.rs` - Windows procmgr Rust build, rustfmt, clippy, and tests in CI ### Additional Notes - No `ENC[...]` / secret backend resolution in this PR (fleet policy `ENC[...]` values are not resolved here either). - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Schema comment sync in `pkg/config/schema/yaml/process_config.yaml` and `core_schema.yaml` for env binding documentation. - Sync comments in `pkg/system-probe/config/` so procmgr gate derivations stay aligned with Go `adjust*` / module enablement logic. - Restores sketch v3beta shadow schema defaults accidentally renamed during the config-gates split. - Linux `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR` for the procmgr systemd unit is deferred to #54168 and a follow-up unit-env change.

signals.title: [procmgr] Secret backend resolution for config gates
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Resolves `ENC[...]` values during config gate evaluation so dd-procmgr matches Agent secret handling. Adds: - `config_gate/secrets.rs`: resolve handles via `secret_backend_command`, native `secret_backend_type`, and `multi_secret_backends` (same precedence as the core Agent) - Platform secret backend runners (Windows `CreateProcessAsUserW` under the Agent account; Unix setuid when procmgr runs as root for Privileged children) - `secret_backend_exec.rs`: shared spawn, timeout, concurrent stdout drain, process-group termination, and bounded reader join - Executable permission checks before spawn: Windows DACL validation (`secret_backend_rights.rs`) and Unix mode-bit checks (mirrors `filesystem.CheckRights`, honors `secret_backend_command_allow_group_exec_perm`) - Fail closed on unresolved pre-fleet secrets: env and base YAML `ENC[...]` resolution errors block config gates instead of falling through to lower-priority sources - Reject empty secret backend response values (Agent parity with `fetch_secret.go`) - Unix privilege drop: `initgroups` for the agent service user before `setgid`/`setuid` when dropping from root - Agent config precedence for backend settings: `DD_SECRET_BACKEND_*` env (including core Agent SCM `Environment` on Windows) over `datadog.yaml` - `clear_secret_caches()` helper exported for the reload PR; not wired to manager reload here Fleet policy `ENC[...]` values stay unresolved here, matching Agent `MergeFleetPolicy` running after secret resolution. **Stack context:** PR 3. Builds on [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) (`jose/procmgr-config-gates`). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | This PR | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (merged) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload (calls `clear_secret_caches`) | ### Motivation PR 2 config gates read YAML, env, and fleet policy, but many customers gate features with secret-backed settings (`ENC[api_key]`, secret-backed booleans, etc.). Without secret resolution, gates would mis-evaluate and auto-start behavior would diverge from the Agent. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/secrets.rs` and config gate integration tests (serialized env to avoid cross-test leakage) - Coverage for fail-closed unresolved ENC, empty backend values, fleet ENC left unresolved, and secret-backed env/YAML gate paths - Windows procmgr Rust build/tests in CI - Linux CI: secret-backend tests run under the agent service user where required ### Additional Notes - Secret backends always run as the core Agent service account, not as the procmgr supervisor (LocalSystem) or a Privileged managed child. - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Invokes `secret-generic-connector` when no custom `secret_backend_command` is configured. - Addresses Codex and Autotest review feedback from the initial PR iteration (fail-closed ENC, process groups, Unix groups/ACL, empty values).

signals.title: [procmgr] Supervise process-agent on Windows via dd-procmgr
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Moves Windows **process-agent** supervision to **dd-procmgr** using the same dual-mode pattern as PAR: - Fleet installer writes `processes.d/datadog-agent-process.yaml` under the MSI install root (shared `install_root` helper, `#54168` `tmpl/gen/windows/` codegen layout) - `condition_config_any` gates auto-start on process collection settings (inherits secret-backend resolution from the base branch) - Legacy `datadog-process-agent` SCM service is suppressed when procmgr owns process-agent - Agent startup waits on `dd-procmgr-service` before starting gated legacy children; independent services (sysprobe, security-agent, installer) start without blocking on procmgr - Process-agent runs under dd-procmgr's **Privileged** spawn profile via the embedded catalog for `datadog-agent-process` (from [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731)); the fleet YAML does not set `spawn_profile` - COAT migratable-services catalog includes process-agent so adoption telemetry (`management_mode`, `procmgr_process_running`) tracks the migration **Stack context:** PR 4. Builds on [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) → [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) → [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731). List/describe ([#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568)) is parallel and is not a parent of this PR. Reload lands in [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | This PR | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (parallel on spawn profiles) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation We want subservices on dd-procmgr instead of SCM. Process-agent needs LocalSystem on Windows; other agent children should stay on the agent user. This PR wires the product integration once the procmgr foundation (PRs 1–3) is in place. `dd-procmgr-service` already runs as LocalSystem from [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731). ### Describe how you validated your changes - Go unit tests for dependent Windows service startup (`dependent_services_windows_test.go`) - Go unit tests for fleet installer templates and YAML path substitution (`processmanager/...`) - COAT unit tests for the new process-agent migratable service entry - New Windows E2E: process-agent supervised by procmgr, runs as LocalSystem, legacy SCM stopped - Windows E2E: privileged catalog rejects tampered `processes.d` YAML (args, env, stdio) ### Additional Notes - Linux process-agent stays on systemd for now. Legacy SCM service registration is not removed yet. - Process-agent `processes.d` config uses the shared `install_root` helper (same as PAR/ADP). MSI `RemoveFolderEx` handles uninstall/rollback cleanup; no per-file MSI rollback custom actions. - Includes release note `windows-process-procmgr-dual-mode-b7d2e4a1c8f03962.yaml`. - Closes/supersedes [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249) once the full stack merges.

signals.title: feat(softinv): report the OS and OEM kernel-mode drivers
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Extends the software inventory beyond installed applications with two new software types, `os` and `driver`: | Platform | Type | Source | |---|---|---| | Windows | `driver` | `Win32_SystemDriver`, plus `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` joined against `Win32_PnPEntity` | | Windows | `os` | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion` | | macOS | `os` | `/System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist` | **Operating system.** One entry whose version advances, rather than one entry per update. An update is an event, not an installed item whose version moves, so it would produce a permanently static entry — and the host SBOM already carries installed KBs. Name and product code are constant, because the backend keys an item on name + product code with the version excluded; anything version-derived in either field would make an upgrade read as remove + install. The version carries the full patch level: `10.0.26100.4652` on Windows including the UBR, `15.6 (24G84)` on macOS including the build that supplemental updates and RSRs advance. **Drivers.** Only OEM and third-party drivers are reported; the drivers that ship with Windows are excluded. Two sources, because each sees what the other cannot. `Win32_SystemDriver` covers drivers registered as kernel services, including software-only ones — EDR minifilters, network and DLP filters — that have no PnP device node. The class carries no version or vendor, so both come from the version resource of the image path; only the numeric `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` version is accepted, since the `FileVersion` string is routinely decorated or comma-separated. Image paths are normalized (`\??\`, `\SystemRoot\`, `%SystemRoot%`, relative) and MUI display names (`@<dll>,-<id>`) resolved with `SHLoadIndirectString`. Filtered on the binary's `CompanyName`, the only vendor signal the class offers; an absent `CompanyName` is kept, since an unattributed kernel driver is worth seeing. Identity is the service name, which Windows guarantees unique. `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` covers packages bound to a device that register no kernel service of their own, which the first source cannot see. Selected by the INF being published as `oemNN.inf` — `Manufacturer` is not used, because Microsoft's inbox INFs report generic strings such as `(Standard system devices)` and Windows also ships inbox INFs authored by hardware vendors, so filtering on it would keep hundreds of inbox drivers. One `Win32_PnPEntity` query is joined in memory to skip devices that already have a service; a query per device would spend the entire time budget on the join. Identity is the device name, the field the class offers that survives a driver update. Known limitations: UMDF user-mode drivers register no kernel service, and a driver whose service entry is created, loaded, then deleted is invisible. This is an inventory of registered drivers, not of code currently in the kernel. **Deadline.** Each collector is bounded at 90s in the shared snapshot runner. A timeout is fatal, because a timed-out enumeration is an unknown state and a missing row reads downstream as a removal; zero rows is still a valid result. A hung native call cannot be cancelled — the WMI library takes no context — so a collector that misses its deadline is not started again until it returns. ### Motivation The inventory only covered installed applications, leaving OS patch level and kernel drivers invisible — two of the most useful signals for fleet visibility and compliance. The deadline is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: these sources can block, and a single slow `Collect()` previously stalled the whole snapshot with no upper bound. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Windows unit tests run and pass in CI (`tests_windows-x64`); macOS unit tests pass locally; `bazel test //pkg/inventory/software:software_test` passes. - `dda inv linter.go` clean, and clean again under `GOOS=windows`, which type-checks the Windows-tagged files and their tests. - Coverage: deadline and in-flight behaviour, both driver filters, the PnP/service join including case mismatch and devices missing from `Win32_PnPEntity`, path normalization and MUI resolution, the numeric-version requirement, identity stability across a version bump for both driver sources, and entry-ID uniqueness once the new families merge with application entries. - Real-host integration tests compare collected drivers against the `Services` registry key, assert nothing Microsoft-published survives the service filter, and log the OEM/inbox split per source; the macOS one asserts the running version against `sw_vers -productVersion`. - Driver payloads from a real Windows host were inspected end to end. That caught two drivers reporting an unresolved MUI reference as their name, fixed in 2741b66. ### Additional Notes - A fatal error from any single collector still drops the whole snapshot (existing behaviour). - PnP-sourced entries carry no `install_paths`, because `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` names no binary. - Enable with `software_inventory.enabled: true`, which drives both the system-probe module and the core agent component. No status or flare changes were needed, since `populateStatus` already groups by `Source`. - Worst-case snapshot duration is bounded per collector, not globally, so it scales with collector count. A snapshot-wide ceiling would be a separate change.

signals.title: ci: default to GIT_DEPTH=1, full clone for jobs needing git history
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Sets a repo-wide `GIT_DEPTH: 1` default in `.gitlab-ci.yml` to speed up job checkouts, and adds `GIT_DEPTH: 0` overrides on the jobs whose scripts (or the invoke tasks they call) run history-dependent git operations: - `.gitlab/build/source_test/golang_deps_diff.yml` (`golang_deps_diff` — `git merge-base` via `go-deps.diff`) - `.gitlab/test/e2e/e2e.yml` (`.new_e2e_template` — `git merge-base` for `--impacted` test selection) - `.gitlab/.pre/ci_configuration.yml` (`test_gitlab_compare_to`, `compute_gitlab_ci_config`, `lint_github_actions_shellcheck` — all use `git merge-base`) - `.gitlab/build/binary_build/fakeintake.yml` (`fakeintake_check_version_bump` — `git merge-base` + reading a file at the merge-base commit) - `.gitlab/deploy/internal_kubernetes_deploy/internal_kubernetes_deploy.yml` (`notify-slack` — `git log` over a commit range for the changelog) - `.gitlab/build/lint/technical_linters.yml` (`lint_releasenotes_rst` — `git merge-base`) - `.gitlab/.pre/setup/setup.yml` (`setup_agent_version` — `git describe --tags`, needs full history to find the nearest tag) Jobs that already had an explicit `GIT_DEPTH`/`GIT_STRATEGY` override (`regression_detector.yml`, `static_quality_gate.yml`, `files_inventory_check.yml`, the Windows bazel runner) were left untouched. The Windows `GIT_STRATEGY: "clone"` templates in `deploy/conditions.yml` / `agent7.yml` are unrelated to git history (they work around CIEXE-1152 for cancelled jobs) and don't need `GIT_DEPTH: 0`. ### Motivation Shallow clones reduce checkout time/bandwidth across the pipeline, which runs on every commit/PR. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Validated YAML syntax of all changed files. - Manually traced every git operation (`git merge-base`, `git log` ranges, `git describe --tags`) reachable from CI jobs, including through the invoke tasks they call (`tasks/libs/common/git.py`, `tasks/gotest.py`, `tasks/libs/releasing/version.py`, etc.) to confirm which jobs need full history. - Ran the `gitlab-configuration` pre-push linter (`dda inv linter.full-gitlab-ci -t main --pre-push-linters --fail-fast`) locally — passed with pre-existing warnings unrelated to this change. ### Additional Notes **Known risk, intentionally not addressed here:** the Linux/macOS/Windows unit-test jobs use `--only-impacted-packages` on essentially every dev-branch pipeline (via `FAST_TESTS=true`), which calls `git merge-base` through `tasks/gotest.py:get_impacted_packages` with **no error handling**. Under `GIT_DEPTH=1`, if the merge-base predates the 1-commit shallow window, this would hard-fail the test job rather than gracefully falling back to running all tests. This wasn't addressed in this PR to avoid setting `GIT_DEPTH: 0` on the largest and most CI-time-costly category of jobs, which would defeat much of the purpose of this change. Options going forward: harden the fallback in `get_impacted_packages` (deepen fetch or fall back to "run all tests" on merge-base failure), or scope `GIT_DEPTH: 0` to those jobs if the risk materializes.
