signals.title: feat(notableevents): add macOS shutdown-cause notable event
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a macOS notable event that reports **why the previous boot ended**, recovered after the fact from the PMU rather than observed live. On Apple silicon, PMU/PMIC driver services publish an `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` IORegistry property: an array of short ASCII tokens naming the fault conditions that preceded the last power-off. This PR reads that property, classifies the tokens, and emits one notable event per boot when the classification is a fault. Five fault classes are covered, spanning the whole dictionary of 80 known tokens — 59 of which are faults: | Class | Title | Tokens | Example families | | ---------- | ------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------- | | `thermal` | macOS overheated shutdown | 14 | `ot`, `sochot`, `ntc_shdn` | | `power` | macOS power fault shutdown | 29 | `uv`, `ov`, `oc`, `buck`, `pgood` | | `crash` | macOS crash shutdown | 6 | `crash` | | `watchdog` | macOS watchdog timeout shutdown | 5 | `timeout` | | `hardware` | macOS hardware fault shutdown | 5 | `spmi`, `sgpio`, `fault`, `otp_crc` | - **Native reader** (`shutdown_cause_iokit_darwin.{c,h}`) walks the IOService plane, flattens every `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` array into a single `0x1f`-separated token sequence, and dedups as it writes — so no Core Foundation type crosses the cgo boundary. The whole plane is walked rather than matching a class because the publishing class is PMIC-specific and varies by Mac model, and IOKit cannot match on a property key alone (`kIOPropertyMatchKey` matches key *and* value). - **Classifier** (`shutdown_classify_darwin.go`) maps a token to its *family* (prefix before the first comma, a declared underscore family, or the whole token) and the family to one of five classes, resolved by fixed precedence: **thermal → power → crash → watchdog → hardware**. Thermal wins deliberately: a machine collapsing from heat also asserts reset, crash and power lines, and the event that matters most must not be titled as a crash. - **Event shape** (`format_darwin.go`) — `EventType` is the constant `"System shutdown fault"` so consumers can filter shutdown causes on one value; the class varies the title and message only. The payload reports every token observed *plus* the families and the fault subset the classifier acted on, so a reader sees both the raw evidence and what the verdict was based on: ```json "macos_shutdown_cause": { "source": "IOPMUBootFaultInfo", "classification": "thermal", "primary_family": "ot", "families": ["ot", "sochot"], "tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "fault_tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "boot_uuid": "…", "boot_time": "2026-08-11T09:55:21Z" } ``` - **Dedup is boot-scoped.** Identity is `shutdown:<bootUUID>:<sortedFaultTokens>`, hashed under a new `macos-shutdown-v1:` event-ID prefix. Both halves are load-bearing: the boot UUID alone says nothing about *what* was read, and the token set alone is identical across boots — a Mac that overheats every afternoon would emit one ID forever and be deduplicated into silence. Tokens are sorted first because PMU enumeration order is not stable (measured: two triggers with an identical fault set reported the groups in different order). - **Storage.** A new `ShutdownCause` bookmark field records the examined boot *whether or not* an event was emitted, so a cleanly-rebooting Mac does not re-read the property on every Agent restart. It is the primary guard rather than the `Acknowledged` map, which prunes after 30 days or 4096 entries — a Mac up longer than that would otherwise re-emit. The check runs **once per collector lifetime**, before the first directory scan, and is retried from the reconcile tick when it could not commit. It reads the property as an ordinary user (no root needed; system-probe runs as root regardless), and the whole feature is gated behind the existing `notable_events.enabled` setting, which defaults to `false`. **No benchmarks, deliberately.** There is no steady-state cost to measure: the IOService walk happens once per collector lifetime, is bounded at 16 services, and short-circuits as soon as every distinct token is accounted for. It is not on any per-event, per-scan or per-tick path. **Bookmark schema version stays at 1, deliberately.** `Load()` and `validateDarwinBookmarkState()` both require exact equality, so bumping to `2` would fail every existing v1 bookmark as corrupt — which resets state and re-baselines, discarding pending undelivered crash events on every upgraded host. `ShutdownCause` is `omitempty` with a nil zero value, so v1 bookmarks deserialize with no migration. Relatedly, `types.IsEventID()` had to learn the new prefix in the same change: a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID written under the old single-prefix check would fail validation on the next `Load()` and wipe the bookmark, silently losing every pending crash event. ### Motivation [https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040) **A hard shutdown kills the Agent before it can report why.** Whether the machine overheated, lost a power rail, asserted its CRASH line, tripped a watchdog or hit a hardware fault, the Agent is gone before it can say so — the cause has to be recovered from the PMU on the next boot, or it is never recovered at all. All five fault classes are in scope here; thermal is one of them, not the point of the feature. **Predecessor: macOS app crash notable events (#54084).** This builds directly on it, reusing its bookmark, its `Pending`/`Ack` delivery contract and its at-least-once semantics unchanged — a second event *source* on that pipeline, not a second pipeline. It complements rather than replaces it: #54084 reports `.ips` files, which are written by a *running* OS about a *running* process, so a PMU-forced power cut leaves no `.ips` at all. The one adjacent artifact that does exist, `.shutdownStall` spindumps, records a *stalled* shutdown, not its cause. Everything else was surveyed and rejected: `pmset -g log` carries no cause data (25,117 lines grepped, nothing), `nvram -p` has no shutdown-cause variable, `ioreg -rc IOPMrootDomain` has no such property, `last -x reboot` is empty, and the `AppleSMC: Previous shutdown cause: <N>` unified-log line that Intel Macs emit **does not exist on Apple silicon**. Without this, a machine that overheated or lost a power rail badly enough to be cut off is a silent gap in the fleet record. `kern.shutdownreason` is **deliberately not read** — not as a source, not as a fallback, not as payload. It is the same PMU data flattened into an 80-byte-capped string, and it was already destroying data on an ordinary clean shutdown of the test machine: the cap was hit in 4 of 6 measured boots, always cutting *mid-token* and synthesising fault names that do not exist (`crash,crash`, `btn_rst,btn`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_d`). Absence of a token from that sysctl carries no information at all. The tradeoff is accepted and known: the sysctl also carries application-processor tokens (`ap_restart`, `ap_panic`) that `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not, and this PR gives those up rather than add a second parsing path and a second failure mode. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests — 240 tests pass in `pkg/notableevents`** (verified locally on the branch head with `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/notableevents/...`). Classifier tests deliberately use **payloads measured from real hardware** as fixtures rather than invented ones: | Pattern | Tokens (distinct union) | Emits | | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | A — clean shutdown | `target_off_restart`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | B — `sudo reboot` | `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | C — button/force restart | + `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `crash,crash0_in` | `crash`, `fault_tokens = ["crash,crash0_in"]` | Also covered: the full 80-token dictionary maps to exactly one family each with the asserted **59 fault / 21 benign** split (14 thermal, 29 power, 6 crash, 5 watchdog, 5 hardware) — this pins a typo in the family map that would otherwise silently misclassify; class precedence in every pairing; unknown *suffix* within a known family (`ot,some_future_sensor`) still classifies thermal, which is the prefix contract; permuted group order yields an identical event ID; benign-token exclusions are dead-weight-free (each is in the measured dictionary *and* would otherwise be a fault); every classification fits the wire limit; malformed and oversized payloads are rejected. Collector tests cover the delivery contract end to end: one event per boot; `Start()` → `Close()` → `Start()` yields one event, not two; same boot UUID after Ack yields nothing; a *different* boot UUID with the same tokens yields a new event; a saturated pending queue **defers** rather than records, because recording the boot would be final and the fault cannot be reproduced by a later boot; a `Save` failure leaves nothing pending and is retried; a check blocked by an in-flight bookmark commit is retried from the reconcile tick rather than stranded for the process lifetime; reader failure, absent property and untrusted payload all leave crash-report collection unaffected; a v1 bookmark with no `shutdown_cause` key loads without being treated as corrupt. **Manual QA on real hardware.** `Mac17,9` / M5 Pro / macOS 26.5.2 (`25F84`), SIP enabled, no `boot-args`. **Six real boot sessions** executed one trigger at a time — the property is destroyed by the next reboot, so the runs could not be batched — with an immediate capture script per boot: `sudo reboot`, Control-Command-Power force restart, power button held ~10s, a deliberately stalled shutdown ended by the power button, the same stall resolved via Try Again → Force Quit, and a battery run-down. Three distinct payloads were observed across six distinct boot UUIDs, verified byte-identical by MD5, reverting to pattern A after a clean shutdown. That establishes the load-bearing premise: **the property is a live, event-driven, self-clearing signal, not a constant** — which is what validates both the read path and the boot-UUID dedup key. **How to reproduce a fault event yourself — the `crash` class, on demand.** One fault class is reproducible at will on Apple silicon, so a reviewer can exercise the whole path end to end without waiting for real hardware trouble. A force restart asserts the AP's CRASH line, which emits `crash,crash0_in`: 1. Enable the feature — it is off by default: ```bash # datadog.yaml notable_events: enabled: true ``` 2. Clear any prior bookmark so the check is not skipped as already-examined, and note that the file is root-owned: ```bash sudo rm -f /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json ``` 3. Record the current boot identity and the pre-restart payload, for comparison: ```bash sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo ``` 4. Force restart: hold **Control-Command-Power** until the screen blanks. (Holding the power button ~10s, or ending a stalled shutdown with the power button, both produce the same payload — see the resolution caveat in Additional Notes.) 5. After the machine boots, confirm the PMU now reports the crash token. Expect pattern C — `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `target_off_restart`, `crash,crash0_in`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert`: ```bash ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid # must differ from step 3 ``` 6. Start the Agent and system-probe, and confirm the event: ```bash sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.agent sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.sysprobe sudo cat /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json | jq . ``` Expect a `shutdown_cause` object whose `boot_uuid` matches step 5, and a `pending` entry with a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID, `"event_type": "System shutdown fault"`, title `macOS crash shutdown`, `"classification": "crash"`, and `fault_tokens` of exactly `["crash,crash0_in"]` — all six tokens appear in `tokens`, but only the crash one elected the class. 7. Confirm the dedup guard: restart the Agent without rebooting. No second event should be emitted, and `shutdown_cause.boot_uuid` should be unchanged. To verify the **negative** case, `sudo reboot` instead of step 4 (pattern B) or shut down cleanly from the Apple menu (pattern A). Both must produce a `shutdown_cause` record with **no** event — a clean shutdown emitting an event is the failure mode most worth catching, since `wdog,reset_in_1` is present on every ordinary shutdown. **`qa/rc-required` — why this needs RC validation.** The classes that matter most in the field cannot be triggered on any machine we control, and cannot be simulated at all: the property is written by the PMU at power-off and is read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store. Reproducing a genuine thermal, power-rail or hardware fault means real failing hardware. Virtualized macOS runners expose no PMU, so the property is simply absent there and CI can only assert graceful degradation. What RC deployment adds is a full end-to-end test on real hardware: that the notable event is actually emitted and delivered, and that its tags and payload arrive intact. The predecessor, #54084, carried the same label for the same reason. **What was NOT validated, and cannot be:** - **No thermal token has ever been observed on this machine** — not `ot,*`, not `sochot,*`, not `ntc_shdn`. The thermal classification is inferred from token names in the PMU's own declared dictionary (published as `info-fault_name-<N>` properties on the `pmu,spmi` device-tree nodes). This is a hard limit, not a gap in the testing: there is **no native way to fake a thermal shutdown cause**. The value is produced by the PMU at power-off and exposed read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store — `sysctl -w` refuses (read-only OID), there is no user-settable IORegistry path, no `nvram` variable, and a userspace `os_log` line would not carry the right sender image. Generating real heat was out of scope. **The thermal path should not be described as verified in any customer-facing text or release note.** - **The real IOKit read on CI.** macOS VMs expose no PMU, so the property is absent and the reader returns empty. No E2E test is added; on a virtualized runner one could only assert graceful degradation, which is worth having but would not be thermal coverage. ### Additional Notes **Known tradeoff — `crash` fires on user force-restarts.** Measured, not hypothetical: `crash,crash0_in` appeared in pattern C with no panic induced. The token means the AP's CRASH line was asserted, which a hard reset satisfies, so **every user-initiated force restart on this hardware emits a `crash`-classified event.** Accepted because a force restart is itself a signal that something went wrong badly enough that the user gave up on the machine, and the alternative — treating the family as benign — silently dropped genuine AP and hypervisor crashes. Two commitments follow: the message says "followed a CRASH signal from the processor" and never claims a kernel panic; and if force restarts dominate emitted volume, the fix is to split `crash,hyp_*` from `crash,crash*_in`, not to revert the family to benign. **Fault allowlist, not benign denylist.** Under a denylist, any Mac whose clean shutdown emits an uncatalogued token would raise a shutdown-fault event on *every boot*. A permanent false positive is noticed and distrusted; a missed rare fault is not. The cost is that a genuinely new fault token on unfamiliar hardware is dropped silently — mitigated by matching on the family *prefix*, so `ot,anything_new` still classifies thermal. **Two benign per-token exceptions** (`shutdownBenignTokens`), for tokens whose family is a fault but whose meaning is not: `buck_boot_charge` (booting after the battery charged from depleted, not a regulator failure) and `timeout,dblclick_timeout` (the power-button double-click window). Both produced a user-visible fault event on a machine that had not faulted. Scoped to these two deliberately — the other `buck_*` tokens name real regulator failures. Excluding one only changes the outcome when it is the sole evidence for its class. **Graceful degradation is strictly additive** — nothing here can block `Start()` or interfere with crash-report collection. Property absent → no event, debug log. IOKit failure → no event. `kern.bootsessionuuid` unreadable → skip the whole check, since without a dedup key an event could repeat on every Agent restart. `kern.boottime` unreadable → fall back to the current time and omit `boot_time`. Event over the wire limit → drop and warn, **never truncate a fault payload**, because a truncated one would be misleading. Save-failure and saturation warnings latch so a persistent condition warns once rather than on every reconcile tick, and are kept separate so neither can silence the other. **Bounds are derived from real hardware, and shared between C and Go so they cannot drift.** `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKENS_PER_SERVICE 88` and `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKEN_CHARS 53` come from the largest known real payload (80-token dictionary, longest token 35 bytes) plus margin — 10% on count, 50% on length — and the Go-side `maxShutdownTokens` / `maxShutdownTokenBytes` are derived from those same macros. `DD_PMU_MAX_SERVICES` is 16, matching how few PMU-publishing services exist in practice. A service exceeding its bounds is dropped and logged rather than failing the read; an oversized token is truncated rather than dropping its whole service; the walk stops early once every distinct token is accounted for, since no remaining service can contribute one that has not been seen. **Intel Macs silently emit nothing.** `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not exist there; `readPMUBootFaultInfo` returns `errShutdownCauseUnsupported` when `runtime.GOARCH != "arm64"`. The Intel path (SMC shutdown-cause code `-81` via `log show`, which needs root) is unimplemented and unvalidated — no Intel Mac available. Apple documents none of this property: `org:apple-oss-distributions` returns zero hits for both `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` and `info-fault_name`. Provenance is the device's own ADT table, community string dumps of the `AppleD2255PMU` kext, and independent confirmation of the prefix decodings in `hack-different/apple-knowledge`. The *read mechanism*, by contrast, is entirely public API: `IOServiceMatching`, `IOServiceGetMatchingServices`, `IOIteratorNext`, `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty`.

signals.title: Add a lightweight gate for prepared Agent rollouts
signals.text: ### Why A DaemonSet update can delete a working Agent before Kubernetes pulls and starts its replacement. A slow or failed pull can therefore leave the node without an Agent. ### What does this PR do? This PR adds an experimental Linux `agent-rollout-gate` binary to the node Agent images. The Operator can start this binary before each Agent component. The gate waits for a component-specific host lock before it starts the real process. This lets Kubernetes pull and create a replacement Pod while the old Agent still serves. Each component changes ownership independently. A slow `system-probe` shutdown does not block the core Agent or trace Agent. The gate keeps the startup probe unsuccessful while it sleeps. Kubernetes does not run readiness or liveness probes until startup succeeds. After the gate gets the lock, it starts the Agent and uses the original probe and termination behavior. This mechanism does not claim zero-gap telemetry. Agent caches, Cluster Agent assignments, metadata, and process state still start cold after handoff. ### Validation - `dda inv test --targets=./cmd/agent-rollout-gate`: 9 tests passed on macOS. - `dda inv agent-rollout-gate.build`: passed for Linux arm64. - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./cmd/agent-rollout-gate`: 0 issues. - Formatting and Python task compilation: passed. The Linux lock, signal, and probe tests must pass in CI. Experimental-cluster validation starts after the three PoC PRs are reviewed. ### Related PRs - Operator: https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-operator/pull/3355 - Experimental deployment: https://github.com/DataDog/k8s-datadog-agent-ops/pull/9477 The gate-capable Agent image must be deployed with the ordinary rollout before prepared mode is enabled.

signals.title: [NTWK-812] Filter dynamic tests across all reverse-DNS names
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes Network Path dynamic tests incorrectly scheduling traceroutes to Datadog intake endpoints when a destination IP is associated with multiple DNS names. Previously, Network Path filtered only the first DNS name associated with an IP. Because DNS cache ordering is not deterministic, the default `*.datadoghq.com` exclusion could be missed when another name appeared first. This PR: - Passes every existing DNS name associated with a destination IP to Network Path. - Evaluates the ordered connection-filter chain against the connection as a whole. A rule matches when its domain pattern matches any associated name, or its IP condition matches; the last matching rule wins. - Uses the domain matched by the winning include rule as the path-test hostname. - Preserves Remote Config ID, name, and tags from the winning rule. - Keeps customer include rules able to override the built-in Datadog exclusions. This does not modify the shared reverse-DNS parser or cache, change CNM payload behavior, or add an AWS ELB-specific exclusion. ### Motivation [NTWK-812 / ZD 2972181](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/NTWK-812) A destination IP for a Datadog intake endpoint can be associated with both its `*.datadoghq.com` name and a CNAME target. Network Path previously collapsed that list to its first entry before filtering, making the result dependent on cache ordering. For the reporting organization, this represented approximately 37% of dynamic test runs—more than 3,000 unnecessary runs per day. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added unit coverage for: - Datadog and ELB names in either order. - An ELB name by itself receiving no special treatment. - Unrelated domains and customer-owned ELBs. - Customer include rules overriding built-in exclusions across aliases. - Last-match-wins behavior across different aliases. - Empty and partially empty DNS-name lists. - Hostname selection for local and Remote Config include rules. - Preservation of Remote Config ID, name, and tags. `gofmt` and diff whitespace validation pass. The focused local test command was blocked before compilation because Bazel could not download `gotestsum` from `proxy.golang.org`. CI validation is in progress following the merge from `main`. ### Additional Notes The filtering behavior remains ordered and last-match-wins, but each rule now evaluates all names associated with the connection instead of only one arbitrarily selected name.

signals.title: feat(otel-metrics): share SDK trace stats mapping
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a shared `tracestats` mapping to `opentelemetry-mapping-go`. It converts `traces.span.sdk.metrics.duration` delta histograms into transport-neutral APM trace stats for the Agent and public OTLP intake. ### Why? Using one mapping keeps tags, status handling, operation names, time windows, validation, and serialization consistent across both ingestion paths. ### Differences from the current dd-source implementation Compared with the current local mapper in dd-source, this implementation: - Uses a data point's `service.name` when present and applies Agent service-name normalization. - Emits lowercase span kinds and maps `datadog.is_trace_root`. - Accepts OTel error status code `2` and case-insensitive `ERROR` / `STATUS_CODE_ERROR` forms. - Converts named gRPC status values to their canonical numeric codes. - Maps `telemetry.sdk.language` to payload languages and structured `datadog.peer_tags` arrays to grouped stats peer tags. - Normalizes and sorts additional metric tags while excluding fields already mapped into grouped stats. - Skips only invalid data points and reports conversion errors instead of emitting buckets with missing sketches. - Keeps the existing `otlp-intake-metrics` source attribution instead of adding `otlp-intake-metrics-sdk` / `span_source:ddsdk_otlp`. - Owns the payload protobuf and serialization so the Agent and dd-source share the same wire contract. These behavioral fixes can be split into their own dd-source fix PR if reviewers prefer. Keeping them here makes it easier to test the complete, up-to-date mapping contract end to end across Agent and agentless intake without an intermediate mismatched state. ### Testing - Focused `tracestats` package passed with the race detector. - Focused lint passed with 0 issues. - [Staging collector test](https://dd.datad0g.com/apm/entity/service%3Ajava-sdkstats-collector-updated-20260821t1428z?dependencyMap.showNetworkMetrics=false&env=sdkstats-e2e&fromUser=true&groupMapByOperation=null&historicalData=true&operationName=internal&panels=qson%3A%28data%3A%28%29%2Cversion%3A%210%29&spanKind=internal&start=1787314370460&end=1787327226848&paused=true#resources): 120 requests produced 120 trace hits; the raw SDK histogram was absent. - [Staging agentless test](https://dd.datad0g.com/apm/entity/service%3Ajava-sdkstats-agentless-evp-20260821t1416z?dependencyMap.showNetworkMetrics=false&env=%2A&fromUser=false&operationName=internal&panels=qson%3A%28data%3A%28%29%2Cversion%3A%210%29&refresh_mode=sliding&spanKind=internal&start=1787244191834&end=1787330591834&paused=false#traces): 120 requests produced 120 trace hits.

signals.title: Publish datadog-fips-proxy to the pipeline testing repositories
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Publishes the released `datadog-fips-proxy` package into the testing repositories of the pipelines whose install-script tests need it, so the install script resolves it from the same repository as the Agent packages built by that pipeline. ### Motivation `test_install_script` triggers the `agent-linux-install-script` pipeline with `TESTING_APT_URL` and `TESTING_YUM_URL` so the install script installs the Agent built by the pipeline. Those variables land in the apt and yum configuration, so every Datadog package the script installs is resolved against the pipeline repository — including `datadog-fips-proxy`, which is released from another repository and is not published there. Nightly and RC pipelines failed with `Error: Unable to find a match: datadog-fips-proxy`. The mitigation was to stop forwarding those variables for the FIPS test, which leaves it installing the latest stable Agent instead of the pipeline's packages. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv linter.full-gitlab-ci` passes locally, including the configuration check across all nine pipeline contexts, which confirms the optional need resolves where the new job is absent. `shellcheck` with the repository's exclude list is clean on the job's expanded script. The `.pre` stage runs the same linter on this PR. The publish targets match what the child pipeline computes: `testing/pipeline-<id>-a7/7/x86_64/` for yum, and prefix `datadog-agent/pipeline-<id>-a7` with codename `stable-x86_64`, component `7` and architecture `amd64` for apt. Both pinned artifact URLs resolve, and the deb declares only `Recommends: datadog-signing-keys`, which `deploy_deb_testing-a7_x64` already uploads to the same repository. This PR changes the file the job's change rule watches, so the job runs on its own pipeline. From that run, with `<ID>` the pipeline id: ``` curl -fsI https://yumtesting.datad0g.com/testing/pipeline-<ID>-a7/7/x86_64/datadog-fips-proxy-1.1.29-1.x86_64.rpm curl -fsS https://apttesting.datad0g.com/datadog-agent/pipeline-<ID>-a7/dists/stable-x86_64/7/binary-amd64/Packages | grep -A4 'Package: datadog-fips-proxy' ``` Both indexes still list the Agent packages afterwards, and the RPM carries the testing signature rather than the production one. ### Additional Notes Publishing before the Agent uploads instead of after them fails safe. The arrangement assumes `rpm-s3` merges into existing metadata rather than replacing it, which is what it is built to do but is not verifiable outside CI. In this order, if that assumption is wrong the Agent job's pass drops `datadog-fips-proxy` from the index and the FIPS test behaves as it does today; in the reverse order it would drop the Agent packages and break every e2e test that consumes them. The ordering costs one thing: a failed download now blocks the two Agent testing uploads rather than only the install-script test. Making the job `allow_failure: true` would trade that for a silent index race.
signals.author: ofek

signals.title: fix(network/tracer): fix data race on conntrackerTelemetry.lastRegisters
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on `conntrackerTelemetry.lastRegisters`: `Collect()` did a non-atomic read-modify-write on the package-level field, racing when two Prometheus Gather ticks overlapped. Switched `lastRegisters` to `atomic.Uint64` and use `Load`/`Store` in `Collect`. No behavior change — same subtraction, same package-level scope. ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes The race is eliminated by construction — `Load`/`Store` are atomic, so concurrent `Collect` calls can't race on `lastRegisters`.

signals.title: [SVLS-9526] Prototype: serverless-init inventory payload + 9-platform POC deploy scripts
signals.text: ## What this is A **prototype branch** containing the full stack of changes for SVLS-9526 in a single PR. Intended for review and discussion — these changes will be broken into the stacked PRs below before merge. ## Stacked PRs (final form) | PR | Branch | Contents | |---|---|---| | #54537 | `svls-9526/force-collect` | `ForceCollect()` — send inventory payload on every cold start | | #54538 | `svls-9526/diagnostic-v2` | `inventories_first_run_delay` config key + diagnostic enhancements | | #54543 | `svls-9526/serverless-agent-table` | `cmd/serverless-init/inventory`: `serverless_*` fields in inventoryagent payload | ## What's in this PR **Agent changes (will land via the stacked PRs above):** - `ForceCollect()` added to `inventoryagent.Component` — fires before `modeConf.Runner()` so the inventory payload is sent before the container can scale to zero - `inventories_first_run_delay` config key to control startup delay - New `cmd/serverless-init/inventory` package: populates `serverless_*` fields (cloud provider, workload type, origin, resource name, deployment model, runtime, agent commit, DD config) into the inventoryagent payload - Enhanced startup diagnostics (`DD_SERVERLESS_DIAGNOSTIC_INFO=true`) including UUID, CCRID, and inventory pipeline config **POC deploy scripts (`scripts/serverless-deploy/`, not intended to merge to main):** - Deploys 9 test services across GCP (Cloud Run Service/Job/Function) and Azure (Container App, Web App Containers, Web App SITECONTAINERS, Web App Linux Code) - `demo.sh` — one-command end-to-end runner: build → deploy all 9 → trigger cold starts → collect logs → print REDAPL SQL query ## How to run the POC ```bash export GCP_PROJECT=datadog-serverless-gcp-demo export AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<sub-id> export DD_API_KEY=$(vault kv get -field=api_key kv/dd/api_keys/dddev) export IMAGE_TAG=1.10.2-poc-$(date +%Y%m%d) cd scripts/serverless-deploy ./demo.sh ``` ###dd-auth command equivalent: `export DD_API_KEY=$(dd-auth vault kv get -field=api_key kv/dd/api_keys/dddev)` Or if it's wrapping the whole script: `dd-auth ./demo.sh ` Then paste the generated SQL into **go/redapl → Queries → SQL** to see the agents in `datadog_agent`. ## Key findings from 9-platform testing | Platform | UUID behaviour | `datadog_agent` rows | |---|---|---| | GCP Cloud Run | New UUID per cold start | `ForceCollect()` required — container scales to zero before 60s delay | | Azure Container App | Stable UUID per replica | Upserts same row reliably | | Azure Web App | DMI UUID from underlying VM | Apps on same App Service Plan share UUID → need CCRID-based PK | This motivates `serverless_init_agent` (SVLS-9604): a separate REDAPL table keyed by `resource_id` (CCRID) instead of Agent UUID. ## Not in scope for merge - `scripts/serverless-deploy/` — test infrastructure only, not shipped in the agent - `scripts/serverless-deploy/diagnostic-results-*.txt` — personal test output

signals.title: fix(ebpf): synchronize perfUsageCollector.Collect with Manager.Start
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race between `perfUsageCollector.Collect` (reads PerfMap/RingBuffer telemetry fields during a Prometheus Gather tick) and `Manager.Start` (writes those fields during eBPF manager startup). Adds a shared `sync.Mutex` (`TelemetryMu`) in `pkg/ebpf` that both `Start` and `Collect` hold. It lives in `pkg/ebpf` to avoid a circular import (`pkg/ebpf/telemetry` already imports `pkg/ebpf`). ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes No unit test added — the race requires eBPF support to trigger (`Manager.Start` writes to PerfMap/RingBuffer internal fields that can't be constructed in a unit test). The race is eliminated by construction: `Collect` and `Start` now share the same mutex, so they can never access the telemetry fields concurrently.

signals.title: test: fix double-stop penalty and grace period in logs agent tests
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Removes a redundant `agent.stop()` call from the test cleanup that caused a double-stop penalty, reducing `TestAgentTestSuite` from 41s to 5s and `TestRestartTestSuite` from 70s to 63s. ### Motivation The cleanup registered by `createAgent` and the explicit `agent.stop()` calls in test methods both invoked `stopComponents`, which blocked for 5s each on non-idempotent component `Stop()` methods (e.g. `fileLauncher.Stop()` blocks on an unbuffered channel when `Start()` was never called). Removing the redundant cleanup eliminates the double-stop. ### Describe how you validated your changes Both test suites were run in full (no cache) before and after the change to confirm all tests still pass and measure the speedup. ### Additional Notes All changes are test-only; no non-test code was modified.

signals.title: feat(dogstatsd): detect client payload drops
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Detects sustained DogStatsD client-reported payload-byte drops for UDS and UDS-stream clients using telemetry from the normal final aggregation path. When the drop rate exceeds 1%, the Agent reports a per-Agent Agent Health issue containing queue, writer, and unclassified drop totals. The issue resolves after sustained healthy telemetry. This adds two confirmation-period settings: - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.unhealthy_confirmation_window` defaults to `1m` and prevents transient drops from opening an issue. - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.recovery_confirmation_window` defaults to `30m` and prevents intermittent drops from repeatedly resolving and reopening the issue. ### Motivation This builds on #54381, which exposes DogStatsD client byte telemetry through Agent Telemetry/COAT. Detecting sustained drops in the Agent provides consistent behavior across supported clients and surfaces an actionable Agent Health issue without requiring new client payloads or library changes. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Unit tests covering detection, confirmation, recovery, missing telemetry, restart reconciliation, and multi-worker flush ordering - Fakeintake integration test covering ACTIVE and RESOLVED Agent Health reports - Updated the benchmarks ### Additional Notes

signals.title: Enables the v3 metrics intake for series in DDOT
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Enables the **v3 metrics intake for series** in DDOT (the `otel-agent` binary). By default is ON with extra requirements: - no proxy - only recognized Datadog sites ### Motivation OTAGENT-1130, under epic OTAGENT-1133 ("Reduce customer metrics egress bandwidth 30–50% with v3 payload"). DDOT was the last OTel surface still on the v2 series intake. This PR moves DDOT onto the v3 series path, aligning it with the core Agent (series v3 default since 7.81). ### Describe how you validated your changes - **Unit:** `cmd/otel-agent/config` tests pass; the guard tests now assert the resolved value is `datadog_only`. - **Static:** `dda inv linter.go` — 0 issues; `dda inv otel-agent.build` — OK. - **Manual (local, standalone otel-agent → fakeintake, `DD_USE_V3_API_SERIES_ENABLED=true`, zstd):** series routed to `/api/intake/metrics/v3/series` and **0** on `/api/v2/series`; all payloads zstd (wire magic `28b52ffd`); v3 payloads decode correctly; a cumulative Sum arrived as a delta `COUNT` (c2d); sketches stayed on `/api/beta/sketches` (v2). - **Manual + telemetrygen + delta** - metrics are posted to https://api.datadoghq.com/api/intake/metrics/v3/series" (202 Accepted) - **Manual + telemetrygen + cumulative** - metrics are converted to delta & posted to https://api.datadoghq.com/api/intake/metrics/v3/series" (202 Accepted) - **E2E:** new `TestOTelAgentV3Series` (KinD DDOT with v3 enabled) asserts OTLP metrics reach the intake, series land on the v3 endpoint (`RouteStats`), and v3 payloads are zstd. Auto-wired into the `new-e2e-otel` job — no CI changes. (Runs in CI on this PR.) - Telemetry gen + UI: sums & gauge ### Additional Notes - **Kill-switch / rollout:** enablement follows `use_v3_api.series.enabled` (default `datadog_only`). v2 remains the compat/fallback path (non-Datadog destinations, non-zstd builds, non-migrated regions). Opt out with `use_v3_api.series.enabled=false` (or `DD_USE_V3_API_SERIES_ENABLED=false`). - **Scope:** series only. Sketches (distributions) stay on v2 (v3 for sketches is a separate opt-in). - **Known follow-up (this PR):** the auto-injected `datadog/dd-autoconfigured` flare extension keeps its own zlib serializer and now logs a benign but misleading "disabling v3 metrics intake" warning — the same warning #52301 suppressed on the OSS path, surfaced because v3 is now enabled in-process. Egress is unaffected (verified v3 + zstd); the warning does not reflect the actual series path. To be addressed. - this deliberately does **not** revert #52301 (`serializerexporter/serializer.go`). That line only runs for the OSS Datadog exporter in opentelemetry-collector-contrib - for case "datadog_only" - the PR updates "use_v3_api.series.endpoints" by "https://api.xxxx" https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1130

signals.title: [AAD-6] Unify detector point windows
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? > [!NOTE] > 1. This is mostly for metrics that arrive every 15s, I'm thinking about how to properly manage logs that are every 1s in a future PR (instead of a 30m retention they have 2m retention this way) -> [comment](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55024#discussion_r3802840340). > 2. The end goal is to unify storage when we do the warmup, some values are duplicated (future PR). This unifies all detectors (except RRCF) with an interface to get the min / max number of points per series. This way there is no discrepancy with the storage max retention (now deduced by default [1]). Warmup lazy behavior: Max retention behavior [2]: Detectors follow these conditions: 1. A new series has < min points -> no detector state created (discarded) 2. A new series has min points -> create initial state 3. The series has > min and < max points -> process + can trigger anomalies 4. The series has < min points now but had before > min points -> process (update state only if needed) but don't trigger anomalies 5. Internal detector states have max MaxPoints state points (we don't have a state for a point not present in the storage) 6. A new series can't have > max points nor > max state points (eviction) It improves memory / CPU since series that have few points don't have state, it's lazy computation. It's a tradeoff but it makes more sense to not save the states of points that are stale. Extra changes: - Bocpd has less points: (120, 200) -> (60, 120) - Added all the min / max points to the config Benchmark (all detectors enabled): Overall metric | Baseline | Changed | Delta -- | -- | -- | -- In-use heap, average | 261.02 MB | 135.29 MB | **-48.16%** Detector-phase time, average | 10.751 s | 9.835 s | **-8.52%** Macro F1 | 0.265206 | 0.267651 | +0.92% Macro precision | 0.332990 | 0.491846 | +47.70% Macro recall | 0.578832 | 0.511810 | -11.58% Predictions | 682 | 420 | -38.42% ### Motivation Memory / cpu optimization + unify detectors ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes [1] The max retention time is based on 15s / point -> `15 * max(detectors.MaxPoints) + 16` seconds [2] This is enforced by the retention time deduced by the max points for each detector so storage is always big enough We need to fine tune again to improve the scores (all detectors enabled): Scenario | F1 baseline → changed | Detector phase | Heap -- | -- | -- | -- block-building-outage | 0.285714 → 0.000000 | 22.3 → 9.7 ms | 194.7 → 39.2 MB byzantine-fault-cascade | 0 → 0 | 128.815 → 117.926 s | 1216.5 → 1219.1 MB cascading-regional-outage | 0.063224 → 0.000000 | 9.2 → 5.4 ms | 165.7 → 29.3 MB cassandra-repair-degradation | 0.318046 → 0.641981 | 48.2 → 19.5 ms | 294.8 → 62.6 MB dns-upstream-outage | 0.052606 → 0.025667 | 14.0 → 6.5 ms | 182.9 → 46.3 MB kafka-partition-saturation | 0.117641 → 0.108369 | 32.8 → 20.4 ms | 248.4 → 55.1 MB lock-contention-cascade | 0.971969 → 0.365964 | 8.9 → 3.6 ms | 141.5 → 45.4 MB memcached-eviction-storm | 0.057796 → 0.115670 | 13.5 → 4.2 ms | 129.6 → 26.8 MB pool-exhaustion | 0.093612 → 0.097034 | 9.2 → 5.5 ms | 119.1 → 15.9 MB redis-billing-latency | 0.604642 → 0.928561 | 17.6 → 9.4 ms | 185.9 → 32.6 MB redis-cpu-saturation | 0.615742 → 0.928561 | 13.7 → 5.6 ms | 147.2 → 32.6 MB tiered-cascading-outage | 0.001476 → 0.000000 | 10.1 → 3.7 ms | 106.0 → 18.6 MB

signals.title: [AAD-6] Rely on storage for detectors
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? > [!NOTE] > [Context](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55024): states / points are aligned. Some detectors were using duplicated data that could be found from the storage, now they rely only on the storage. It's especially true for warmups, now everything is initialized once (per series) relying only on the storage points so extra warmup memory is short term now. Benchmark (https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55024 vs this PR, F1 are the same): Scenario | Detector phase baseline → candidate | Phase Δ | Heap baseline → candidate | Heap Δ -- | -- | -- | -- | -- block-building-outage | 8.327 → 6.919 ms | -16.9% | 39.93 → 33.25 MB | -16.7% byzantine-fault-cascade | 29.884 → 27.714 s | -7.3% | 1195.64 → 1108.92 MB | -7.3% cascading-regional-outage | 4.431 → 4.352 ms | -1.8% | 29.88 → 27.98 MB | -6.4% cassandra-repair-degradation | 18.982 → 18.504 ms | -2.5% | 63.23 → 63.66 MB | +0.7% dns-upstream-outage | 6.447 → 6.262 ms | -2.9% | 37.92 → 35.40 MB | -6.6% kafka-partition-saturation | 16.429 → 16.461 ms | +0.2% | 54.85 → 52.65 MB | -4.0% lock-contention-cascade | 3.980 → 4.048 ms | +1.7% | 45.09 → 37.54 MB | -16.7% memcached-eviction-storm | 2.760 → 3.198 ms | +15.9% | 26.29 → 24.45 MB | -7.0% pool-exhaustion | 5.220 → 5.621 ms | +7.7% | 18.01 → 14.83 MB | -17.7% redis-billing-latency | 7.932 → 9.415 ms | +18.7% | 40.72 → 36.58 MB | -10.2% redis-cpu-saturation | 4.476 → 4.213 ms | -5.9% | 32.29 → 28.39 MB | -12.1% tiered-cascading-outage | 2.511 → 2.228 ms | -11.3% | 20.47 → 19.29 MB | -5.8% **Aggregate** | 81.496 → 81.221 ms | **-0.3%** | 1604.32 → 1482.94 MB | **-7.6%** ### Motivation Memory optimizations. ### Describe how you validated your changes Generated test data (22 cases) and verified that the internal detector states were exactly the same before / after the change. ### Additional Notes

signals.title: Also stop the coverage job from thrashing Bazel analysis cache
signals.text: ### Motivation "Bazel analysis cache thrashing on `main` (containerized job)" keeps alerting after #54963 ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1963914110)): all 49 occurrences of the last 24 hours come from `bazel:coverage:linux-amd64`, which now flips `cover_format`, `--collect_code_coverage` and `--instrumentation_filter`. The last one `bazel coverage` derives from the target patterns, some 400 package regexes that a post-test command cannot replay. ### What does this PR do? Skip `test2json` and UTOF where their `bazel run` cannot match the test invocation, which is only the coverage job: its tests are a **subset** of `bazel:test:linux-amd64`, still reporting them, while its JUnit tar needs no Bazel and its coverage profile only `bazel info`, which analyzes nothing. Guard the remaining `bazel run` with `--noallow_analysis_cache_discard`, turning a future divergence into a failure of the job that introduces it, rather than a warning nobody reads until a monitor fires hours later on `main` pipelines. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv bazel.process-test-results --result-json=` runs no Bazel and still packages JUnit, while a non-empty one keeps converting logs. With the server left in the coverage configuration, the guarded command exits 2 on "analysis cache would have been discarded", and stays silent after `bazel test --config=gorace`. ### Additional Notes The guard is safe for the four `bazel:test:*` jobs: `INSTALL_DIR` and `AGENT_FLAVOR` are set by packaging jobs only, so `omnibazel_flags` injects nothing there, and neither monitor has reported a flip in those jobs since #54963.

signals.title: sbom: default runtime usage properties only on OS packages
signals.text: The enrichment merge copies the runtime usage properties onto the components the system-probe report covers, then defaults LastSeenRunning to "0" and HasSetSuidBit and RunningAsRoot to "false" on every other component of the image SBOM. The runtime scanner reads the dpkg, rpm and apk databases, so a "0" on a language package, on the image's operating-system component or on one of Trivy's per-lockfile application components claims the Agent watched a package outside its scope. Default the three properties on the components the report carried and on those whose purl marks them an OS package. The rest keep them absent, which a consumer reads as out of scope. Trivy maps every OS family onto the deb, rpm and apk purl types, so the prefix decides, and the SBOM e2e tests already use the same three.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: sbom: key the runtime enrichment dedup on bom-ref
signals.text: The enrichment merge rebuilds the component list of the image SBOM it annotates, emitting the first component of each name and normalised version and dropping the rest. Trivy reports one component per install location, so a library version pinned by two lockfiles arrives once per lockfile, each entry with its own bom-ref, and the merge kept one of them. The dependency graph, which the merge carries over as it stands, went on referencing the components that went missing. On the Agent image in the e2e fleet, 362 of its 2673 components share a name and version with another. Deduplicate the components that carry a bom-ref, which is what identifies a component in CycloneDX, and emit the others in turn. A byte-for-byte duplicate shares its bom-ref, so the stored SBOM the guard was added for still collapses.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: sbom: run the SBOM e2e job on core-agent collector changes
signals.text: The runtime usage properties an SBOM payload carries come from the merge in comp/core/workloadmeta/collectors/internal/remote/sbomcollector, and TestSBOMPackageInUseKubeadmSuite exercises that merge end to end. The rule that triggers new-e2e-sbom lists the system-probe resolver and the test tree, so a change confined to the collector reaches the suite only when someone starts the job by hand. Add the collector to the rule.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: env: warn when a container socket exists but is not reachable
signals.text: Feature detection reports this with log.Infof, but it runs while the configuration is still loading, so the message is buffered and only filtered against the final log level once the logger is installed. On an Agent running at log_level warn it is discarded and never written anywhere. The condition deserves a warning. On Unix socket.IsAvailable calls a socket unreachable only when the dial fails with a permission error, so the Agent user cannot open it and container metrics, container image collection and container image vulnerability scanning are all silently disabled. Windows also counts a pipe that is merely busy, but a pipe the Agent cannot open in half a second is worth surfacing too.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: sbom: warn when container image scanning has no container runtime
signals.text: Container image SBOMs come from images that workloadmeta discovers through the container runtime. With no runtime the collectors stay disabled, no image entity is ever created, and the check reports itself healthy while emitting only the host SBOM. A customer spent a week on a correct configuration because nothing said the images were never found. Warn once at configuration time. The gate is sbom.container_image.enabled, which defaults to false, rather than container_image.enabled, which defaults to true and would warn on nearly every host without containers. The check is only scheduled when sbom.enabled is true, so setting sbom.container_image.enabled on its own stays as silent as before. Only Docker, containerd and CRI-O build image SBOMs, so the runtime test names those three rather than calling IsAnyContainerFeaturePresent. That helper also answers true for Kubernetes, ECS, Cloud Foundry and Podman, and a Kubernetes node whose runtime socket is not mounted is precisely the case this warning exists for.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: healthplatform: correct the docker permission issue impact
signals.text: The check that raises this issue detects an unreachable Docker socket, so the Agent cannot query the daemon at all and container metrics, container image collection and container image vulnerability scanning all go quiet. The impact named only the log tailing fallback, so an operator chasing missing images would read the issue and dismiss it. Worse, that fallback cannot happen. Socket tailing needs the very socket that is unreachable. Everything named is scoped to Docker. The check only proves that a default Docker socket exists and cannot be opened, not that Docker is the runtime in use, so a containerd or CRI-O node with a stale inaccessible socket keeps reporting all of it through its own collector. Title, Description and the remediation still describe the log directory case that the logs producer raised before 058e777637d removed it, and the remediation ACLs "<socket>/containers", which helps nobody whose dd-agent user is not in the docker group. Correcting those means replacing the embedded scripts, so they are left for a separate change.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: compliance/k8sconfig: fix kubelet defaults when --config is used
signals.text: Kubernetes keeps the historical command line default of a few kubelet flags to preserve the command line API, and drops them as soon as the kubelet is started with --config. The configuration file is then loaded with the KubeletConfiguration defaults instead, and only the flags that appear on the command line are applied on top of it. The loader applied the command line defaults in both cases. The two sets of defaults disagree on exactly the three settings the CIS Kubernetes benchmarks care about. A kubelet reading a configuration file that leaves them out runs with the read-only port disabled, anonymous authentication disabled and Webhook authorization, while the loader reported a read-only port on 10255, anonymous authentication enabled and an AlwaysAllow authorization mode. OpenShift and kubeadm both leave readOnlyPort out of their rendered configuration, so their nodes failed "The kubelet read-only port should be disabled" with the port closed. The generator now carries the configuration file default next to the command line one for those three flags, and the loader picks between them by whether the component reads a configuration file. The payload version is bumped so that rules can tell the two apart. Updates CSPDE-1519.
signals.author: 0intro

signals.title: compliance/k8sconfig: tell an unreadable file from an empty one
signals.text: The loader stats a configuration file, reads it, then parses whatever it got. A read that fails, typically a permission denied on a root-owned kubeconfig, went to the errors list alone. Parsing an empty read yields an empty configuration, matching a file that really is empty, and the errors list stays out of reach of the rules. So an unreadable file quietly became a file holding nothing. detectManagedEnvironment falls back to the kubelet kubeconfig to recognize an EKS, GKE or AKS control plane when the node labels say nothing, and it walked the three empty maps of a manufactured kubeconfig to conclude that the node was unmanaged. Content that could not be read is now left out rather than parsed, so the detection sees an absent kubeconfig rather than invented evidence. Such a node is still reported as unmanaged: classifying it needs a resource type the rule set would have to define, which is a separate matter. The ownership and permissions from the stat are kept, which also fixes the benchmarks looking at them. They used to see a mode of zero for an unreadable kubelet configuration file and pass. Updates CSPDE-1519.
signals.author: 0intro

### What does this PR do? Allows `DatadogInstrumentation` checks and logs configurations to target Strimzi `StrimziPodSet` workloads. The root-owner resolver explicitly recognizes direct `StrimziPodSet` ownership, with regression coverage ensuring CEL matching uses the Strimzi workload kind and name. ### Motivation Strimzi-managed Kafka pods use a custom workload owner instead of a native Kubernetes workload kind, so customers could not target them with `DatadogInstrumentation` configurations. signals.title: fix(windows): don't lock out the domain agent user account on upgrade
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the Windows MSI set `dd-procmgr-service`'s start type to **disabled** when the Agent user password is not available, and back to **demand start** once it is available again. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3052 #incident-59268 `dd-procmgr-service` created and runs as `ddagentuser` in 7.82.0 and, unlike the earlier services that hit this same class of bug (security-agent, DDOT, PAR), it **runs by default**. On a manual MSI upgrade that does not re-provide `DDAGENTUSER_PASSWORD` and has no LSA secret — the case for hosts first installed with **7.65 or earlier**, since only 7.66+ began storing it: 1. `InstallServices` creates the service with a domain account and an **empty password**. 2. `ConfigureServiceUsers` sees no password and passes `null` to `SetCredentials`, which leaves the empty password in place. 3. The service fails to log on (Event 7000/7038, Security 4625 substatus `0xC000006A`). 4. Failure actions are `restart` ×3 with `RestartServiceDelayInSeconds = 60`, but **`ResetPeriodInDays = 0`** makes the SCM reset the failure counter immediately, so it applies the *first* action forever and never exhausts the three restarts. Hence Event 7031 reporting *"It has done this 1 time(s)"* on every iteration, and an **unbounded 60-second retry loop**. 5. Five failed logons **lock out the account in about 4 minutes**, unattended, on a single host — and because it is a domain account, the Agent then fails to start on **every host sharing it**. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests** — new `CustomActions.Tests/Service/ProcmgrStartTypeTests.cs`, 8 cases: domain-without-password → `Disabled`; domain-with-password, **local-without-password**, gMSA and LocalSystem → `Manual`; `ERROR_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` swallowed; any other failure propagates; and no other service's start type is touched. **E2E, domain** — new `testUpgradeWithoutStoredPasswordSuite` in `tests/windows/domain-test` installs **7.65.2-1** with a domain account and password, upgrades **without** a password, then asserts that `dd-procmgr-service` start type is `SERVICE_DISABLED`, that the core Agent is healthy and payloads reach the fakeintake, and — as a positive control — that re-installing *with* the password restores `SERVICE_DEMAND_START` and the service starts. The existing `testUpgradeSuite` does not catch this, because it installs last stable (7.82.x), which already stores the LSA secret. **E2E, non-domain** — one assertion added to `install-test`'s `TestUpgrade`, which is the exact local-account analogue (default local `ddagentuser`, upgraded without a password), asserting the service **stays enabled**. **Manual QA — reproduced the bug, then verified the fix against it** Run on a domain VM (`WIN-Q4KDLA2CBJF.test.local`, domain account `TEST\ddagentuser`), as an A/B against an identical baseline. *A — unpatched build (7.82.2, unpatched).* Installed Agent **7.65.2** (pre-dates the LSA secret store, matching real affected hosts), then upgraded to 7.82.2 without re-supplying the password. Reproduced the exact incident signature: - System **7000 / 7031 / 7038** every 60s, each reporting *"done this 1 time(s)"* forever — the `ResetPeriodInDays = 0` behavior described above - Security **4625** sub-status `0xC000006A` from `services.exe` - **account locked out in ~4 minutes**, matching the incident report *B — this PR* (build from pipeline `132180801`, commit `c9e8439f`). Reset to the identical clean baseline and repeated the same no-password upgrade: - `dd-procmgr-service` came up **Disabled** instead of retry-looping - **zero** logon-failure events, `badPwdCount` stayed **0**, no lockout across a 5+ minute observation window - `datadogagent` kept running normally *Positive control.* Reinstalled the fixed build **with** the password supplied — `dd-procmgr-service` flipped back to **Manual** (demand start) and started successfully. ### Additional Notes **Why the MSI and not `pkg/fleet/installer`** (per `.claude/rules/msi.md`): For now it is a simpler fix to do in the MSI. Though doing it in the `pkg/fleet/installer` is possible and could be done instead. **Why disabling is safe:** every service uses `StartOn = null` / `StopOn = null`, `ConfigureServices` runs `When.After Step.InstallServices`, and `StartDDServices` runs later — so the service is disabled *before any logon attempt exists*. A disabled procmgr does not break the core Agent: `startDependentServices` only logs a warning when a dependent service fails to start. **Re-enabling is done by this custom action, not by MSI.** Services are *not* deleted and recreated on upgrade. Verified from the MSI logs of the E2E run: `DeleteServices` never executes, and after `RemoveExistingProducts` the `StopDDServices` pass still finds `datadogagent`, `datadog-trace-agent`, `datadog-process-agent`, `datadog-system-probe` and `datadog-security-agent` already present. That is also *why* the underlying bug is limited to newly added services — existing ones keep their stored credentials, which is exactly what would break fleet-wide if MSI rewrote them from the `ServiceInstall` table on every upgrade. So a disabled start type **does persist across upgrades**, and the `else` branch setting `Manual` is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: it is the only thing that brings procmgr back. Confirmed in the reinstall log: `ConfigureProcmgrStartType. Setting dd-procmgr-service start type to Manual`. This matters for #54735 / #54731: when procmgr moves to LocalSystem, that call must be **replaced with an unconditional enable, not deleted**. `passwordUnavailable` describes the Agent user, not the account the service runs as, so leaving it would disable a service that no longer needs a password — but deleting it outright would strand every host this fix disabled in a permanently disabled state. **Behavior change to be aware of:** while procmgr is disabled, DDOT / PAR / ADP do not run. **Rollback record is currently ommited:** For now we are just rolling back with the service disabled. As the service could be unhealthy in the previous state. So we are just leaving it disabled for now. **Not in this PR, follow-ups:** 1. An `agent status` warning when procmgr is disabled for this reason. 2. #54735 / #54731 run procmgr as LocalSystem with spawn profiles, removing the ddagentuser logon entirely. this MSI workaround can be relaxed once they land. 3. Should we add support for rollback Intended for backport to `7.82.x` for 7.82.3. Every production file touched is byte-identical between `main` and `origin/7.82.x`, so the cherry-pick should be conflict-free.
signals.author: jack0x2

signals.title: feat(windows): enforce the config root security check on uninstall too
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Stacked on #55136. Extends that PR's config-root owner check to uninstall and upgrade-removal, which it currently skips, and trusts one more owner: - `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` now runs unconditionally in the MSI's `InstallExecuteSequence`, including on uninstall and removal for an upgrade, instead of being skipped there. It only asserts ownership and never changes anything, so it can't leave a partial uninstall behind. - `DDCreateFolders` now runs on every install/upgrade/repair/uninstall pass instead of only on first install, creating the config root if it's missing. It only resets an existing directory's permissions on a true first install, so upgrade/repair/uninstall never strips access (e.g. ddagentuser's) granted after the directory was first created. - The maintenance dialog's config-root check is now a single check on the Welcome dialog's `Next`, covering Change, Repair, and Remove alike, instead of a separate per-button check that skipped Remove. - `ContainerAdministrator` (the account Windows containers run as by default) is trusted alongside `Administrators`/`SYSTEM` in both the Go and MSI checks. ### Motivation Uninstall-time steps that depend on the config root (e.g. the fleet installer's `prerm` hook) should get the same defense-in-depth guarantee installation already has, instead of only install/upgrade/repair being covered. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New/updated `SecureDirectory` unit tests for the create-if-missing-without-reset behavior used outside first install, and for trusting `ContainerAdministrator`. - Fixed a race in `TestInstallAltDirAndCorruptForUninstall`: the test deleted the Agent's registry key while the service was still running, which could let the running Agent (as `ddagentuser`) recreate the default config directory itself before the fix stopped the service first.
signals.author: clarkb7

signals.title: feat(windows): require the Agent configuration directory to be owned by an administrator
signals.text: _Re-lands #54269 (reverted for #incident-58787) unchanged. Follow-up fixes and the uninstall/upgrade-removal enforcement are stacked on top in #55133._ ### What does this PR do? Installation now fails when `C:\ProgramData\Datadog` already exists and is not owned by `Administrators` or `SYSTEM`, in both the MSI and the Go installer. The error names the owner found and the `takeown.exe` command to resolve it. - **MSI**: new `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` custom action after `InstallValidate`, so nothing has been changed on the system when it fails. It is skipped when uninstalling or being removed for an upgrade. The same check runs from the Welcome dialog and from maintenance Change/Repair, reporting through a popup; Remove is deliberately not checked. - **New `SecureDirectory` primitive** shared by `DDCreateFolders` and the rollback data store. It creates a directory with a protected SYSTEM/Administrators DACL, then reads the owner and applies permissions through a single handle that does not follow reparse points. - **Go installer**: `ensureDatadogDataDir` creates or validates the configuration directory, and `IsDirSecure` returns an actionable message. A new msiexec log pattern surfaces the failure in installer output. - **Error dialog**: replaces WixUI's `ErrorDlg` with `Custom_ErrorDialog`, sized like the existing modal, because the stock 205x60 text control clips these messages. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2998 Defense in depth. The Agent's configuration directory must be attributable to an administrator; if it already exists under another owner, resetting its permissions is not sufficient, so installation stops and explains how to resolve it instead of adopting the directory. This is a behavior change on both fresh installs and upgrades - existing installations are already compatible, since the MSI sets SYSTEM as the owner. Covered by the included `upgrade` release note. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New E2E test `TestInstallWithUntrustedConfigRoot`, wired into the `e2e_install_packages` job and run against AWS. - New tests for `SecureDirectory`, the MSI message escaping, `ensureDatadogDataDir`/`IsDirSecure`, and the msiexec log pattern - whose fixture is taken from a real MSI log. - Installed manually on a Windows VM with the configuration directory owned by a non-administrator, checking the message and the error dialog. - cross-ref'd ansible and chef packages to ensure compatability ### Additional Notes `Custom_ErrorDialog` is a renamed copy rather than a redefinition of `ErrorDlg`, since a WixUI library dialog cannot be redefined. Per the MSI spec it keeps `ErrorText` as its first control and all seven `Error*` buttons. MSI popup

signals.title: otel-agent: support standalone DDOT without a datadog exporter
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? - Keeps `standaloneAgentFxOptions` in the fx graph in standalone mode (`DD_OTEL_STANDALONE=true`) even when no datadog exporter is configured, so a standalone DDOT can run with e.g. an OTLP-only exporter forwarding to a gateway collector. - Adds e2e coverage: a standalone otel-agent DaemonSet leaf (dogtel extension, OTLP exporter) forwarding traces/metrics/logs to a separate Helm-deployed gateway otel-agent, which ships them to fakeintake. Also verifies the dogtel liveness metric and tagger server on the leaf, and that neither side of the topology runs a core Datadog Agent pod. ### Motivation Today, `getDDExporterConfig` returns `ErrNoDDExporter` and previously prevented standalone DDOT from starting at all when the OTel Collector config has no `datadog` exporter block (e.g. a pure leaf-to-gateway OTLP topology). This PR allows that mode to run. Related: [OTAGENT-1083](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1083) **Note on API keys in this mode:** when there is no `datadog` exporter in the config, the sync from the OTel Collector's `exporters.datadog.api.key`/`.api.site` into the agent config (`cmd/otel-agent/config/agent_config.go`, `getDDExporterConfig`) never runs, since that code path returns early on `ErrNoDDExporter`. Any component that still needs an API key in this mode (e.g. the agent serializer for the dogtel liveness metric) must instead get it the same way a regular core Agent does: via the `DD_API_KEY` env var or `api_key:` in the core config file (`--core-config`), which is loaded unconditionally, independent of the OTel Collector config. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv linter.go --module=test/new-e2e --targets=./tests/otel/otel-agent` — 0 issues - `TestDogtelStandaloneGateway` e2e suite run on a local kind cluster: verifies traces/metrics/logs reach fakeintake through the leaf -> gateway path, the dogtel liveness metric and tagger server on the leaf, and that no core Agent pod runs on either side. ### Additional Notes [OTAGENT-1083]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1083?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: remote queries: add deterministic intake relay proof tooling
signals.text: ## Stack - Base: #55153 (`nubtron/remote-queries-intake-poc`) - This draft: test-only deterministic relay proof ## Summary - drive exact 8 MiB and 32 MiB producer streams through the actual relay - verify bounded chunking, aggregate hashing, receipt-only output, and backpressure - cover rejection-before-accept and lost-response-after-accept idempotent retries ## Validation - 135 focused package tests passed after the production lint fix was merged - synthetic M3/M5 proof passed all cases - lint and reliabilint passed - signed commits independently reviewed ## Deployment Test-only local proof tooling; no production deployment.

signals.title: [Backport 7.83.x]  fix(ssi): run host SSI instrument-start/stop before Docker run
signals.text: Backport 78ff898c238d669cb2cbbfa4ca3379cfbb9b20af from #55020. ___ In a stale state (ld.preload pointing to a non existent tmp injector), Docker doesn't start correctly. We should always run the SSI installer before Docker to clean/repair ld.preload file. Also always run the shutdown phase, even if the start was not successful (stop is idempotent).

signals.title: [PoC] Add metricslogs component for local metrics-as-logs debugging
signals.text: ## What this change does Adding `comp/forwarder/metricslogs` component. This component writes metrics as structured JSON lines to the agent's own local log. Other internal agent components can use this component to write metrics as logs, bypassing tags cardinality limits. ## Why we need this change `ebpf-check` emits metrics for each map and each program. This creates too many tag combinations. These combinations overflow the metrics cardinality limits. This component gives a safe way to write this kind of data as a structured log line, not as a tagged metric. ## Important limits This component is for internal use only. Do not use it for customer-facing metrics. This component only writes to the agent's local log. It never sends data over the network. It does not need `logs_enabled`. It does not create billable Log volume. It has no config gate: any caller can use it at any time. ## How the component behaves The caller sends one batch of metrics in one call, through `LogMetrics(metrics []*Metric) error`. The component builds one structured JSON line from the batch and writes it to the local log at Debug level. All metrics in the batch share one log line. An empty batch is a no-op. ## How this was tested - Unit tests cover the component: a normal call with several metrics, and an empty batch. - The full agent binary was built with this change. The build was successful. - The Go linter was run on the new code. The linter found no issues. ## Follow-up work - A separate PR (#55234) adds a `WithLevel` option, so a caller can choose Trace instead of Debug. - Connect the ebpf-check to this component.

signals.title: fix(rtloader): do not crash when formatting lone-surrogate Python exceptions
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a crash in rtloader when formatting a Python check exception whose message or traceback contains a Unicode lone surrogate (for example `\ud800`). `_fetchPythonError()` in `rtloader/three/three.cpp` converted traceback and exception strings with strict `as_string()`. Lone surrogates cannot be encoded as UTF-8, so conversion returned `NULL`, and appending that to a `std::string` caused a SIGSEGV in the core Agent process. This PR: - Adds `as_string_lossy()` in `rtloader/common/stringutils.c`, which encodes Unicode with UTF-8 `backslashreplace` for diagnostic paths. - Routes all exception formatting in `_fetchPythonError()` through a safe helper that skips on allocation failure. - Adds rtloader regression tests for lone-surrogate exceptions in `run_check` and `discover_config`. Strict `as_string()` behavior is unchanged for tags, metrics, events, and other hot paths. ### Motivation Reported by the rtloader vuln audit (`agent-vuln-hunt`, finding `rtloader-lone-surrogate-exception-crash`). A Python integration can raise an exception whose text embeds monitored-service data containing a lone surrogate (for example JSON `{"statusstring":"\ud800"}`). That should surface as a check error, but instead crashed the entire Agent on every scheduled run. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //rtloader/test/rtloader:rtloader_test` - `bazel test //rtloader/test/rtloader:rtloader_test --test_arg=-test.run='LoneSurrogate' --test_output=all` New tests: - `TestRunCheckLoneSurrogateException` - `TestDiscoverConfigRaisesLoneSurrogate` Both assert the Agent gets a Python error containing `\ud800` instead of crashing. ### Additional Notes - Release note: `releasenotes/notes/rtloader-lone-surrogate-exception-78250a6675432d3a.yaml` (`fixes`) - This closes the reported availability issue only. Other `as_string()` call sites already handle `NULL` without crashing and they may still drop or reject unencodable strings on non-exception paths.

signals.title: [CONTINT-5550] Fix Leader Engine initialization retrying
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? This PR changes the way that the global leader election engine is initialized. We will now block waiting for the leader election engine to successfully initialize, patterned after the way the apiserver client is initialized. ### Motivation [Bug finding brief](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~71202044c43e36ccff4aac9e966f298724ef65/pages/7090144314/Cluster+Agent+Crash+Due+to+Apiserver+Network+Blip+During+Startup) [CONTINT-5550](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONTINT-5550) When the leader election engine is first initialized, and the API server is temporarily unavailable, the initialization will fail with a `FailWillRetry` error, but since it happens during startup, the error ends up being bubbled up and causes the DCA to exit. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added three unit tests. ### Additional Notes [CONTINT-5550]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONTINT-5550?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
