signals.text: Backport f776f333c334087d4b4c2f66b7f5dbaf4c051df6 from #55014. ___ ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process can not resolve secret handles and expects to receive them from the core agent already resolved ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.

signals.title: [ACTP] Test PAR task verification end to end
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Updates the PAR E2E tests to run with task signature verification enabled. `fakeintake` now provides the signing key through Remote Config and serves signed tasks through its fake OPMS endpoints. This also separates `fakeintake` OPMS routing from the task-verification bypass and removes the Core Agent restart workaround. Depends on #55208.
signals.author: embeaken

signals.title: Add per-loop trace and per-function spans to sample debugger demo
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the sample debugger demo produce more useful trace data. Each time the demo loop runs, it now starts a fresh trace, and each of the demo's internal steps shows up as its own span within that trace instead of everything being lumped together. ### Motivation Before this change, one run of the demo loop showed up as a single flat block in the trace, so you couldn't tell which part of the demo was doing what. Breaking it into separate steps makes the demo's output more realistic and easier to look at. ### Describe how you validated your changes Ran the demo program directly to confirm it still works end to end. Also ran the full existing test suite for this code and updated the saved test data to match the small internal changes, confirming everything still passes.

signals.title: [Backport 7.83.x]  fix(windows): don't lock out the domain agent user account on upgrade
signals.text: Backport 5cf80f4c717f401d4af45d9ba42fb7c390d5fe13 from #55130. ___ ### What does this PR do? Makes the Windows MSI set `dd-procmgr-service`'s start type to **disabled** when the Agent user password is not available, and back to **demand start** once it is available again. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3052 #incident-59268 `dd-procmgr-service` created and runs as `ddagentuser` in 7.82.0 and, unlike the earlier services that hit this same class of bug (security-agent, DDOT, PAR), it **runs by default**. On a manual MSI upgrade that does not re-provide `DDAGENTUSER_PASSWORD` and has no LSA secret — the case for hosts first installed with **7.65 or earlier**, since only 7.66+ began storing it: 1. `InstallServices` creates the service with a domain account and an **empty password**. 2. `ConfigureServiceUsers` sees no password and passes `null` to `SetCredentials`, which leaves the empty password in place. 3. The service fails to log on (Event 7000/7038, Security 4625 substatus `0xC000006A`). 4. Failure actions are `restart` ×3 with `RestartServiceDelayInSeconds = 60`, but **`ResetPeriodInDays = 0`** makes the SCM reset the failure counter immediately, so it applies the *first* action forever and never exhausts the three restarts. Hence Event 7031 reporting *"It has done this 1 time(s)"* on every iteration, and an **unbounded 60-second retry loop**. 5. Five failed logons **lock out the account in about 4 minutes**, unattended, on a single host — and because it is a domain account, the Agent then fails to start on **every host sharing it**. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests** — new `CustomActions.Tests/Service/ProcmgrStartTypeTests.cs`, 8 cases: domain-without-password → `Disabled`; domain-with-password, **local-without-password**, gMSA and LocalSystem → `Manual`; `ERROR_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` swallowed; any other failure propagates; and no other service's start type is touched. **E2E, domain** — new `testUpgradeWithoutStoredPasswordSuite` in `tests/windows/domain-test` installs **7.65.2-1** with a domain account and password, upgrades **without** a password, then asserts that `dd-procmgr-service` start type is `SERVICE_DISABLED`, that the core Agent is healthy and payloads reach the fakeintake, and — as a positive control — that re-installing *with* the password restores `SERVICE_DEMAND_START` and the service starts. The existing `testUpgradeSuite` does not catch this, because it installs last stable (7.82.x), which already stores the LSA secret. **E2E, non-domain** — one assertion added to `install-test`'s `TestUpgrade`, which is the exact local-account analogue (default local `ddagentuser`, upgraded without a password), asserting the service **stays enabled**. **Manual QA — reproduced the bug, then verified the fix against it** Run on a domain VM (`WIN-Q4KDLA2CBJF.test.local`, domain account `TEST\ddagentuser`), as an A/B against an identical baseline. *A — unpatched build (7.82.2, unpatched).* Installed Agent **7.65.2** (pre-dates the LSA secret store, matching real affected hosts), then upgraded to 7.82.2 without re-supplying the password. Reproduced the exact incident signature: - System **7000 / 7031 / 7038** every 60s, each reporting *"done this 1 time(s)"* forever — the `ResetPeriodInDays = 0` behavior described above - Security **4625** sub-status `0xC000006A` from `services.exe` - **account locked out in ~4 minutes**, matching the incident report *B — this PR* (build from pipeline `132180801`, commit `c9e8439f`). Reset to the identical clean baseline and repeated the same no-password upgrade: - `dd-procmgr-service` came up **Disabled** instead of retry-looping - **zero** logon-failure events, `badPwdCount` stayed **0**, no lockout across a 5+ minute observation window - `datadogagent` kept running normally *Positive control.* Reinstalled the fixed build **with** the password supplied — `dd-procmgr-service` flipped back to **Manual** (demand start) and started successfully. ### Additional Notes **Why the MSI and not `pkg/fleet/installer`** (per `.claude/rules/msi.md`): For now it is a simpler fix to do in the MSI. Though doing it in the `pkg/fleet/installer` is possible and could be done instead. **Why disabling is safe:** every service uses `StartOn = null` / `StopOn = null`, `ConfigureServices` runs `When.After Step.InstallServices`, and `StartDDServices` runs later — so the service is disabled *before any logon attempt exists*. A disabled procmgr does not break the core Agent: `startDependentServices` only logs a warning when a dependent service fails to start. **Re-enabling is done by this custom action, not by MSI.** Services are *not* deleted and recreated on upgrade. Verified from the MSI logs of the E2E run: `DeleteServices` never executes, and after `RemoveExistingProducts` the `StopDDServices` pass still finds `datadogagent`, `datadog-trace-agent`, `datadog-process-agent`, `datadog-system-probe` and `datadog-security-agent` already present. That is also *why* the underlying bug is limited to newly added services — existing ones keep their stored credentials, which is exactly what would break fleet-wide if MSI rewrote them from the `ServiceInstall` table on every upgrade. So a disabled start type **does persist across upgrades**, and the `else` branch setting `Manual` is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: it is the only thing that brings procmgr back. Confirmed in the reinstall log: `ConfigureProcmgrStartType. Setting dd-procmgr-service start type to Manual`. This matters for #54735 / #54731: when procmgr moves to LocalSystem, that call must be **replaced with an unconditional enable, not deleted**. `passwordUnavailable` describes the Agent user, not the account the service runs as, so leaving it would disable a service that no longer needs a password — but deleting it outright would strand every host this fix disabled in a permanently disabled state. **Behavior change to be aware of:** while procmgr is disabled, DDOT / PAR / ADP do not run. **Rollback record is currently ommited:** For now we are just rolling back with the service disabled. As the service could be unhealthy in the previous state. So we are just leaving it disabled for now. **Not in this PR, follow-ups:** 1. An `agent status` warning when procmgr is disabled for this reason. 2. #54735 / #54731 run procmgr as LocalSystem with spawn profiles, removing the ddagentuser logon entirely. this MSI workaround can be relaxed once they land. 3. Should we add support for rollback Intended for backport to `7.82.x` for 7.82.3. Every production file touched is byte-identical between `main` and `origin/7.82.x`, so the cherry-pick should be conflict-free.

The bazel migration is now complete enough so that - There is little (or no) need to make global changes to BUILD.bazel files. - The tools to update BUILD files are reliable enough for people to use without an extra audit.

signals.title: [ACTP] Fakeintake RC improvements for full PAR task verification
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? 1. Makes fakeintake serve one shared set of Remote Config files (see note on behavior below). 2. Adds support for sending signed PAR tasks so E2E tests can run with task verification enabled. ### Motivation This enables PAR E2E tests to exercise real task-signature verification. See #55202 for the tests that use this support. #### Remote Config behavior `fakeintake` now returns the full config set to the Agent under test. Upstream from `fakeintake`, the Agent still gives each component only the products it requested. This keeps `fakeintake` config delivery independent of component startup order. For example, a component that subscribes after the Agent’s first Remote Config poll can still receive a config that was already stored in `fakeintake`.

signals.title: fix(lint_windows-x64): move `cwdLogLimiter` out of shared file
signals.text: ### Motivation Despite #55076 and #55162, `lint_windows-x64` still fails, this time on the system-probe go linter step ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1971344465)): ``` Linter failures: pkg\network\sender\event_consumer.go:96:5: var cwdLogLimiter is unused (unused) var cwdLogLimiter = logutil.NewLogLimit(20, 10*time.Minute) ^ 1 issues: * unused: 1 system-probe Go linter result is 1 system-probe go linter failed 1 ``` `event_consumer.go` builds under `linux || (windows && npm)`, but `cwdLogLimiter` is only read from `event_consumer_linux.go`, whose `_linux.go` suffix restricts it to `GOOS=linux`: the `windows && npm` build declares the limiter and never uses it. ### What does this PR do? Move the `cwdLogLimiter` declaration, and its now-unused `time` and `logutil` imports, from `event_consumer.go` into `event_consumer_linux.go`, next to its only caller. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/network/sender/...`

signals.title: Update gcc-toolchain to 0.12.1
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Updates gcc-toolchain to 0.12.1 and adjusts patches accordingly. ### Motivation https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54846 has run into linking errors (https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1968744747). The issue has to do with the linker resolving against the actual filesystem root instead of the sysroot's. I think https://github.com/f0rmiga/gcc-toolchain/pull/231 is what fixes this for us in this case, and this version incorporates the change. ### Describe how you validated your changes Green CI, and build passing for https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54846 locally (under linux arm64, at least). ### Additional Notes The core of the issue is that the linker was picking files from the sysroot via `-L%workspace%/{include_prefix}sysroot/lib` etc., which picked up at least one linker script with absolute (sysroot-relative) paths. Given that we're not providing a `--sysroot`, this is trying to link against things in the host, which is obviously wrong and breaks loudly here. Upstream gcc-toolchain has dropped these `-B` and `-L` flags pointing into the sysroot, which removes the problem. I still don't know exactly why that target specifically was the one to hit this error (despite having other targets that link against zstd via cgo).
signals.author: alopezz

signals.title: Remove explicit execution of otel integration test (task and CI)
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? It removes the otel-agent.integration invoke task and removes the run of the integration test that runs on the `integration_tests_otel` job. ### Motivation https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55117 (which https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55163 made possible) runs all go tests without race detection, which includes this test. This test is skipped in "legacy" test jobs because they run exclusively with race detection enabled and the test is tagged with `!race`. Given that we're now running this test under Bazel already, running it again from this job and having an ad-hoc task for the test looks redundant. ### Describe how you validated your changes Green CI. ### Additional Notes I'm open to keeping the task (which could invoke bazel instead) for now if the owning team feels strongly about it, but I'd strongly suggest we don't and that we use bazel to run the test when needed.

Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/33469) for more information. --- ### Release Notes <details> <summary>open-policy-agent/opa (github.com/open-policy-agent/opa)</summary> ### [`v1.19.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/releases/tag/v1.19.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/compare/v1.18.2...v1.19.0) This release contains a mix of new features and bug fixes. Notably: - A fixed SQL injection vector in the Compile API - Stricter safety checking for Rego assignments (`:=`) - A cgo-free, faster WebAssembly runtime (wazero replaces wasmtime-go) - Startup warnings for unknown configuration options - A new `strings.split_n` built-in function - A REPL line reader that handles pasted input correctly, migrating existing history files ##### Fix SQL injection vector in Compile API: Quote SQL filter field identifiers ([#​8945](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/pull/8945)) The field names in the SQL emitted by the Compile API come from partially evaluated refs, so a policy that selects a dynamic key — such as `input.fruits[input.column]` — puts caller-controlled text in an identifier position. That text was emitted verbatim, which turns ```sql WHERE fruit.name = 'allowed' ``` into ```sql WHERE fruit.name = 'allowed' OR 1=1 -- = 'allowed' ``` and an application appending the filter to its query returns rows the policy denies. Field segments that are not bare identifiers are now quoted at the UCAST-to-SQL boundary, with any embedded quote character escaped. Ordinary column names stay unquoted, so existing filters keep their current shape and remain case-insensitive on Postgres. Authored by [@​thevilledev](https://redirect.github.com/thevilledev) ##### Behavior change: stricter safety for assignment (`:=`) ([#​3546](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/issues/3546)) The assignment operator (`:=`) is documented as "syntactic sugar for `=`, local variable creation, and additional compiler checks," and the safety checker reflects that: after rewriting, `:=` is treated identically to `=` (unification), so an assignment's right-hand side can be made safe by unifying "backwards" through the left-hand side. This means policies like `x := y; x = 7` compile (binding `y` to `7`) even though `y` is never assigned, and `x := y; obj[x]` can silently degrade an expected constant-time lookup into full iteration. This change makes the right-hand-side of `:=` be treated as a read that must be made safe by other expressions, and can no longer be satisfied through the left-hand-side. Affected policies that previously compiled now fail with a `rego_unsafe_var_error`. Reference iteration on the right-hand-side (e.g. `some k; v := obj[k]`) is unaffected. Note: this is a deliberate semantic change, not a fix to match documented behavior — the intended semantics of `:=` in this case were never specified. Authored by [@​sspaink](https://redirect.github.com/sspaink), reported by [@​tsandall](https://redirect.github.com/tsandall) ##### WebAssembly runtime: wasmtime-go replaced with wazero ([#​7557](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/issues/7557)) OPA's WebAssembly runtime — used by the `wasm` evaluation target and the WASM SDK — now runs on the pure-Go [wazero](https://wazero.io/) runtime instead of `bytecodealliance/wasmtime-go`. This removes the cgo dependency from this path, so `wasm`-enabled builds no longer need a C toolchain. Compiled policy modules are now cached process-wide, so repeated VM creation for the same policy skips recompilation. On an Apple M4 Max this makes wasm cold start (compile + instantiate + first eval) about 73% faster, and warm evaluation about 29% faster with \~28% fewer allocations. Authored by [@​srenatus](https://redirect.github.com/srenatus), reported by [@​sspaink](https://redirect.github.com/sspaink) ##### Configuration validation moved to Rego, with warnings on unknown options ([#​8891](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/pull/8891)) Top-level configuration validation and default injection (`default_decision`, `default_authorization_decision`, `labels`) is now expressed as an embedded Rego policy rather than hand-written Go, as is the validation of `server.metrics` and `metrics_export`. The user-visible effect is that unrecognized configuration options are reported instead of being silently ignored. A typo such as `decision_log` instead of `decision_logs` now logs a warning at startup: ```json {"level":"warning","msg":"unknown configuration option \"decision_log\" encountered"} ``` These are warnings, not errors: OPA starts as before, and sections that are intentionally user-extensible are left alone, so extra keys there do not warn. Embedders reading configuration through `config.ParseConfig` can find the same messages on `Config.Warnings`. Authored by [@​sspaink](https://redirect.github.com/sspaink) ##### Add `strings.split_n` built-in function ([#​8344](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/issues/8344)) Policies often need only the first or last few parts of a split string, but the existing `split` built-in always returns every part, so the count has to be worked around with wildcards or a slice. `strings.split_n` takes the first `n` split parts from the front or the back of the string, depending on whether `n` is positive or negative: ```rego result := strings.split_n("a.b.c.d", ".", 2) # result == ["a", "b"] ``` ```rego result := strings.split_n("a.b.c.d", ".", -2) # result == ["c", "d"] ``` If `abs(n)` is larger than the number of parts, all parts are returned. An `n` of `0` returns an empty array. Authored by [@​wonju-dev](https://redirect.github.com/wonju-dev), reported by [@​anderseknert](https://redirect.github.com/anderseknert) ##### Improved REPL line editing, with history file migration ([#​962](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/issues/962)) Pasting a tab-indented snippet into the REPL triggered tab-completion on the pasted tab, corrupting the input (e.g. injecting a completion candidate mid-line and producing a spurious parse error). Fixing that requires bracketed paste, where the terminal wraps pasted text in markers so the line reader inserts it literally instead of treating an embedded tab as a completion request. The previous reader, `peterh/liner`, has no bracketed-paste support and is unmaintained (last release 2021\), so it has been replaced with `reeflective/readline`. The new reader persists history as JSON lines instead of one command per line. Existing history files (`~/.opa_history` by default, or the path given to `--history`) are detected and migrated in place the first time the REPL loads them, so history written by earlier versions of OPA is kept. OPA's own multi-line buffering is unchanged, and `readline`'s native multi-line editing is left disabled to avoid changing REPL behavior. Authored by [@​sspaink](https://redirect.github.com/sspaink), reported by [@​aeneasr](https://redirect.github.com/aeneasr) ##### Runtime, SDK, Tooling - cmd: Avoid intermediate buffer when writing bundle ([#​8909](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/pull/8909)) authored by [@​anderseknert](https://redirect.github.com/anderseknert) - Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/33469) for more information. --- ### Release Notes <details> <summary>sirupsen/logrus (github.com/sirupsen/logrus)</summary> ### [`v1.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/sirupsen/logrus/releases/tag/v1.10.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sirupsen/logrus/compare/v1.9.4...v1.10.0) ### Logrus v1.10.0 This release focuses on substantial performance improvements, concurrency correctness, and better interoperability with modern Go logging APIs. #### 🚀 Performance Major improvements across `TextFormatter`, entry handling, and common logger paths: - \~17% lower geomean runtime across the benchmark suite - \~27% higher geomean formatter throughput - Common enabled logging paths are \~30–44% faster - `WithError` is \~40% faster - Chained fields are \~46% faster - `TextFormatter` paths are up to \~40% faster - Allocation counts are reduced by \~25–74% across measured `TextFormatter` cases, with the largest reductions in colored output The improvements also show up in complete logger paths: - Logger + `TextFormatter` is \~31% faster, with \~24% fewer allocations - Logger + `JSONFormatter` is \~21% faster, with \~10% fewer allocations `JSONFormatter` itself remains largely unchanged in runtime performance, with small allocation reductions. #### 🔄 `log/slog` interoperability v1.10 adds bidirectional interoperability between Logrus and Go's `log/slog`: - A Logrus `slog` hook can forward existing Logrus entries to an `slog` logger. - `hooks/slog.NewHandler` implements `slog.Handler`, allowing `log/slog` records to use an existing Logrus logger and its hooks, formatter, and output. - The handler preserves levels, fields, groups, context, record timestamps, and optionally caller information. - Caller reporting is configured per handler, without requiring Logrus's logger-wide `ReportCaller` option. - Custom `slog` levels can be mapped to Logrus levels. - The hook and handler can be combined, providing a practical path for incrementally migrating from Logrus to `log/slog` without requiring an all-at-once transition. This allows applications to migrate their logging API and logging backend independently: existing Logrus call sites can start using an `slog` backend, while new `slog` code can continue using an established Logrus setup. #### 🔒 Concurrency & Correctness - Fix reentrant logging deadlocks, including logging from within `MarshalJSON` or formatter code. - Fix generic `Log`, `Logf`, `Logln`, and `LogFn` methods unexpectedly panicking when called with `PanicLevel`, contrary to their documented behavior. - Eliminate race conditions in entry and formatter paths. - Improve locking boundaries around formatters and hooks. #### ➕ Added - `TextFormatter` now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching behavior on other platforms. - `Entry.Caller` can now be set explicitly and is preserved across derived entries. When caller reporting is enabled, Logrus only detects and populates caller information when none was provided, allowing custom caller detection and wrapper-aware logging without adding additional caller configuration APIs. - Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level, allowing consumers to depend on narrower interfaces and making logging implementations easier to substitute or adapt. - Expand CI verification to include TinyGo and every cross-compile target reported by go tool dist list, improving coverage across alternative toolchains and platforms. #### ⚠️ Behavioral Changes - Minimum supported Go version is now **1.23**. - `TextFormatter` now renders `[]byte` as raw/quoted strings instead of numeric slices. If you relied on the previous slice-of-ints output, convert explicitly before logging. - `TextFormatter` now uses dim cyan for debug output and dim white for trace output in colorized TTY output. - `Entry.HasCaller` is now deprecated in favor of checking `Entry.Caller` directly. A `//go:fix inline` directive was added so existing uses can be updated automatically. - `MutexWrap`, which was unintentionally exposed as public API, is deprecated. It remains available as an alias for compatibility but should not be used directly. *** v1.10 is primarily a performance, correctness, and interoperability release with no intentional breaking public signals.title: fix(tasks): ignore standalone files when checking pkg ownership
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Updates `directory_has_packages_without_owner` (used by the CODEOWNERS ownership linter) to skip standalone files directly under `/pkg` (e.g. `BUILD.bazel`), only checking directory entries. It now uses `os.scandir` instead of `os.listdir` to filter out non-directory entries, and builds paths with `pathlib.Path` (using `.as_posix()`) to keep path separators forward-slash on all platforms, including Windows. ### Motivation The linter was flagging root-level files like `/pkg/BUILD.bazel` as unowned "packages", which isn't correct — single files at the root of `/pkg` aren't standalone packages and shouldn't require a dedicated CODEOWNERS entry. This was causing a CI failure: https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/datadog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1971316454 ### Describe how you validated your changes Added/updated unit tests in `tasks/unit_tests/codeowner_linter_tests.py` covering the new behavior (root-level files under `/pkg` are ignored) and updated an existing test whose fixture relied on the old behavior. Ran the full `codeowner_linter_tests` and `linter_tests` suites (43 tests, all passing) and `ruff check`/`ruff format`.

signals.title: [AAD-6] Update BOCPD posterior in place
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? This reduces BOCPD detector memory by removing 3 arrays `newRunProbs, newMeans, newPrecisions` which are replaced by a backward recurrence instead. It reduces by almost 50% the memory of this detector. signals.title: [Backport 7.82.x] Bump Bazel to 9.2.0  for remote cache and Windows fixes (#53619)
signals.text: Bump the pinned Bazel version from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0 and refresh `MODULE.bazel.lock` accordingly. Bazel 9.2.0 ships fixes this repo has been working around over the past month. Our contributions: - bazelbuild/bazel#29984, which should remove the need for temporary countermeasures we had to come up with: - DataDog/datadog-agent-buildimages#1212 (alas ineffective), - DataDog/datadog-agent-buildimages#1215 (effective), - #52500, - bazelbuild/bazel#30182, which should remove the need for: - #52061, - #53591. - bazelbuild/bazel#29791, - bazelbuild/bazel#29868, - bazelbuild/bazel#29885, - bazelbuild/bazel#30193, a caveat mentioned in: - #53356. Also worth noting, though not tied to a specific incident here: - bazelbuild/bazel#29807, - bazelbuild/bazel#29898, - bazelbuild/bazel#30194. `bazel version` reports 9.2.0 after `bazelisk` re-bootstraps. `bazel build //pkg/config/schema/...` completes successfully. `bazel shutdown` followed by `bazel mod deps --lockfile_mode=refresh` leaves `MODULE.bazel.lock` unchanged. None of the .bazelrc UAC/8dot3 workarounds (DataDog/datadog-agent-buildimages#1215, #52500, #52061, #53591) are removed here. Each needs its own re-verification on Windows before being reverted as follow-ups. signals.text: <!-- dd-meta {"pullId":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000","source":"chat","resourceId":"1dd901d3-691c-4fc8-ac44-10e6da9179e0","workflowId":"92770bc9-1d63-478d-bfcc-a935837edd32","codeChangeId":"92770bc9-1d63-478d-bfcc-a935837edd32","sourceType":"slack"} --> ### What does this PR do? Two related changes to make the `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-{ubuntu,debian}-*` E2E jobs resilient to Ubuntu package-mirror outages: 1. **Wire `(*Host).ConfigureAptMirrors()` into the DDOT install suite** (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-platform/tests/ddot_install_test.go`), called from `SetupSuite` next to the existing `ConfigureYumMirrors()`. On Ubuntu it bounds apt's per-request timeout/retries and rewrites the apt sources to a `mirror+file` list so apt fails over to the global `archive.ubuntu.com` / `ports.ubuntu.com` mirrors when the regional EC2 mirror is unavailable. Both helpers no-op on the other's package manager. 2. **Guard the `mirror+file` source rewrite behind a method-driver check** in the shared helper (`test/new-e2e/tests/installer/host/host.go`). The `mirror+file` transport only exists in apt >= 1.6 (Ubuntu >= 18.04). On older releases (Ubuntu 16.04 ships apt 1.2) the method driver is absent, so rewriting the sources to `mirror+file:` makes every subsequent apt operation fail with `The method driver /usr/lib/apt/methods/mirror+file could not be found`. The helper now probes `test -e /usr/lib/apt/methods/mirror+file` and skips the source rewrite when it is missing; the Acquire retry/timeout hardening still applies on those hosts. ### Motivation The `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-ubuntu-a7-arm64` job flakes red on `main` (incident 59571). Its Ubuntu/Debian install path runs `apt-get update && apt-get install -y apt-transport-https curl gnupg` against a single regional EC2 Ubuntu mirror with no fallback and no bounded timeout; a `503`/slow mirror either fails fast or hangs to the 2h CI timeout. The apt-mirror resilience helper already existed and was used by the installer suites; a prior fix (#54987) added only the yum counterpart to the DDOT suite. Change 1 closes that gap. Change 2 fixes a regression that change 1 introduced: because the installer suites only run Ubuntu 24.04, the helper's `mirror+file` rewrite had never been exercised on old apt. The DDOT job runs Ubuntu 16.04, where the rewrite made `apt-get update` fail deterministically (job `1972006537`: only the `16-04` subtest failed with the `mirror+file` method-driver error; 18.04/20.04/22.04/24.04 passed). ### Changes - `test/new-e2e/tests/agent-platform/tests/ddot_install_test.go`: call `is.host.ConfigureAptMirrors()` in `SetupSuite`. - `test/new-e2e/tests/installer/host/host.go`: skip the Ubuntu `mirror+file` source rewrite when the `mirror+file` apt method driver is not present (apt < 1.6, e.g. Ubuntu 16.04); keep the Acquire timeout/retry hardening for all apt hosts. Doc comment updated. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Root-caused the failure on the PR pipeline (`new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-ubuntu-a7-x86_64`, job `1972006537`) from CI logs: the `16-04` subtest failed at `apt-get update` with `E: The method driver /usr/lib/apt/methods/mirror+file could not be found`, while the newer Ubuntu subtests in the same job passed — confirming the discriminator is the presence of the `mirror+file` method driver. - Confirmed the installer suites (`tests/installer/unix`, `tests/installer/script`) that already call `ConfigureAptMirrors()` only run Ubuntu 24.04, which is why the incompatibility was latent until now. - `gofmt` reports both files clean. - Type-safe: `h.remote.Execute` already returns `(string, error)` and is used identically in `host.New`; no new imports. - End-to-end validation is the DDOT jobs themselves once this runs in CI: the `16-04` subtest should now skip the rewrite and install normally, while 18.04+ keeps the mirror fallback. ### Additional Notes Test-only change (E2E test setup); no Agent runtime behavior is affected, so no release note is added. The change is scoped to the DDOT suite plus the shared apt-mirror helper; extending the same hardening to the other `new-e2e-agent-platform-*` suites (install-script, step-by-step, upgrade) is intentionally left as a follow-up. --- PR by Bits - [View session in Datadog](https://app.datadoghq.com/code/1dd901d3-691c-4fc8-ac44-10e6da9179e0) Comment @datadog to request changes

signals.title: Add WithLevel option to metricslogs LogMetrics
signals.text: ## What this change does This is a follow-up to #55182. Adding a `WithLevel` option to `LogMetrics`. The caller can now pick which local log level a batch writes at. ## Why we need this change By default, `LogMetrics` writes at Debug level. Some callers want a quieter option than agent-wide Debug. This change lets a caller ask for Trace level instead, one call at a time. ## How the component behaves `LogMetrics` keeps its existing signature and default behavior. It gains a variadic `opts ...Option` parameter. - No options: the call writes at Debug level, same as before. - `WithLevel(LevelTrace)`: the call writes at Trace level instead. ## How this was tested - Unit tests cover both levels: the default (Debug), and an explicit `WithLevel(LevelTrace)` call. - The full agent binary was built with this change. The build was successful. - The Go linter was run on the new code. The linter found no issues.

signals.title: fix(e2e-framework): stop leaking Windows VM admin password in test logs
signals.text: ## Summary - The Windows admin password generated for AWS/Azure e2e VMs used `random.NewRandomString` (not marked secret by the Pulumi provider), and `pulumi_provisioner.go` unconditionally logged the raw marshalled stack outputs — so the password was printed in plain text in e2e test logs. - Mark the password as a real Pulumi secret at both generation sites (`pulumi.ToSecret(...)`), and make the provisioner's log line redact any output flagged secret while still returning the real value via `RawResources` for in-process use (SSH connection, `RemoteHost.Password`). - Adds `test/new-e2e/examples/vm_win_test.go`, a Windows variant of the existing `vm_test.go` example, used to reproduce and verify the leak. Verified manually against a live AWS stack: `dd-Host-aws-vm` now logs as `[secret value redacted from logs]` instead of the plaintext password JSON, the test still passes end-to-end, and `dda inv aws.rdp-vm` (via `pulumi stack output --json --show-secrets`) still retrieves the real password. ## Test plan - [x] `go build ./...` in `test/e2e-framework` - [x] `go test ./testing/provisioners/...` (new `TestDumpRawResourcesRedactsSecrets` passes) - [x] `dda inv new-e2e-tests.run --targets=./test/new-e2e/examples --run TestVMWindowsSuite` — passes, log no longer contains the password - [x] Confirmed `pulumi stack output --json --show-secrets` still returns the real password for a live stack (used by `dda inv aws.rdp-vm`) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Mute flaky TestEC2VMWKitDirectSuite (NPM Windows)
signals.text: <!-- dd-meta {"pullId":"1b0dd00a-544a-4014-91c8-b161fd29d782","source":"chat","resourceId":"4e51c89b-d268-469a-a871-53e7be5d177b","workflowId":"39b8eba4-963e-430b-a676-26f2455715a6","codeChangeId":"39b8eba4-963e-430b-a676-26f2455715a6","sourceType":"slack"} --> ### What does this PR do? Marks the new-e2e suite `TestEC2VMWKitDirectSuite` (`test/new-e2e/tests/npm`) as flaky in `flakes.yaml`, referencing incident 59580. ### Motivation The `new-e2e-npm-packages-windows` job has been failing intermittently on `main` (~8 errors / 11 successes since it was introduced), blocking the pipeline and driving incident #59580. Root cause: the suite was added on 2026-08-21 in PR #52410 ("add support for CNM direct send to windows"). Its `Test00FakeIntakeNPM_HostRequests` assertion (`common_1host.go:91`) locks onto the first-seen hostname and requires at least 5 CollectorConnections payloads (30s cadence, ~150s) within a 150s window. On Windows EC2, the VM hostname changes mid-run (rename + reboot → system-probe restart → new cached hostname), so payloads split across two hostname/networkID keys. The first-seen hostname then freezes (e.g. at 2 payloads) and the test fails with "not enough payloads". Test is [flaky](https://app.datadoghq.com/ci/ci-cd/explorer?query=test_level%3Atest%20%40test.name%3ATestEC2VMWKitDirectSuite%2A%20-%40test.status%3Apass&agg_m=count&agg_m_source=base&agg_t=count&ci_cd_explorer_tab=tests&citest_explorer_sort=%40duration%2Cdesc&cols=timestamp%2C%40test.status%2C%40test.name%3A209%2C%40test.suite%3A274%2C%40test.is_known_flaky%2C%40duration%2C%40test.service%2Cerror.type&currentTab=overview&eventStack=&fromUser=false&index=citest&refresh_mode=paused&start=1787229769000&end=1787403431000&paused=true) since they were created ### Describe how you validated your changes ### Additional Notes Tracking: https://app.datadoghq.com/incidents/59580. This is a temporary mitigation and should be reverted once the hostname-stability fix lands. --- PR by Bits - [View session in Datadog](https://app.datadoghq.com/code/4e51c89b-d268-469a-a871-53e7be5d177b) Comment @datadog to request changes

signals.title: APM: wire serverless span/payload modifiers into the V1 (idx) pipeline
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the V1 (idx) equivalents of the serverless span/payload modifier hooks and wires them into `Agent.ProcessV1`. This simplifies a future PR to enable v1 conversion by default and after successful testing/dogfooding all the old versions of these functions will be removed. ### Motivation The V1 processing path (`Agent.ProcessV1`, used when the `convert-traces` feature is enabled) had no equivalent of the serverless span discard filter, span modifier, or tracer payload modifier, we need these so we can use the v1 conversion path in serverless and eventually remove the old path entirely This is **split out of #53732** ("APM: Enable convert-traces feature by default (take 2)") to reduce the review burden there. #53732 keeps the actual default flip. **This PR is a noop if trace conversion is disabled** ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests were added for every new V1 code path (`agent_test.go` for `discardSpansV1` / `SpanModifierV1` / `TracerPayloadModifierV1` in `ProcessV1`, `span_modifer_test.go`, `tracer_payload_modifier_test.go`, `trace_test.go` for `filterSpanV1`, `span_modifier_test.go` for the Cloud Run Jobs V1 modifier). Ran locally: - `bazel build //pkg/trace/agent/... //pkg/serverless/trace/... //pkg/serverless/otlp/... //cmd/serverless-init/... //comp/trace/payload-modifier/... //comp/trace/agent/... //pkg/trace/payload/...` — success - `bazel test` on the same targets — 13 tests pass; `//pkg/serverless/otlp:otlp_test` (tagged `manual`) run explicitly — pass - `bazel run //:gazelle` on every changed directory and `bazel run //bazel/buildifier` — no remaining BUILD.bazel churn - `dda inv linter.go` on all changed Go packages — 0 issues ### Additional Notes

signals.title: feat(dogstatsd): guard CLI commands when ADP owns the socket
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a guard to all five DogStatsD diagnostic CLI commands (`dogstatsd-stats`, `dogstatsd-capture`, `dogstatsd-replay`, `dogstatsd top`, `dogstatsd dump-contexts`) that checks whether the Agent Data Plane is configured to handle DogStatsD traffic (`data_plane.enabled` + `data_plane.dogstatsd.enabled`, or the deprecated `DD_ADP_ENABLED` env var). If so, the command prints a clear error and exits instead of silently producing empty or misleading results. The guard for `dogstatsd top --path <file>` is intentionally placed inside the online-only branch (`if path == ""`) so that offline file analysis of a previously-generated context dump artifact is unaffected. **New files:** - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdcommon/check.go` — shared helper with `CheckDataPlaneOwnsDogstatsd()` and `ErrDataPlaneOwnsDogstatsd` - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdcommon/check_test.go` — table-driven tests covering: ADP enabled via config, data plane enabled but dogstatsd disabled, `use_dogstatsd=false` override, deprecated `DD_ADP_ENABLED` env var, and defaults - `test/new-e2e/tests/agent-subcommands/dogstatsdadpguard_nix_test.go` — e2e test verifying `dogstatsd-capture` fails with the expected error message when ADP owns the socket **Modified files:** - `comp/dogstatsd/config/config.go` — made `enabledDataPlane()` to `EnabledDataPlane()` (public) so the helper can call it - `comp/dogstatsd/config/config_test.go` — updated test to call the renamed public method - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsd/command.go` — guard in `topContexts` (online path only) and `dumpContexts` - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdcapture/command.go` — guard in `dogstatsdCapture` - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdstats/command.go` — guard in `requestDogstatsdStats` - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdreplay/command.go` — guard in `dogstatsdReplay` - Four `BUILD.bazel` files — added `dogstatsdcommon` dependency ### Motivation When ADP owns the DogStatsD socket, the Core Agent's DogStatsD pipeline is dormant — its IPC endpoints are still registered but operate on empty state. The five `agent dogstatsd*` commands would either error out with confusing messages (e.g. `dogstatsd-stats` returns a 400 "not enabled") or silently produce empty results (e.g. `dogstatsd top` writes a valid but zero-record context dump, `dogstatsd-capture` produces an empty `.dog` file). Users have no indication that they should be using `agent-data-plane` instead. [Jira: DADP-96](https://datadog.atlassian.net/browse/DADP-96) ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go build` — all 6 affected packages compile clean - `go vet` — no issues - `gofmt` — all files formatted - `go test -tags test` — all 6 packages pass (config truth table with 21 subtests, 4 existing command flag-parsing tests, 5 new guard tests) - Verified the `top --path` offline path is not blocked by the guard - E2e test `TestDogstatsdCaptureBlockedByADP` added under `test/new-e2e/tests/agent-subcommands/`

signals.title: comp/api: restrict IPC/CMD unix socket to dd-agent
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Restricts the IPC and CMD server Unix socket (`agent_ipc.socket`) on Linux: - `chmod 0770` (was default `0755`) - when the Core Agent runs as root, `chown` the socket to the `dd-agent` user/group when they exist This matches the precedent already set by the runtime security agent gRPC server (`pkg/security/utils/grpc/grpc.go`). ### Motivation Deploying the host profiler under a non-root UID fails with: ``` Error: failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '<https+unix://localhost>/config/v1/' ? ``` When the core agent runs as root in docker, it creates `agent_ipc.socket` as `root:root` with mode `0755`. Connecting to a Unix socket on Linux requires **write** permission, so a subagent running as `dd-agent` (e.g. the host profiler) cannot connect. Other agent sockets (statsd, apm, the runtime security agent) already lock down their permissions; the IPC/CMD socket did not. ### Describe how you validated your changes CI ### Additional notes Behavior matrix: | Agent runs as | `dd-agent` exists | Socket owner | Socket mode | Host profiler (dd-agent) can connect? | |---|---|---|---|---| | root | yes | `dd-agent:dd-agent` | `0770` | ✅ (group write) | | root | no | `root:root` | `0770` | ❌ (no dd-agent user — expected) | | dd-agent | — | `dd-agent:dd-agent` | `0770` | ✅ (owner) |

signals.title: fix(procmgr): anchor in-flight Stop RPCs to SCM shutdown budget
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Ensures Stop RPC child teardown respects the Windows SCM shutdown deadline when a service stop is in progress. - Adds `ShutdownBudget::prefer_service_stop()` / `refresh()` / `for_single_stop()` so RPC stops share the same SCM-anchored budget as ordered shutdown. - Adds `wait_graceful_or_shutdown()` to interrupt graceful stop waits on `shutdown_notify` (Windows). - Applies the budget in `wait_for_stop_since()` and consolidates Windows spawn-resource cleanup on stop. Follow-up to [Codex review on #54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731#discussion_r3831784217). ### Motivation When SCM stop arrives while the supervisor is handling a `Stop` RPC, `handle_command` stays blocked on `proc.stop()` and cannot poll the shutdown future. RPC stops used an unlimited `ShutdownBudget`, so a configured `stop_timeout` larger than the ~175s service budget could keep the service in `STOP_PENDING` past the SCM wait hint before ordered shutdown begins. With default `stop_timeout` (90s) this stays within budget; this closes the gap for large custom timeouts and for SCM stop arriving mid-RPC. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Added unit test `test_prefer_service_stop_without_signal_preserves_fallback` in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/shutdown.rs`. - Existing shutdown and process stop tests in `shutdown.rs` / `process.rs` cover the refactored paths (CI: `//pkg/procmgr/rust:dd-procmgrd_test`). ### Additional Notes - Windows-only behavior for SCM deadline and `shutdown_notify` interrupt; Unix is unchanged (`service_stop_signal_time()` is always `None`). - **Base branch:** `jose/procmgr-spawn-profiles` (stacked follow-up). Retarget to `main` after #54731 merges if preferred.

signals.title: fix(aggregator): `Stop` no longer leaves a goroutine running
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? `BufferedAggregator.Stop()` now sends its own reply channel on `stopChan` and waits for `run()` to close it, instead of returning as soon as `run()` picks up the stop signal. Also deflaked `TestDemuxFlushAggregatorToSerializer` by replacing a `time.Sleep(250ms)` guess with `assert.Eventually` on `IsInputQueueEmpty()`, which is both faster (10-run mean: ~360ms to ~110ms) and no longer a fixed-duration guess that could be too short on a loaded runner. ### Motivation [tests_macos_gitlab_amd64](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1971012934) panicked in `comp/netflow/topn` with: ``` panic: Log in goroutine after TestTopNScheduling has completed: 2026-08-20 22:37:36 GMT | INFO | (pkg/aggregator/aggregator.go:802 in run) | Stopping aggregator ``` `run()` kept logging and deregistering health after `Stop()` had already returned, so a leaked goroutine could still write through the global logger once a later test rebound it to its own `*testing.T`. Measured under `-race` with a temporary instrumented hook: - before this change, `run()` finished after `Stop()` returned in 500/500 samples (median 263us, p99 767us, max 1.18ms), - after this change, all 500 samples show `run()` completing strictly before `Stop()` unblocks. ### Describe how you validated your changes Ran `dda inv test --race` on `pkg/aggregator/...` and `comp/netflow/topn/...` (241 tests, all pass), confirming the added wait causes no deadlock. ### Additional Notes The delayed log line and `health.Deregister()` have **no production impact** on their own, since the demultiplexer's `flushLoop` already completes its final flush synchronously before `agg.Stop()` is called. The panic is specific to `comp/core/log/mock` binding the global logger to a `*testing.T` that can finish before a leaked goroutine's write. The stop signal uses a request/reply channel (`stopChan chan chan struct{}`), mirroring the `trigger`/`blockChan` pattern already used elsewhere in this file for flush requests.

signals.title: [Backport 7.82.x]  Fix DI proxy dropping when logs_enabled unset
signals.text: Backport 95ac563f4fda703e58a84722440fb9dff8676282 from #54228. ___ ### What does this PR do? Fixes the trace-agent Dynamic Instrumentation proxy so it only drops debugger data when the Logs product is explicitly disabled. Previously, an unset `logs_enabled` was treated the same as an explicit `false`, so DI snapshots were silently dropped. The proxy now forwards unless `logs_enabled` (or the deprecated `log_enabled`) is set to `false` and neither key enables logs, matching how the logs agent itself decides to start. ### Motivation Customers reported that DI snapshots were not reaching the intake even though they had not disabled the Logs product. `core.GetBool("logs_enabled")` returns `false` for both "unset" and "explicitly false", so the proxy dropped snapshots any time the setting was omitted. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests in `comp/trace/config/impl` cover the matrix: both keys unset, each key explicitly `false`, the override, and mixed configurations where one key enables logs while the other is `false`.

signals.title: [DBM][Oracle] Corrected default query timeout
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Changes the Oracle check default `query_timeout` from `20000` to `20` seconds. Updates the integration test to match. ### Motivation The Go Oracle integration treats `query_timeout` as seconds. The default of `20000` produced a ~5.5 hour timeout, not ~20 seconds. That can leave checks hung after DB maintenance or outages when customers rely on the default. This came up from SDBM-2909. ### Describe how you validated your changes Updated `TestTimeout` default expectation from `20000*time.Second` to `20*time.Second`. Oracle integration tests require `-tags oracle` and a live Oracle instance; not run locally in this environment. ### Additional Notes - `query_timeout` stays a hidden option (not in `conf.yaml.example`). - Only applies on the go-ora path, not godror / `oracle_client` / `tns_alias`. This is potentially an area of improvement for the future so that other drivers also use the timeout.

signals.title: feat(remoteagentregistry): add RemoteCommandProvider gRPC service and CLI surface
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds the gRPC and CLI infrastructure for proxying CLI commands through the Remote Agent Registry (RAR). This implements the Command Provider section of the [RFC: Future-proofing the RemoteAgentRegistry](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ARUN/pages/5262901901). **New gRPC service: `RemoteCommandProvider`** - Defined in `pkg/proto/datadog/remoteagent/command.proto` - `ListCommands`: discover commands exposed by registered remote agents - `ExecuteCommand`: route a command execution request to the right agent - Command tree structure with typed parameters (`ParameterType` enum) - Uses `google.protobuf.Struct` for typed argument passing - Unary RPCs (no streaming in this initial iteration) **RAR component changes:** - Added `ListCommands()` and `ExecuteCommand()` to the `Component` interface - Added `AgentCommands` struct to pair commands with their owning agent - Implemented `ListCommands` using the existing `callAgentsForService` fan-out pattern - Implemented `ExecuteCommand` with flavor-based routing and session validation - Added `CommandProviderServiceName` to the known services map - Wired `RemoteCommandProviderClient` into `remoteAgentClient` - Updated mock to satisfy the new interface **gRPC server changes:** - Registered `RemoteCommandProviderServer` on the core agent gRPC server - Added `remoteCommandProviderServer` with `ListCommands`/`ExecuteCommand` handlers **CLI changes:** - New `agent remote` subcommand that dynamically discovers subcommands at runtime - Uses `PersistentPreRunE` to query the agent and build the cobra tree at runtime - Recursively builds cobra commands from the protobuf `Command` tree - Registers typed flags from `CommandParameter` definitions - Includes `subagentNameMapping` for flavor-to-subcommand-name mapping (e.g. `agent_data_plane` -> `data-plane` to avoid stuttering) ### Motivation Customers should not need to interact with remote agent binaries (like `agent-data-plane`) directly. The RAR Command Provider allows the core agent to discover and proxy CLI commands exposed by registered subagents, so users always run `datadog-agent remote [agent] [command]` and the core agent routes transparently. This PR only adds the gRPC and CLI surface -- no remote agents implement `RemoteCommandProvider` yet, and no commands are registered. That work will follow in subsequent PRs (starting with ADP's dogstatsd diagnostic commands: `top`, `dump-contexts`, etc.). ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go build` succeeds for all modified and new packages - Proto generated with `protoc-gen-go` v1.36.12 and `protoc-gen-go-grpc` v1.6.2 (matching existing generated files) - Bazel `BUILD.bazel` updated for the new proto target ### Additional Notes Design decisions (aligned with the RFC): - `is_runnable` instead of the RFC's `run_e` field name - Unary RPCs (not streaming) for the initial iteration - `google.protobuf.Struct` for typed arguments (preserves type info) - Tree-structured commands with `children` for nested subcommands - Optional `agent_flavor` field on `ExecuteCommandRequest` for explicit routing - `subagentNameMapping` in the CLI to avoid subcommand name stuttering

signals.title: [CONTINT-5549] Retry if the external metrics server fails to start
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? signals.title: Add adaptive sampler COAT metrics
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? - Emits bounded adaptive-sampler configuration gauges when a sampler is instantiated: - adoption mode (adaptive sampling vs. detection-only) - global vs. per-source enablement and configuration origin - numeric setting buckets for max patterns, rate limit, burst size, match threshold, and tokenizer size - option categories for important-log protection, pattern hashes, and include/exclude rule types - smart-severity-profile and disabled-source usage - Adds a bounded bypass-reason counter and gives kept/pattern/protection counters a detection-only dimension. - Exports the configuration and operational metrics through the logs-and-metrics COAT profile. - Explicitly strips log_source from COAT and never records raw rule expressions, samples, source names, or exact numeric configuration values. ### Motivation We need to understand adaptive-sampling adoption across orgs, which configuration shapes are in use, and whether the sampler is dropping, projecting, protecting, or bypassing logs as expected. The bounded dimensions support cross-org product and operational decisions without exposing customer configuration content or creating per-source COAT cardinality. The maximum possible per-host contexts are bounded below the planned 128-context limit: - configuration_seen: 24 - numeric_config_seen: 120 - option_config_seen: 72 ### Describe how you validated your changes - dda inv test --targets=./pkg/logs/internal/decoder/preprocessor,./pkg/logs/internal/decoder,./comp/core/agenttelemetry/impl (1,203 tests passed) - bazel test //pkg/logs/internal/decoder:decoder_test //pkg/logs/internal/decoder/preprocessor:preprocessor_test //comp/core/agenttelemetry/impl:impl_test - dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/logs/internal/decoder,./pkg/logs/internal/decoder/preprocessor,./comp/core/agenttelemetry/impl (0 issues) - Added tests for bucket/filter classification, emitted configuration contexts, bounded bypass reasons, and the exact COAT metric/tag allowlist. ### Additional Notes This is a draft because the standard COAT follow-ups still need to be completed before merge: - file the ASUP governance/tracking ticket - validate the emitted payload on a dev VM and in ddcoat - update the Agent data-security public documentation - record the target Agent release and confirm availability after GA The local pre-push go-mod-tidy hook was skipped after it rewrote 50 unrelated dependency files on a clean checkout of current main; those changes were restored and are not part of this PR. signals.title: feat(serializer): add per-endpoint metric filter lists
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `metric_filterlist_endpoints`, a per-endpoint list of metric names to leave out of the payload built for that endpoint. It is keyed by the endpoint URL as configured under `dd_url` or `additional_endpoints`, and endpoints without an entry keep receiving every metric. Names are matched exactly. ```yaml metric_filterlist_endpoints: "https://app.datadoghq.com": - myapp.request.duration - myapp.cache.miss ``` A telemetry counter tagged by endpoint reports how many metrics each list left out. ### Motivation `metric_filterlist` is applied while metrics are sampled, so a filtered metric is removed from every destination. An Agent configured with `additional_endpoints` has no way to stop sending a metric to one endpoint while still sending it to the others, so the choice today is all destinations or none. That distinction matters when one Agent feeds two destinations with different needs, for example a primary intake alongside a secondary that only needs a subset of the metrics, or a cost sensitive destination next to one that keeps everything. The serializer is where this belongs, because it is the only stage that knows which destination a payload is being built for. `comp/filterlist` runs during ingestion, before any destination exists, so it cannot express a per-endpoint rule. Two per-destination filters already live in `buildPipelines` and are built the same way: `getFailoverAllowlist` for multi-region failover and `getAutoscalingFailoverMetrics` for autoscaling. This adds a third, `getEndpointFilterLists`, and attaches it to that destination's `PipelineConfig`. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/serializer`: 104 tests pass. New coverage for `ExcludeFilter` and its empty case, pipeline level tests for a filtered endpoint alongside an unfiltered one and for an entry naming an endpoint that is not configured, plus a test that sketches still honor the lists when series fall back to the v1 API. - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/serializer`: 0 issues. - `dda inv schema.lint`: both schemas pass. - `dda inv tidy` and `bazel run //:gazelle`: no module or BUILD changes. ### Additional Notes - Prefix matching is deliberately not applied. `metric_filterlist_match_prefix` is reset by Remote Config whenever it pushes a metric filter list, so honoring it would let an unrelated remote update silently change how these lists match. Remote Config matches exactly, so exact matching also keeps the two consistent. - The lists require `use_v2_api.series`, which is the default. The v1 series path builds a single payload and the forwarder copies it to every destination, so there is no point at which a per-endpoint filter could be applied; the Agent logs a warning if both are set. Sketches always honor the lists. - `ExcludeFilter` uses a map rather than `pkg/util/strings.Matcher`. That package is in the root module and `pkg/serializer` depends only on submodules, so importing it would add a root module dependency to a leaf. - Giving one endpoint its own filter means its payload is no longer shared with endpoints that have none, so that payload is built separately. It is the smaller of the two. - Follow-ups that are out of scope here: delivery through the Metric Control Remote Config product, and parity in the ADP metric pipeline.

signal.title: IMDS lookups retry every 15s forever when IMDS is unreachable from a container
signal.text: ### Agent version 7.78.1 ### Bug Report On EC2 instances with `HttpPutResponseHopLimit: 1` and `HttpTokens: required`, IMDS is unreachable from the agent when it runs in a container. The hop limit drops the IMDSv2 token response before it reaches the container, and IMDSv1 is refused, so no code path can succeed. `cloud_hostinfo` retries anyway, every 15s, indefinitely. Each attempt blocks a collector slot for ~600ms waiting on a socket, so roughly 4% of the time a collector slot is occupied doing nothing that can ever succeed. Please back the IMDS lookup off to 60s after repeated failures. ### Reproduction Steps 1. Run the agent in a container on an EC2 instance with `HttpPutResponseHopLimit: 1` and `HttpTokens: required`. 2. `agent status collector` — `cloud_hostinfo` shows ~600ms average execution time, indefinitely. 3. From inside the container, `curl -X PUT http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token -H 'X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60'` hangs until timeout, while `curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id` returns 401 in under 10ms. ### Other environment details Seen on EKS Auto Mode, whose nodes default to those metadata options, but nothing here is specific to it — any container on a hop-limited instance should reproduce.

signal.title: [ACTP] package and activate par-control
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Packages and activates split-mode PAR on Linux and Windows hosts: - installs `par-control` and process-manager definitions for it and the on-demand executor; - adds Agent package, installer, and Windows executable-resource wiring; - preserves a standard Unix service `PATH` for process-manager children; - adds fake-OPMS support plus Linux and Windows lifecycle/bootstrap E2E suites and CI jobs. Two details about how the definitions delegate to `dd-procmgrd`: - Windows has no console for a service to inherit, so the `par-control` definition redirects `stdout`/`stderr` to `<ETC_ROOT>/logs/par-control.log` instead of the binary managing its own log file. `dd-procmgrd` now creates a missing stdio parent directory rather than silently falling back to inherit on a fresh install. - The PAR definitions set `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR=${DD_CONF_DIR}/managed/datadog-agent/stable`, which `dd-procmgrd` expands from the supervising unit, so a stable or experiment unit selects the matching config tree. Hardcoding the rendered stable path would have made the control plane and executor read stable policies during an experiment while the core Agent read the experiment's. This matches what the DDOT definition already does. Windows keeps reading `fleet_policies_dir` from the registry, as `pkg/config/setup/config_windows.go` does, because there are no experiment services there. Docker and Kubernetes deployments remain monolithic. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages:packages_test //pkg/fleet/installer/packages/embedded:tmpl_test //pkg/procmgr/rust:dd-procmgrd_test` - `dda inv linter.go --module=test/new-e2e --targets=./tests/privateactionrunner` The installer test now pins the full `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR` value for both definitions; asserting only the key name would not catch a regression to a hardcoded path. Live Linux and Windows E2E execution is left to CI. _Stack 9 of 9; based on #54594._

signal.title: [ACTP] orchestrate par-control tasks
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the production `par-control` orchestration loop. It dequeues tasks with bounded concurrency, starts the executor on demand, synchronizes signing keys, dispatches actions, and publishes outcomes. Executor idle shutdown is self-owned by the Go executor rather than driven by `par-control` process-manager calls. Task heartbeats run from dequeue through cold start, execution, and terminal publication. Runner health checks are independent of task flow, and shutdown drains in-flight work without calling `dd-procmgrd` from the shutdown path. ### Validation - `dda env dev run -- bazel test //pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control:par-control_test` - `dda env dev run -- env -u PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR cargo clippy --manifest-path pkg/privateactionrunner/par-control/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` _Stack 7 of 9; based on #54592 and followed by #54594._

signal.title: feat(softinv): report the OS and OEM kernel-mode drivers
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Extends the software inventory beyond installed applications with two new software types, `os` and `driver`: | Platform | Type | Source | |---|---|---| | Windows | `driver` | `Win32_SystemDriver`, plus `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` joined against `Win32_PnPEntity` | | Windows | `os` | `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion` | | macOS | `os` | `/System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist` | **Operating system.** One entry whose version advances, rather than one entry per update. An update is an event, not an installed item whose version moves, so it would produce a permanently static entry — and the host SBOM already carries installed KBs. Name and product code are constant, because the backend keys an item on name + product code with the version excluded; anything version-derived in either field would make an upgrade read as remove + install. The version carries the full patch level: `10.0.26100.4652` on Windows including the UBR, `15.6 (24G84)` on macOS including the build that supplemental updates and RSRs advance. **Drivers.** Only OEM and third-party drivers are reported; the drivers that ship with Windows are excluded. Two sources, because each sees what the other cannot. `Win32_SystemDriver` covers drivers registered as kernel services, including software-only ones — EDR minifilters, network and DLP filters — that have no PnP device node. The class carries no version or vendor, so both come from the version resource of the image path; only the numeric `VS_FIXEDFILEINFO` version is accepted, since the `FileVersion` string is routinely decorated or comma-separated. Image paths are normalized (`\??\`, `\SystemRoot\`, `%SystemRoot%`, relative) and MUI display names (`@<dll>,-<id>`) resolved with `SHLoadIndirectString`. Filtered on the binary's `CompanyName`, the only vendor signal the class offers; an absent `CompanyName` is kept, since an unattributed kernel driver is worth seeing. Identity is the service name, which Windows guarantees unique. `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` covers packages bound to a device that register no kernel service of their own, which the first source cannot see. Selected by the INF being published as `oemNN.inf` — `Manufacturer` is not used, because Microsoft's inbox INFs report generic strings such as `(Standard system devices)` and Windows also ships inbox INFs authored by hardware vendors, so filtering on it would keep hundreds of inbox drivers. One `Win32_PnPEntity` query is joined in memory to skip devices that already have a service; a query per device would spend the entire time budget on the join. Identity is the device name, the field the class offers that survives a driver update. Known limitations: UMDF user-mode drivers register no kernel service, and a driver whose service entry is created, loaded, then deleted is invisible. This is an inventory of registered drivers, not of code currently in the kernel. **Deadline.** Each collector is bounded at 90s in the shared snapshot runner. A timeout is fatal, because a timed-out enumeration is an unknown state and a missing row reads downstream as a removal; zero rows is still a valid result. A hung native call cannot be cancelled — the WMI library takes no context — so a collector that misses its deadline is not started again until it returns. ### Motivation The inventory only covered installed applications, leaving OS patch level and kernel drivers invisible — two of the most useful signals for fleet visibility and compliance. The deadline is a prerequisite rather than a nicety: these sources can block, and a single slow `Collect()` previously stalled the whole snapshot with no upper bound. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Windows unit tests run and pass in CI (`tests_windows-x64`); macOS unit tests pass locally; `bazel test //pkg/inventory/software:software_test` passes. - `dda inv linter.go` clean, and clean again under `GOOS=windows`, which type-checks the Windows-tagged files and their tests. - Coverage: deadline and in-flight behaviour, both driver filters, the PnP/service join including case mismatch and devices missing from `Win32_PnPEntity`, path normalization and MUI resolution, the numeric-version requirement, identity stability across a version bump for both driver sources, and entry-ID uniqueness once the new families merge with application entries. - Real-host integration tests compare collected drivers against the `Services` registry key, assert nothing Microsoft-published survives the service filter, and log the OEM/inbox split per source; the macOS one asserts the running version against `sw_vers -productVersion`. - Driver payloads from a real Windows host were inspected end to end. That caught two drivers reporting an unresolved MUI reference as their name, fixed in 2741b66. ### Additional Notes - A fatal error from any single collector still drops the whole snapshot (existing behaviour). - PnP-sourced entries carry no `install_paths`, because `Win32_PnPSignedDriver` names no binary. - Enable with `software_inventory.enabled: true`, which drives both the system-probe module and the core agent component. No status or flare changes were needed, since `populateStatus` already groups by `Source`. - Worst-case snapshot duration is bounded per collector, not globally, so it scales with collector count. A snapshot-wide ceiling would be a separate change.

signal.title: [DBM][Oracle] Corrected default query timeout
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Changes the Oracle check default `query_timeout` from `20000` to `20` seconds. Updates the integration test to match. ### Motivation The Go Oracle integration treats `query_timeout` as seconds. The default of `20000` produced a ~5.5 hour timeout, not ~20 seconds. That can leave checks hung after DB maintenance or outages when customers rely on the default. This came up from SDBM-2909. ### Describe how you validated your changes Updated `TestTimeout` default expectation from `20000*time.Second` to `20*time.Second`. Oracle integration tests require `-tags oracle` and a live Oracle instance; not run locally in this environment. ### Additional Notes - `query_timeout` stays a hidden option (not in `conf.yaml.example`). - Only applies on the go-ora path, not godror / `oracle_client` / `tns_alias`. This is potentially an area of improvement for the future so that other drivers also use the timeout.
