signal.title: feat(serializer): add per-endpoint metric filter lists
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `metric_filterlist_endpoints`, a per-endpoint list of metric names to leave out of the payload built for that endpoint. It is keyed by the endpoint URL as configured under `dd_url` or `additional_endpoints`, and endpoints without an entry keep receiving every metric. Names are matched exactly. ```yaml metric_filterlist_endpoints: "https://app.datadoghq.com": - myapp.request.duration - myapp.cache.miss ``` A telemetry counter tagged by endpoint reports how many metrics each list left out. ### Motivation `metric_filterlist` is applied while metrics are sampled, so a filtered metric is removed from every destination. An Agent configured with `additional_endpoints` has no way to stop sending a metric to one endpoint while still sending it to the others, so the choice today is all destinations or none. That distinction matters when one Agent feeds two destinations with different needs, for example a primary intake alongside a secondary that only needs a subset of the metrics, or a cost sensitive destination next to one that keeps everything. The serializer is where this belongs, because it is the only stage that knows which destination a payload is being built for. `comp/filterlist` runs during ingestion, before any destination exists, so it cannot express a per-endpoint rule. Two per-destination filters already live in `buildPipelines` and are built the same way: `getFailoverAllowlist` for multi-region failover and `getAutoscalingFailoverMetrics` for autoscaling. This adds a third, `getEndpointFilterLists`, and attaches it to that destination's `PipelineConfig`. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/serializer`: 104 tests pass. New coverage for `ExcludeFilter` and its empty case, pipeline level tests for a filtered endpoint alongside an unfiltered one and for an entry naming an endpoint that is not configured, plus a test that sketches still honor the lists when series fall back to the v1 API. - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/serializer`: 0 issues. - `dda inv schema.lint`: both schemas pass. - `dda inv tidy` and `bazel run //:gazelle`: no module or BUILD changes. ### Additional Notes - Prefix matching is deliberately not applied. `metric_filterlist_match_prefix` is reset by Remote Config whenever it pushes a metric filter list, so honoring it would let an unrelated remote update silently change how these lists match. Remote Config matches exactly, so exact matching also keeps the two consistent. - The lists require `use_v2_api.series`, which is the default. The v1 series path builds a single payload and the forwarder copies it to every destination, so there is no point at which a per-endpoint filter could be applied; the Agent logs a warning if both are set. Sketches always honor the lists. - `ExcludeFilter` uses a map rather than `pkg/util/strings.Matcher`. That package is in the root module and `pkg/serializer` depends only on submodules, so importing it would add a root module dependency to a leaf. - Giving one endpoint its own filter means its payload is no longer shared with endpoints that have none, so that payload is built separately. It is the smaller of the two. - Follow-ups that are out of scope here: delivery through the Metric Control Remote Config product, and parity in the ADP metric pipeline.
signal.author: jhoenzsch

signal.title: fix(network/tracer): fix data race on conntrackerTelemetry.lastRegisters
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on `conntrackerTelemetry.lastRegisters`: `Collect()` did a non-atomic read-modify-write on the package-level field, racing when two Prometheus Gather ticks overlapped. Switched `lastRegisters` to `atomic.Uint64` and use `Load`/`Store` in `Collect`. No behavior change — same subtraction, same package-level scope. ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes The race is eliminated by construction — `Load`/`Store` are atomic, so concurrent `Collect` calls can't race on `lastRegisters`.

signal.title: fix(tasks): ignore standalone files when checking pkg ownership
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Updates `directory_has_packages_without_owner` (used by the CODEOWNERS ownership linter) to skip standalone files directly under `/pkg` (e.g. `BUILD.bazel`), only checking directory entries. It now uses `os.scandir` instead of `os.listdir` to filter out non-directory entries, and builds paths with `pathlib.Path` (using `.as_posix()`) to keep path separators forward-slash on all platforms, including Windows. ### Motivation The linter was flagging root-level files like `/pkg/BUILD.bazel` as unowned "packages", which isn't correct — single files at the root of `/pkg` aren't standalone packages and shouldn't require a dedicated CODEOWNERS entry. This was causing a CI failure: https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/datadog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1971316454 ### Describe how you validated your changes Added/updated unit tests in `tasks/unit_tests/codeowner_linter_tests.py` covering the new behavior (root-level files under `/pkg` are ignored) and updated an existing test whose fixture relied on the old behavior. Ran the full `codeowner_linter_tests` and `linter_tests` suites (43 tests, all passing) and `ruff check`/`ruff format`.

signal.title: Harden ddot ubuntu e2e job against apt mirror 503
signal.text: <!-- dd-meta {"pullId":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000","source":"chat","resourceId":"1dd901d3-691c-4fc8-ac44-10e6da9179e0","workflowId":"92770bc9-1d63-478d-bfcc-a935837edd32","codeChangeId":"92770bc9-1d63-478d-bfcc-a935837edd32","sourceType":"slack"} --> ### What does this PR do? Two related changes to make the `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-{ubuntu,debian}-*` E2E jobs resilient to Ubuntu package-mirror outages: 1. **Wire `(*Host).ConfigureAptMirrors()` into the DDOT install suite** (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-platform/tests/ddot_install_test.go`), called from `SetupSuite` next to the existing `ConfigureYumMirrors()`. On Ubuntu it bounds apt's per-request timeout/retries and rewrites the apt sources to a `mirror+file` list so apt fails over to the global `archive.ubuntu.com` / `ports.ubuntu.com` mirrors when the regional EC2 mirror is unavailable. Both helpers no-op on the other's package manager. 2. **Guard the `mirror+file` source rewrite behind a method-driver check** in the shared helper (`test/new-e2e/tests/installer/host/host.go`). The `mirror+file` transport only exists in apt >= 1.6 (Ubuntu >= 18.04). On older releases (Ubuntu 16.04 ships apt 1.2) the method driver is absent, so rewriting the sources to `mirror+file:` makes every subsequent apt operation fail with `The method driver /usr/lib/apt/methods/mirror+file could not be found`. The helper now probes `test -e /usr/lib/apt/methods/mirror+file` and skips the source rewrite when it is missing; the Acquire retry/timeout hardening still applies on those hosts. ### Motivation The `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-ubuntu-a7-arm64` job flakes red on `main` (incident 59571). Its Ubuntu/Debian install path runs `apt-get update && apt-get install -y apt-transport-https curl gnupg` against a single regional EC2 Ubuntu mirror with no fallback and no bounded timeout; a `503`/slow mirror either fails fast or hangs to the 2h CI timeout. The apt-mirror resilience helper already existed and was used by the installer suites; a prior fix (#54987) added only the yum counterpart to the DDOT suite. Change 1 closes that gap. Change 2 fixes a regression that change 1 introduced: because the installer suites only run Ubuntu 24.04, the helper's `mirror+file` rewrite had never been exercised on old apt. The DDOT job runs Ubuntu 16.04, where the rewrite made `apt-get update` fail deterministically (job `1972006537`: only the `16-04` subtest failed with the `mirror+file` method-driver error; 18.04/20.04/22.04/24.04 passed). ### Changes - `test/new-e2e/tests/agent-platform/tests/ddot_install_test.go`: call `is.host.ConfigureAptMirrors()` in `SetupSuite`. - `test/new-e2e/tests/installer/host/host.go`: skip the Ubuntu `mirror+file` source rewrite when the `mirror+file` apt method driver is not present (apt < 1.6, e.g. Ubuntu 16.04); keep the Acquire timeout/retry hardening for all apt hosts. Doc comment updated. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Root-caused the failure on the PR pipeline (`new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-ubuntu-a7-x86_64`, job `1972006537`) from CI logs: the `16-04` subtest failed at `apt-get update` with `E: The method driver /usr/lib/apt/methods/mirror+file could not be found`, while the newer Ubuntu subtests in the same job passed — confirming the discriminator is the presence of the `mirror+file` method driver. - Confirmed the installer suites (`tests/installer/unix`, `tests/installer/script`) that already call `ConfigureAptMirrors()` only run Ubuntu 24.04, which is why the incompatibility was latent until now. - `gofmt` reports both files clean. - Type-safe: `h.remote.Execute` already returns `(string, error)` and is used identically in `host.New`; no new imports. - End-to-end validation is the DDOT jobs themselves once this runs in CI: the `16-04` subtest should now skip the rewrite and install normally, while 18.04+ keeps the mirror fallback. ### Additional Notes Test-only change (E2E test setup); no Agent runtime behavior is affected, so no release note is added. The change is scoped to the DDOT suite plus the shared apt-mirror helper; extending the same hardening to the other `new-e2e-agent-platform-*` suites (install-script, step-by-step, upgrade) is intentionally left as a follow-up. --- PR by Bits - [View session in Datadog](https://app.datadoghq.com/code/1dd901d3-691c-4fc8-ac44-10e6da9179e0) Comment @datadog to request changes

signal.title: Add adaptive sampler COAT metrics
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? - Emits bounded adaptive-sampler configuration gauges when a sampler is instantiated: - adoption mode (adaptive sampling vs. detection-only) - global vs. per-source enablement and configuration origin - numeric setting buckets for max patterns, rate limit, burst size, match threshold, and tokenizer size - option categories for important-log protection, pattern hashes, and include/exclude rule types - smart-severity-profile and disabled-source usage - Adds a bounded bypass-reason counter and gives kept/pattern/protection counters a detection-only dimension. - Exports the configuration and operational metrics through the logs-and-metrics COAT profile. - Explicitly strips log_source from COAT and never records raw rule expressions, samples, source names, or exact numeric configuration values. ### Motivation We need to understand adaptive-sampling adoption across orgs, which configuration shapes are in use, and whether the sampler is dropping, projecting, protecting, or bypassing logs as expected. The bounded dimensions support cross-org product and operational decisions without exposing customer configuration content or creating per-source COAT cardinality. The maximum possible per-host contexts are bounded below the planned 128-context limit: - configuration_seen: 24 - numeric_config_seen: 120 - option_config_seen: 72 ### Describe how you validated your changes - dda inv test --targets=./pkg/logs/internal/decoder/preprocessor,./pkg/logs/internal/decoder,./comp/core/agenttelemetry/impl (1,203 tests passed) - bazel test //pkg/logs/internal/decoder:decoder_test //pkg/logs/internal/decoder/preprocessor:preprocessor_test //comp/core/agenttelemetry/impl:impl_test - dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/logs/internal/decoder,./pkg/logs/internal/decoder/preprocessor,./comp/core/agenttelemetry/impl (0 issues) - Added tests for bucket/filter classification, emitted configuration contexts, bounded bypass reasons, and the exact COAT metric/tag allowlist. ### Additional Notes This is a draft because the standard COAT follow-ups still need to be completed before merge: - file the ASUP governance/tracking ticket - validate the emitted payload on a dev VM and in ddcoat - update the Agent data-security public documentation - record the target Agent release and confirm availability after GA The local pre-push go-mod-tidy hook was skipped after it rewrote 50 unrelated dependency files on a clean checkout of current main; those changes were restored and are not part of this PR. The remaining pre-push tests and linter passed.

Logger + `TextFormatter` is \~31% faster, with \~24% fewer allocations - Logger + `JSONFormatter` is \~21% faster, with \~10% fewer allocations `JSONFormatter` itself remains largely unchanged in runtime performance, with small allocation reductions. #### 🔄 `log/slog` interoperability v1.10 adds bidirectional interoperability between Logrus and Go's `log/slog`: - A Logrus `slog` hook can forward existing Logrus entries to an `slog` logger. - `hooks/slog.NewHandler` implements `slog.Handler`, allowing `log/slog` records to use an existing Logrus logger and its hooks, formatter, and output. - The handler preserves levels, fields, groups, context, record timestamps, and optionally caller information. - Caller reporting is configured per handler, without requiring Logrus's logger-wide `ReportCaller` option. - Custom `slog` levels can be mapped to Logrus levels. - The hook and handler can be combined, providing a practical path for incrementally migrating from Logrus to `log/slog` without requiring an all-at-once transition. This allows applications to migrate their logging API and logging backend independently: existing Logrus call sites can start using an `slog` backend, while new `slog` code can continue using an established Logrus setup. #### 🔒 Concurrency & Correctness - Fix reentrant logging deadlocks, including logging from within `MarshalJSON` or formatter code. - Fix generic `Log`, `Logf`, `Logln`, and `LogFn` methods unexpectedly panicking when called with `PanicLevel`, contrary to their documented behavior. - Eliminate race conditions in entry and formatter paths. - Improve locking boundaries around formatters and hooks. #### ➕ Added - `TextFormatter` now automatically enables colors on Windows terminals with ANSI support, matching behavior on other platforms. - `Entry.Caller` can now be set explicitly and is preserved across derived entries. When caller reporting is enabled, Logrus only detects and populates caller information when none was provided, allowing custom caller detection and wrapper-aware logging without adding additional caller configuration APIs. - Add minimal, composable logging interfaces for each log level, allowing consumers to depend on narrower interfaces and making logging implementations easier to substitute or adapt. - Expand CI verification to include TinyGo and every cross-compile target reported by go tool dist list, improving coverage across alternative toolchains and platforms. #### ⚠️ Behavioral Changes - Minimum supported Go version is now **1.23**. - `TextFormatter` now renders `[]byte` as raw/quoted strings instead of numeric slices. If you relied on the previous slice-of-ints output, convert explicitly before logging. - `TextFormatter` now uses dim cyan for debug output and dim white for trace output in colorized TTY output. - `Entry.HasCaller` is now deprecated in favor of checking `Entry.Caller` directly. A `//go:fix inline` directive was added so existing uses can be updated automatically. - `MutexWrap`, which was unintentionally exposed as public API, is deprecated. It remains available as an alias for compatibility but should not be used directly. *** v1.10 is primarily a performance, correctness, and interoperability release with no intentional breaking public signal.title: Publish datadog-fips-proxy to the pipeline testing repositories
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Publishes the released `datadog-fips-proxy` package into the testing repositories of the pipelines whose install-script tests need it, so the install script resolves it from the same repository as the Agent packages built by that pipeline. ### Motivation `test_install_script` triggers the `agent-linux-install-script` pipeline with `TESTING_APT_URL` and `TESTING_YUM_URL` so the install script installs the Agent built by the pipeline. Those variables land in the apt and yum configuration, so every Datadog package the script installs is resolved against the pipeline repository — including `datadog-fips-proxy`, which is released from another repository and is not published there. Nightly and RC pipelines failed with `Error: Unable to find a match: datadog-fips-proxy`. The mitigation was to stop forwarding those variables for the FIPS test, which leaves it installing the latest stable Agent instead of the pipeline's packages. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv linter.full-gitlab-ci` passes locally, including the configuration check across all nine pipeline contexts, which confirms the optional need resolves where the new job is absent. `shellcheck` with the repository's exclude list is clean on the job's expanded script. The `.pre` stage runs the same linter on this PR. The publish targets match what the child pipeline computes: `testing/pipeline-<id>-a7/7/x86_64/` for yum, and prefix `datadog-agent/pipeline-<id>-a7` with codename `stable-x86_64`, component `7` and architecture `amd64` for apt. Both pinned artifact URLs resolve, and the deb declares only `Recommends: datadog-signing-keys`, which `deploy_deb_testing-a7_x64` already uploads to the same repository. This PR changes the file the job's change rule watches, so the job runs on its own pipeline. From that run, with `<ID>` the pipeline id: ``` curl -fsI https://yumtesting.datad0g.com/testing/pipeline-<ID>-a7/7/x86_64/datadog-fips-proxy-1.1.29-1.x86_64.rpm curl -fsS https://apttesting.datad0g.com/datadog-agent/pipeline-<ID>-a7/dists/stable-x86_64/7/binary-amd64/Packages | grep -A4 'Package: datadog-fips-proxy' ``` Both indexes still list the Agent packages afterwards, and the RPM carries the testing signature rather than the production one. ### Additional Notes Publishing before the Agent uploads instead of after them fails safe. The arrangement assumes `rpm-s3` merges into existing metadata rather than replacing it, which is what it is built to do but is not verifiable outside CI. In this order, if that assumption is wrong the Agent job's pass drops `datadog-fips-proxy` from the index and the FIPS test behaves as it does today; in the reverse order it would drop the Agent packages and break every e2e test that consumes them. The ordering costs one thing: a failed download now blocks the two Agent testing uploads rather than only the install-script test. Making the job `allow_failure: true` would trade that for a silent index race.

signal.title: feat(dogstatsd): guard CLI commands when ADP owns the socket
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a guard to all five DogStatsD diagnostic CLI commands (`dogstatsd-stats`, `dogstatsd-capture`, `dogstatsd-replay`, `dogstatsd top`, `dogstatsd dump-contexts`) that checks whether the Agent Data Plane is configured to handle DogStatsD traffic (`data_plane.enabled` + `data_plane.dogstatsd.enabled`, or the deprecated `DD_ADP_ENABLED` env var). If so, the command prints a clear error and exits instead of silently producing empty or misleading results. The guard for `dogstatsd top --path <file>` is intentionally placed inside the online-only branch (`if path == ""`) so that offline file analysis of a previously-generated context dump artifact is unaffected. **New files:** - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdcommon/check.go` — shared helper with `CheckDataPlaneOwnsDogstatsd()` and `ErrDataPlaneOwnsDogstatsd` - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdcommon/check_test.go` — table-driven tests covering: ADP enabled via config, data plane enabled but dogstatsd disabled, `use_dogstatsd=false` override, deprecated `DD_ADP_ENABLED` env var, and defaults - `test/new-e2e/tests/agent-subcommands/dogstatsdadpguard_nix_test.go` — e2e test verifying `dogstatsd-capture` fails with the expected error message when ADP owns the socket **Modified files:** - `comp/dogstatsd/config/config.go` — made `enabledDataPlane()` to `EnabledDataPlane()` (public) so the helper can call it - `comp/dogstatsd/config/config_test.go` — updated test to call the renamed public method - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsd/command.go` — guard in `topContexts` (online path only) and `dumpContexts` - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdcapture/command.go` — guard in `dogstatsdCapture` - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdstats/command.go` — guard in `requestDogstatsdStats` - `cmd/agent/subcommands/dogstatsdreplay/command.go` — guard in `dogstatsdReplay` - Four `BUILD.bazel` files — added `dogstatsdcommon` dependency ### Motivation When ADP owns the DogStatsD socket, the Core Agent's DogStatsD pipeline is dormant — its IPC endpoints are still registered but operate on empty state. The five `agent dogstatsd*` commands would either error out with confusing messages (e.g. `dogstatsd-stats` returns a 400 "not enabled") or silently produce empty results (e.g. `dogstatsd top` writes a valid but zero-record context dump, `dogstatsd-capture` produces an empty `.dog` file). Users have no indication that they should be using `agent-data-plane` instead. [Jira: DADP-96](https://datadog.atlassian.net/browse/DADP-96) ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go build` — all 6 affected packages compile clean - `go vet` — no issues - `gofmt` — all files formatted - `go test -tags test` — all 6 packages pass (config truth table with 21 subtests, 4 existing command flag-parsing tests, 5 new guard tests) - Verified the `top --path` offline path is not blocked by the guard - E2e test `TestDogstatsdCaptureBlockedByADP` added under `test/new-e2e/tests/agent-subcommands/`

signal.title: otel-agent: support standalone DDOT without a datadog exporter
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? - Keeps `standaloneAgentFxOptions` in the fx graph in standalone mode (`DD_OTEL_STANDALONE=true`) even when no datadog exporter is configured, so a standalone DDOT can run with e.g. an OTLP-only exporter forwarding to a gateway collector. - Adds e2e coverage: a standalone otel-agent DaemonSet leaf (dogtel extension, OTLP exporter) forwarding traces/metrics/logs to a separate Helm-deployed gateway otel-agent, which ships them to fakeintake. Also verifies the dogtel liveness metric and tagger server on the leaf, and that neither side of the topology runs a core Datadog Agent pod. ### Motivation Today, `getDDExporterConfig` returns `ErrNoDDExporter` and previously prevented standalone DDOT from starting at all when the OTel Collector config has no `datadog` exporter block (e.g. a pure leaf-to-gateway OTLP topology). This PR allows that mode to run. Related: [OTAGENT-1083](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1083) **Note on API keys in this mode:** when there is no `datadog` exporter in the config, the sync from the OTel Collector's `exporters.datadog.api.key`/`.api.site` into the agent config (`cmd/otel-agent/config/agent_config.go`, `getDDExporterConfig`) never runs, since that code path returns early on `ErrNoDDExporter`. signal.title: [NTWK-812] Filter dynamic tests across all reverse-DNS names
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes Network Path dynamic tests incorrectly scheduling traceroutes to Datadog intake endpoints when a destination IP is associated with multiple DNS names. Previously, Network Path filtered only the first DNS name associated with an IP. Because DNS cache ordering is not deterministic, the default `*.datadoghq.com` exclusion could be missed when another name appeared first. This PR: - Passes every existing DNS name associated with a destination IP to Network Path. - Evaluates the ordered connection-filter chain against the connection as a whole. A rule matches when its domain pattern matches any associated name, or its IP condition matches; the last matching rule wins. - Uses the domain matched by the winning include rule as the path-test hostname. - Preserves Remote Config ID, name, and tags from the winning rule. - Keeps customer include rules able to override the built-in Datadog exclusions. This does not modify the shared reverse-DNS parser or cache, change CNM payload behavior, or add an AWS ELB-specific exclusion. ### Motivation [NTWK-812 / ZD 2972181](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/NTWK-812) A destination IP for a Datadog intake endpoint can be associated with both its `*.datadoghq.com` name and a CNAME target. Network Path previously collapsed that list to its first entry before filtering, making the result dependent on cache ordering. For the reporting organization, this represented approximately 37% of dynamic test runs—more than 3,000 unnecessary runs per day. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added unit coverage for: - Datadog and ELB names in either order. - An ELB name by itself receiving no special treatment. - Unrelated domains and customer-owned ELBs. - Customer include rules overriding built-in exclusions across aliases. - Last-match-wins behavior across different aliases. - Empty and partially empty DNS-name lists. - Hostname selection for local and Remote Config include rules. - Preservation of Remote Config ID, name, and tags. `gofmt` and diff whitespace validation pass. The focused local test command was blocked before compilation because Bazel could not download `gotestsum` from `proxy.golang.org`. CI validation is in progress following the merge from `main`. ### Additional Notes The filtering behavior remains ordered and last-match-wins, but each rule now evaluates all names associated with the connection instead of only one arbitrarily selected name.

signal.title: feat(otel-metrics): share SDK trace stats mapping
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a shared `tracestats` mapping to `opentelemetry-mapping-go`. It converts `traces.span.sdk.metrics.duration` delta histograms into transport-neutral APM trace stats for the Agent and public OTLP intake. ### Why? Using one mapping keeps tags, status handling, operation names, time windows, validation, and serialization consistent across both ingestion paths. ### Differences from the current dd-source implementation Compared with the current local mapper in dd-source, this implementation: - Uses a data point's `service.name` when present and applies Agent service-name normalization. - Emits lowercase span kinds and maps `datadog.is_trace_root`. - Accepts OTel error status code `2` and case-insensitive `ERROR` / `STATUS_CODE_ERROR` forms. - Converts named gRPC status values to their canonical numeric codes. - Maps `telemetry.sdk.language` to payload languages and structured `datadog.peer_tags` arrays to grouped stats peer tags. - Normalizes and sorts additional metric tags while excluding fields already mapped into grouped stats. - Skips only invalid data points and reports conversion errors instead of emitting buckets with missing sketches. - Keeps the existing `otlp-intake-metrics` source attribution instead of adding `otlp-intake-metrics-sdk` / `span_source:ddsdk_otlp`. - Owns the payload protobuf and serialization so the Agent and dd-source share the same wire contract. These behavioral fixes can be split into their own dd-source fix PR if reviewers prefer. Keeping them here makes it easier to test the complete, up-to-date mapping contract end to end across Agent and agentless intake without an intermediate mismatched state. ### Testing - Focused `tracestats` package passed with the race detector. - Focused lint passed with 0 issues. - [Staging collector test](https://dd.datad0g.com/apm/entity/service%3Ajava-sdkstats-collector-updated-20260821t1428z?dependencyMap.showNetworkMetrics=false&env=sdkstats-e2e&fromUser=true&groupMapByOperation=null&historicalData=true&operationName=internal&panels=qson%3A%28data%3A%28%29%2Cversion%3A%210%29&spanKind=internal&start=1787314370460&end=1787327226848&paused=true#resources): 120 requests produced 120 trace hits; the raw SDK histogram was absent. - [Staging agentless test](https://dd.datad0g.com/apm/entity/service%3Ajava-sdkstats-agentless-evp-20260821t1416z?dependencyMap.showNetworkMetrics=false&env=%2A&fromUser=false&operationName=internal&panels=qson%3A%28data%3A%28%29%2Cversion%3A%210%29&refresh_mode=sliding&spanKind=internal&start=1787244191834&end=1787330591834&paused=false#traces): 120 requests produced 120 trace hits.

signal.title: [procmgr] Config gates for processes.d auto-start
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds **config gates** to dd-procmgr so `processes.d` definitions can use `condition_config_any` to auto-start only when Agent config says they should. Implementation mirrors the Windows legacy SCM startup checks in `dependent_services_windows.go` and Agent config resolution: - YAML lookup via saphyr (case-insensitive keys, flattened dotted keys, merge keys, permissive parse fallback) - Go yaml.v2 parity for gate file loading: first document only in multi-doc streams; YAML 1.1 bool/int/float coercion on plain untagged scalars; quoted or explicitly tagged scalars use ParseBool only - Environment bindings (`DD_*`) with Agent precedence (ignore empty values, no trim before `ParseBool`, legacy `process_config.enabled` transforms) - Fleet policy merge - Derived `system_probe_config.enabled` (USM/NPM/security knobs, sk-tracer and discovery adjustments, end-user-device infrastructure mode overrides) - Windows: read `DD_*` overrides from the core Agent SCM `Environment` registry when not set in the procmgr process env Wires gate evaluation into `ManagedProcess` auto-start and on-failure restart paths (not config reload; that lands in #55080). **Stack context:** PR 2. Builds on [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) (`jose/procmgr-spawn-profiles`), which already includes list/describe ([#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568)). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI (includes #53568) | | 2 | This PR | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | ### Motivation Moving subservices (starting with process-agent) to dd-procmgr requires the supervisor to apply the same start/stop rules as the Agent today. Without config gates, a `processes.d` entry would always spawn when registered, which breaks parity with legacy SCM and fleet policy. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/` (env bindings, YAML load, system-probe derivations) - Integration tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate.rs` (process_config transforms, fleet/EUD overrides, multi-document YAML streams, Go yaml.v2 scalar parity) - `may_auto_start` / `condition_config_any` wiring tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/process.rs` - Windows procmgr Rust build, rustfmt, clippy, and tests in CI ### Additional Notes - No `ENC[...]` / secret backend resolution in this PR (fleet policy `ENC[...]` values are not resolved here either). - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Schema comment sync in `pkg/config/schema/yaml/process_config.yaml` and `core_schema.yaml` for env binding documentation. - Sync comments in `pkg/system-probe/config/` so procmgr gate derivations stay aligned with Go `adjust*` / module enablement logic. - Restores sketch v3beta shadow schema defaults accidentally renamed during the config-gates split. - Linux `DD_FLEET_POLICIES_DIR` for the procmgr systemd unit is deferred to #54168 and a follow-up unit-env change.

signal.title: feat(remoteagentregistry): add RemoteCommandProvider gRPC service and CLI surface
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds the gRPC and CLI infrastructure for proxying CLI commands through the Remote Agent Registry (RAR). This implements the Command Provider section of the [RFC: Future-proofing the RemoteAgentRegistry](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ARUN/pages/5262901901). **New gRPC service: `RemoteCommandProvider`** - Defined in `pkg/proto/datadog/remoteagent/command.proto` - `ListCommands`: discover commands exposed by registered remote agents - `ExecuteCommand`: route a command execution request to the right agent - Command tree structure with typed parameters (`ParameterType` enum) - Uses `google.protobuf.Struct` for typed argument passing - Unary RPCs (no streaming in this initial iteration) **RAR component changes:** - Added `ListCommands()` and `ExecuteCommand()` to the `Component` interface - Added `AgentCommands` struct to pair commands with their owning agent - Implemented `ListCommands` using the existing `callAgentsForService` fan-out pattern - Implemented `ExecuteCommand` with flavor-based routing and session validation - Added `CommandProviderServiceName` to the known services map - Wired `RemoteCommandProviderClient` into `remoteAgentClient` - Updated mock to satisfy the new interface **gRPC server changes:** - Registered `RemoteCommandProviderServer` on the core agent gRPC server - Added `remoteCommandProviderServer` with `ListCommands`/`ExecuteCommand` handlers **CLI changes:** - New `agent remote` subcommand that dynamically discovers subcommands at runtime - Uses `PersistentPreRunE` to query the agent and build the cobra tree at runtime - Recursively builds cobra commands from the protobuf `Command` tree - Registers typed flags from `CommandParameter` definitions - Includes `subagentNameMapping` for flavor-to-subcommand-name mapping (e.g. `agent_data_plane` -> `data-plane` to avoid stuttering) ### Motivation Customers should not need to interact with remote agent binaries (like `agent-data-plane`) directly. The RAR Command Provider allows the core agent to discover and proxy CLI commands exposed by registered subagents, so users always run `datadog-agent remote [agent] [command]` and the core agent routes transparently. This PR only adds the gRPC and CLI surface -- no remote agents implement `RemoteCommandProvider` yet, and no commands are registered. That work will follow in subsequent PRs (starting with ADP's dogstatsd diagnostic commands: `top`, `dump-contexts`, etc.). ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go build` succeeds for all modified and new packages - Proto generated with `protoc-gen-go` v1.36.12 and `protoc-gen-go-grpc` v1.6.2 (matching existing generated files) - Bazel `BUILD.bazel` updated for the new proto target ### Additional Notes Design decisions (aligned with the RFC): - `is_runnable` instead of the RFC's `run_e` field name - Unary RPCs (not streaming) for the initial iteration - `google.protobuf.Struct` for typed arguments (preserves type info) - Tree-structured commands with `children` for nested subcommands - Optional `agent_flavor` field on `ExecuteCommandRequest` for explicit routing - `subagentNameMapping` in the CLI to avoid subcommand name stuttering

signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Removes a redundant `agent.stop()` call from the test cleanup that caused a double-stop penalty, reducing `TestAgentTestSuite` from 41s to 5s and `TestRestartTestSuite` from 70s to 63s. ### Motivation The cleanup registered by `createAgent` and the explicit `agent.stop()` calls in test methods both invoked `stopComponents`, which blocked for 5s each on non-idempotent component `Stop()` methods (e.g. `fileLauncher.Stop()` blocks on an unbuffered channel when `Start()` was never called). Removing the redundant cleanup eliminates the double-stop. ### Describe how you validated your changes Both test suites were run in full (no cache) before and after the change to confirm all tests still pass and measure the speedup. ### Additional Notes All changes are test-only; no non-test code was modified.

signal.title: [procmgr] Windows spawn profiles foundation
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Introduces **Windows spawn profiles** in dd-procmgr so managed children can run under different security contexts: - **Privileged**: spawn as LocalSystem (supervisor primary token) - **AgentUser**: spawn as the agent service account (`ddagentuser`) Adds the Windows spawn stack (token logon, user profile load, supervision job, suspended `CreateProcessAsUserW`), a **privileged spawn catalog** that rejects unexpected command/args/env for privileged children, and **gRPC named-pipe caller authentication** (admin for mutating RPCs; agent-profile children may read but not Start/Stop other catalog entries). Separates **spawn credential resolution** from installer identity: - **`AgentAccount`**: who the Agent was installed as (registry, LSA, gMSA classification) - **`SpawnCredential`**: how `CreateProcessAsUserW` obtains its primary token (`InheritSupervisor` vs `Logon`) Privileged spawn verifies the duplicated supervisor token is LocalSystem before proceeding (guards console/dev fallback). Also refactors the daemon runtime into a **`Supervisor` event loop** plus `ProcessManager` handlers, and runs **dd-procmgr-service as LocalSystem** so agent-profile spawn can read the agent password from LSA. Includes **list/describe spawn identity** from [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568): `profile`, `user`, and `runtime_user` in the proto, API, and `dd-procmgr` CLI. **Stack context (PR 1):** | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | This PR | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI + list/describe (#53568) | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | [#54734](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54734) | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload | **Explicitly deferred:** config gates (#54732), secret-backend cache invalidation (#54734), process-agent dual-mode (#54735), full `ReloadConfig` (#55080). RPC/CLI for reload stay in this PR but return `UNIMPLEMENTED` until #55080. ### Motivation Process-agent on Windows must run as LocalSystem; other agent children should stay on the agent user. Spawn profiles make that explicit and enforceable at spawn time, and are a prerequisite for moving process-agent supervision off legacy SCM in #54735. LocalSystem MSI lands here so agent-profile children (ADP, PAR, DDOT) can spawn without waiting for #54735. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Bazel/Cargo procmgr Rust unit tests (Linux + Windows CI), including `SpawnCredential` resolution tests and cfg(test) harness that duplicates the supervisor token on non-LocalSystem runners (no registry/LSA in unit tests) - Privileged spawn catalog and spawn-profile unit tests (`pkg/procmgr/rust/...`) - COAT package tests (`pkg/procmgr/coat/...`) - Windows new-e2e (`test/new-e2e/tests/agent-runtimes/procmgr/`): - ADP running, restart, describe, and COAT telemetry - Spawn identity: procmgr service as LocalSystem, agent-profile children as installer user, userprofile env, admin Create pipe auth - Linux new-e2e: shared CLI tests plus DDOT running, restart, and describe (`procmgr_nix_test.go`) - PAR Windows E2E is unchanged on `main` (`par_procmgr_win_test.go`, not part of this diff) ### Additional Notes - **List/describe:** [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) was merged into this branch; release note ships here. - **Env expansion:** Restores optional `${VAR}` / `try_expand_env_vars` from [#54168](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54168) (lost during rebase). - **Fleet:** DDOT extension uninstall uses `ReloadOrRestartProcmgr()` (reload stub → SCM restart fallback). No process-agent dual-mode changes in this PR. - **ReloadConfig:** Proto and `dd-procmgr reload` remain for API compatibility; handler returns `UNIMPLEMENTED` until [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080). - **Windows DDOT E2E:** Reload-after-yaml tests removed from this PR (reload is deferred to #55080). Linux DDOT smoke tests remain. - **MSI:** After switching `dd-procmgr-service` to LocalSystem, restore **Manual** start type on upgrade so hosts left Disabled by older installers recover ([#55130](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55130) context). - **Shutdown:** `ShutdownBudget` is anchored to the SCM stop signal so ordered teardown shares the service control wait window. - **SpawnCredential:** Production registry/LSA/gMSA resolution is `#[cfg(not(test))]` so Bazel Clippy on `rust_test` targets does not treat it as dead code. - Supersedes the spawn portion of [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249).

signal.title: [procmgr] Secret backend resolution for config gates
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Resolves `ENC[...]` values during config gate evaluation so dd-procmgr matches Agent secret handling. Adds: - `config_gate/secrets.rs`: resolve handles via `secret_backend_command`, native `secret_backend_type`, and `multi_secret_backends` (same precedence as the core Agent) - Platform secret backend runners (Windows `CreateProcessAsUserW` under the Agent account; Unix setuid when procmgr runs as root for Privileged children) - `secret_backend_exec.rs`: shared spawn, timeout, concurrent stdout drain, process-group termination, and bounded reader join - Executable permission checks before spawn: Windows DACL validation (`secret_backend_rights.rs`) and Unix mode-bit checks (mirrors `filesystem.CheckRights`, honors `secret_backend_command_allow_group_exec_perm`) - Fail closed on unresolved pre-fleet secrets: env and base YAML `ENC[...]` resolution errors block config gates instead of falling through to lower-priority sources - Reject empty secret backend response values (Agent parity with `fetch_secret.go`) - Unix privilege drop: `initgroups` for the agent service user before `setgid`/`setuid` when dropping from root - Agent config precedence for backend settings: `DD_SECRET_BACKEND_*` env (including core Agent SCM `Environment` on Windows) over `datadog.yaml` - `clear_secret_caches()` helper exported for the reload PR; not wired to manager reload here Fleet policy `ENC[...]` values stay unresolved here, matching Agent `MergeFleetPolicy` running after secret resolution. **Stack context:** PR 3. Builds on [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) (`jose/procmgr-config-gates`). | # | PR | Notes | |---|-----|--------| | 1 | [#54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731) | spawn profiles + LocalSystem MSI | | 2 | [#54732](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54732) | config gates | | 3 | This PR | secret backend | | 4 | [#54735](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54735) | process-agent dual-mode | | 5 | [#53568](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53568) | list/describe (merged) | | 6 | [#55080](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/55080) | reload (calls `clear_secret_caches`) | ### Motivation PR 2 config gates read YAML, env, and fleet policy, but many customers gate features with secret-backed settings (`ENC[api_key]`, secret-backed booleans, etc.). Without secret resolution, gates would mis-evaluate and auto-start behavior would diverge from the Agent. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Rust unit tests in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/config_gate/secrets.rs` and config gate integration tests (serialized env to avoid cross-test leakage) - Coverage for fail-closed unresolved ENC, empty backend values, fleet ENC left unresolved, and secret-backed env/YAML gate paths - Windows procmgr Rust build/tests in CI - Linux CI: secret-backend tests run under the agent service user where required ### Additional Notes - Secret backends always run as the core Agent service account, not as the procmgr supervisor (LocalSystem) or a Privileged managed child. - No agent startup, fleet installer, or legacy SCM suppression changes in this PR. - Invokes `secret-generic-connector` when no custom `secret_backend_command` is configured. - Addresses Codex and Autotest review feedback from the initial PR iteration (fail-closed ENC, process groups, Unix groups/ACL, empty values).

signal.title: feat(notableevents): add macOS shutdown-cause notable event
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a macOS notable event that reports **why the previous boot ended**, recovered after the fact from the PMU rather than observed live. On Apple silicon, PMU/PMIC driver services publish an `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` IORegistry property: an array of short ASCII tokens naming the fault conditions that preceded the last power-off. This PR reads that property, classifies the tokens, and emits one notable event per boot when the classification is a fault. Five fault classes are covered, spanning the whole dictionary of 80 known tokens — 59 of which are faults: | Class | Title | Tokens | Example families | | ---------- | ------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------- | | `thermal` | macOS overheated shutdown | 14 | `ot`, `sochot`, `ntc_shdn` | | `power` | macOS power fault shutdown | 29 | `uv`, `ov`, `oc`, `buck`, `pgood` | | `crash` | macOS crash shutdown | 6 | `crash` | | `watchdog` | macOS watchdog timeout shutdown | 5 | `timeout` | | `hardware` | macOS hardware fault shutdown | 5 | `spmi`, `sgpio`, `fault`, `otp_crc` | - **Native reader** (`shutdown_cause_iokit_darwin.{c,h}`) walks the IOService plane, flattens every `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` array into a single `0x1f`-separated token sequence, and dedups as it writes — so no Core Foundation type crosses the cgo boundary. The whole plane is walked rather than matching a class because the publishing class is PMIC-specific and varies by Mac model, and IOKit cannot match on a property key alone (`kIOPropertyMatchKey` matches key *and* value). - **Classifier** (`shutdown_classify_darwin.go`) maps a token to its *family* (prefix before the first comma, a declared underscore family, or the whole token) and the family to one of five classes, resolved by fixed precedence: **thermal → power → crash → watchdog → hardware**. Thermal wins deliberately: a machine collapsing from heat also asserts reset, crash and power lines, and the event that matters most must not be titled as a crash. - **Event shape** (`format_darwin.go`) — `EventType` is the constant `"System shutdown fault"` so consumers can filter shutdown causes on one value; the class varies the title and message only. The payload reports every token observed *plus* the families and the fault subset the classifier acted on, so a reader sees both the raw evidence and what the verdict was based on: ```json "macos_shutdown_cause": { "source": "IOPMUBootFaultInfo", "classification": "thermal", "primary_family": "ot", "families": ["ot", "sochot"], "tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "fault_tokens": ["ot,tdie_overtemp", "ot,tsns_overtemp", "sochot,reset_in_3"], "boot_uuid": "…", "boot_time": "2026-08-11T09:55:21Z" } ``` - **Dedup is boot-scoped.** Identity is `shutdown:<bootUUID>:<sortedFaultTokens>`, hashed under a new `macos-shutdown-v1:` event-ID prefix. Both halves are load-bearing: the boot UUID alone says nothing about *what* was read, and the token set alone is identical across boots — a Mac that overheats every afternoon would emit one ID forever and be deduplicated into silence. Tokens are sorted first because PMU enumeration order is not stable (measured: two triggers with an identical fault set reported the groups in different order). - **Storage.** A new `ShutdownCause` bookmark field records the examined boot *whether or not* an event was emitted, so a cleanly-rebooting Mac does not re-read the property on every Agent restart. It is the primary guard rather than the `Acknowledged` map, which prunes after 30 days or 4096 entries — a Mac up longer than that would otherwise re-emit. The check runs **once per collector lifetime**, before the first directory scan, and is retried from the reconcile tick when it could not commit. It reads the property as an ordinary user (no root needed; system-probe runs as root regardless), and the whole feature is gated behind the existing `notable_events.enabled` setting, which defaults to `false`. **No benchmarks, deliberately.** There is no steady-state cost to measure: the IOService walk happens once per collector lifetime, is bounded at 16 services, and short-circuits as soon as every distinct token is accounted for. It is not on any per-event, per-scan or per-tick path. **Bookmark schema version stays at 1, deliberately.** `Load()` and `validateDarwinBookmarkState()` both require exact equality, so bumping to `2` would fail every existing v1 bookmark as corrupt — which resets state and re-baselines, discarding pending undelivered crash events on every upgraded host. `ShutdownCause` is `omitempty` with a nil zero value, so v1 bookmarks deserialize with no migration. Relatedly, `types.IsEventID()` had to learn the new prefix in the same change: a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID written under the old single-prefix check would fail validation on the next `Load()` and wipe the bookmark, silently losing every pending crash event. ### Motivation [https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3040) **A hard shutdown kills the Agent before it can report why.** Whether the machine overheated, lost a power rail, asserted its CRASH line, tripped a watchdog or hit a hardware fault, the Agent is gone before it can say so — the cause has to be recovered from the PMU on the next boot, or it is never recovered at all. All five fault classes are in scope here; thermal is one of them, not the point of the feature. **Predecessor: macOS app crash notable events (#54084).** This builds directly on it, reusing its bookmark, its `Pending`/`Ack` delivery contract and its at-least-once semantics unchanged — a second event *source* on that pipeline, not a second pipeline. It complements rather than replaces it: #54084 reports `.ips` files, which are written by a *running* OS about a *running* process, so a PMU-forced power cut leaves no `.ips` at all. The one adjacent artifact that does exist, `.shutdownStall` spindumps, records a *stalled* shutdown, not its cause. Everything else was surveyed and rejected: `pmset -g log` carries no cause data (25,117 lines grepped, nothing), `nvram -p` has no shutdown-cause variable, `ioreg -rc IOPMrootDomain` has no such property, `last -x reboot` is empty, and the `AppleSMC: Previous shutdown cause: <N>` unified-log line that Intel Macs emit **does not exist on Apple silicon**. Without this, a machine that overheated or lost a power rail badly enough to be cut off is a silent gap in the fleet record. `kern.shutdownreason` is **deliberately not read** — not as a source, not as a fallback, not as payload. It is the same PMU data flattened into an 80-byte-capped string, and it was already destroying data on an ordinary clean shutdown of the test machine: the cap was hit in 4 of 6 measured boots, always cutting *mid-token* and synthesising fault names that do not exist (`crash,crash`, `btn_rst,btn`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_d`). Absence of a token from that sysctl carries no information at all. The tradeoff is accepted and known: the sysctl also carries application-processor tokens (`ap_restart`, `ap_panic`) that `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not, and this PR gives those up rather than add a second parsing path and a second failure mode. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests — 240 tests pass in `pkg/notableevents`** (verified locally on the branch head with `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/notableevents/...`). Classifier tests deliberately use **payloads measured from real hardware** as fixtures rather than invented ones: | Pattern | Tokens (distinct union) | Emits | | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | A — clean shutdown | `target_off_restart`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | B — `sudo reboot` | `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert` | no event | | C — button/force restart | + `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `crash,crash0_in` | `crash`, `fault_tokens = ["crash,crash0_in"]` | Also covered: the full 80-token dictionary maps to exactly one family each with the asserted **59 fault / 21 benign** split (14 thermal, 29 power, 6 crash, 5 watchdog, 5 hardware) — this pins a typo in the family map that would otherwise silently misclassify; class precedence in every pairing; unknown *suffix* within a known family (`ot,some_future_sensor`) still classifies thermal, which is the prefix contract; permuted group order yields an identical event ID; benign-token exclusions are dead-weight-free (each is in the measured dictionary *and* would otherwise be a fault); every classification fits the wire limit; malformed and oversized payloads are rejected. Collector tests cover the delivery contract end to end: one event per boot; `Start()` → `Close()` → `Start()` yields one event, not two; same boot UUID after Ack yields nothing; a *different* boot UUID with the same tokens yields a new event; a saturated pending queue **defers** rather than records, because recording the boot would be final and the fault cannot be reproduced by a later boot; a `Save` failure leaves nothing pending and is retried; a check blocked by an in-flight bookmark commit is retried from the reconcile tick rather than stranded for the process lifetime; reader failure, absent property and untrusted payload all leave crash-report collection unaffected; a v1 bookmark with no `shutdown_cause` key loads without being treated as corrupt. **Manual QA on real hardware.** `Mac17,9` / M5 Pro / macOS 26.5.2 (`25F84`), SIP enabled, no `boot-args`. **Six real boot sessions** executed one trigger at a time — the property is destroyed by the next reboot, so the runs could not be batched — with an immediate capture script per boot: `sudo reboot`, Control-Command-Power force restart, power button held ~10s, a deliberately stalled shutdown ended by the power button, the same stall resolved via Try Again → Force Quit, and a battery run-down. Three distinct payloads were observed across six distinct boot UUIDs, verified byte-identical by MD5, reverting to pattern A after a clean shutdown. That establishes the load-bearing premise: **the property is a live, event-driven, self-clearing signal, not a constant** — which is what validates both the read path and the boot-UUID dedup key. **How to reproduce a fault event yourself — the `crash` class, on demand.** One fault class is reproducible at will on Apple silicon, so a reviewer can exercise the whole path end to end without waiting for real hardware trouble. A force restart asserts the AP's CRASH line, which emits `crash,crash0_in`: 1. Enable the feature — it is off by default: ```bash # datadog.yaml notable_events: enabled: true ``` 2. Clear any prior bookmark so the check is not skipped as already-examined, and note that the file is root-owned: ```bash sudo rm -f /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json ``` 3. Record the current boot identity and the pre-restart payload, for comparison: ```bash sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo ``` 4. Force restart: hold **Control-Command-Power** until the screen blanks. (Holding the power button ~10s, or ending a stalled shutdown with the power button, both produce the same payload — see the resolution caveat in Additional Notes.) 5. After the machine boots, confirm the PMU now reports the crash token. Expect pattern C — `rst`, `btn_rst,btn_seq_reset`, `target_off_restart`, `crash,crash0_in`, `wdog,reset_in_1`, `rst_in,reset_in_1_deassert`: ```bash ioreg -l -w 0 | grep IOPMUBootFaultInfo sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid # must differ from step 3 ``` 6. Start the Agent and system-probe, and confirm the event: ```bash sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.agent sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.datadoghq.sysprobe sudo cat /private/var/db/datadog-agent/notable-events/bookmark.json | jq . ``` Expect a `shutdown_cause` object whose `boot_uuid` matches step 5, and a `pending` entry with a `macos-shutdown-v1:` ID, `"event_type": "System shutdown fault"`, title `macOS crash shutdown`, `"classification": "crash"`, and `fault_tokens` of exactly `["crash,crash0_in"]` — all six tokens appear in `tokens`, but only the crash one elected the class. 7. Confirm the dedup guard: restart the Agent without rebooting. No second event should be emitted, and `shutdown_cause.boot_uuid` should be unchanged. To verify the **negative** case, `sudo reboot` instead of step 4 (pattern B) or shut down cleanly from the Apple menu (pattern A). Both must produce a `shutdown_cause` record with **no** event — a clean shutdown emitting an event is the failure mode most worth catching, since `wdog,reset_in_1` is present on every ordinary shutdown. **`qa/rc-required` — why this needs RC validation.** The classes that matter most in the field cannot be triggered on any machine we control, and cannot be simulated at all: the property is written by the PMU at power-off and is read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store. Reproducing a genuine thermal, power-rail or hardware fault means real failing hardware. Virtualized macOS runners expose no PMU, so the property is simply absent there and CI can only assert graceful degradation. What RC deployment adds is a full end-to-end test on real hardware: that the notable event is actually emitted and delivered, and that its tags and payload arrive intact. The predecessor, #54084, carried the same label for the same reason. **What was NOT validated, and cannot be:** - **No thermal token has ever been observed on this machine** — not `ot,*`, not `sochot,*`, not `ntc_shdn`. The thermal classification is inferred from token names in the PMU's own declared dictionary (published as `info-fault_name-<N>` properties on the `pmu,spmi` device-tree nodes). This is a hard limit, not a gap in the testing: there is **no native way to fake a thermal shutdown cause**. The value is produced by the PMU at power-off and exposed read-only through every interface, with no writable backing store — `sysctl -w` refuses (read-only OID), there is no user-settable IORegistry path, no `nvram` variable, and a userspace `os_log` line would not carry the right sender image. Generating real heat was out of scope. **The thermal path should not be described as verified in any customer-facing text or release note.** - **The real IOKit read on CI.** macOS VMs expose no PMU, so the property is absent and the reader returns empty. No E2E test is added; on a virtualized runner one could only assert graceful degradation, which is worth having but would not be thermal coverage. ### Additional Notes **Known tradeoff — `crash` fires on user force-restarts.** Measured, not hypothetical: `crash,crash0_in` appeared in pattern C with no panic induced. The token means the AP's CRASH line was asserted, which a hard reset satisfies, so **every user-initiated force restart on this hardware emits a `crash`-classified event.** Accepted because a force restart is itself a signal that something went wrong badly enough that the user gave up on the machine, and the alternative — treating the family as benign — silently dropped genuine AP and hypervisor crashes. Two commitments follow: the message says "followed a CRASH signal from the processor" and never claims a kernel panic; and if force restarts dominate emitted volume, the fix is to split `crash,hyp_*` from `crash,crash*_in`, not to revert the family to benign. **Fault allowlist, not benign denylist.** Under a denylist, any Mac whose clean shutdown emits an uncatalogued token would raise a shutdown-fault event on *every boot*. A permanent false positive is noticed and distrusted; a missed rare fault is not. The cost is that a genuinely new fault token on unfamiliar hardware is dropped silently — mitigated by matching on the family *prefix*, so `ot,anything_new` still classifies thermal. **Two benign per-token exceptions** (`shutdownBenignTokens`), for tokens whose family is a fault but whose meaning is not: `buck_boot_charge` (booting after the battery charged from depleted, not a regulator failure) and `timeout,dblclick_timeout` (the power-button double-click window). Both produced a user-visible fault event on a machine that had not faulted. Scoped to these two deliberately — the other `buck_*` tokens name real regulator failures. Excluding one only changes the outcome when it is the sole evidence for its class. **Graceful degradation is strictly additive** — nothing here can block `Start()` or interfere with crash-report collection. Property absent → no event, debug log. IOKit failure → no event. `kern.bootsessionuuid` unreadable → skip the whole check, since without a dedup key an event could repeat on every Agent restart. `kern.boottime` unreadable → fall back to the current time and omit `boot_time`. Event over the wire limit → drop and warn, **never truncate a fault payload**, because a truncated one would be misleading. Save-failure and saturation warnings latch so a persistent condition warns once rather than on every reconcile tick, and are kept separate so neither can silence the other. **Bounds are derived from real hardware, and shared between C and Go so they cannot drift.** `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKENS_PER_SERVICE 88` and `DD_PMU_MAX_TOKEN_CHARS 53` come from the largest known real payload (80-token dictionary, longest token 35 bytes) plus margin — 10% on count, 50% on length — and the Go-side `maxShutdownTokens` / `maxShutdownTokenBytes` are derived from those same macros. `DD_PMU_MAX_SERVICES` is 16, matching how few PMU-publishing services exist in practice. A service exceeding its bounds is dropped and logged rather than failing the read; an oversized token is truncated rather than dropping its whole service; the walk stops early once every distinct token is accounted for, since no remaining service can contribute one that has not been seen. **Intel Macs silently emit nothing.** `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` does not exist there; `readPMUBootFaultInfo` returns `errShutdownCauseUnsupported` when `runtime.GOARCH != "arm64"`. The Intel path (SMC shutdown-cause code `-81` via `log show`, which needs root) is unimplemented and unvalidated — no Intel Mac available. Apple documents none of this property: `org:apple-oss-distributions` returns zero hits for both `IOPMUBootFaultInfo` and `info-fault_name`. Provenance is the device's own ADT table, community string dumps of the `AppleD2255PMU` kext, and independent confirmation of the prefix decodings in `hack-different/apple-knowledge`. The *read mechanism*, by contrast, is entirely public API: `IOServiceMatching`, `IOServiceGetMatchingServices`, `IOIteratorNext`, `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty`.

signal.title: feat(windows): require the Agent configuration directory to be owned by an administrator
signal.text: _Re-lands #54269 (reverted for #incident-58787) unchanged. Follow-up fixes and the uninstall/upgrade-removal enforcement are stacked on top in #55133._ ### What does this PR do? Installation now fails when `C:\ProgramData\Datadog` already exists and is not owned by `Administrators` or `SYSTEM`, in both the MSI and the Go installer. The error names the owner found and the `takeown.exe` command to resolve it. - **MSI**: new `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` custom action after `InstallValidate`, so nothing has been changed on the system when it fails. It is skipped when uninstalling or being removed for an upgrade. The same check runs from the Welcome dialog and from maintenance Change/Repair, reporting through a popup; Remove is deliberately not checked. - **New `SecureDirectory` primitive** shared by `DDCreateFolders` and the rollback data store. It creates a directory with a protected SYSTEM/Administrators DACL, then reads the owner and applies permissions through a single handle that does not follow reparse points. - **Go installer**: `ensureDatadogDataDir` creates or validates the configuration directory, and `IsDirSecure` returns an actionable message. A new msiexec log pattern surfaces the failure in installer output. - **Error dialog**: replaces WixUI's `ErrorDlg` with `Custom_ErrorDialog`, sized like the existing modal, because the stock 205x60 text control clips these messages. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2998 Defense in depth. The Agent's configuration directory must be attributable to an administrator; if it already exists under another owner, resetting its permissions is not sufficient, so installation stops and explains how to resolve it instead of adopting the directory. This is a behavior change on both fresh installs and upgrades - existing installations are already compatible, since the MSI sets SYSTEM as the owner. Covered by the included `upgrade` release note. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New E2E test `TestInstallWithUntrustedConfigRoot`, wired into the `e2e_install_packages` job and run against AWS. - New tests for `SecureDirectory`, the MSI message escaping, `ensureDatadogDataDir`/`IsDirSecure`, and the msiexec log pattern - whose fixture is taken from a real MSI log. - Installed manually on a Windows VM with the configuration directory owned by a non-administrator, checking the message and the error dialog. - cross-ref'd ansible and chef packages to ensure compatability ### Additional Notes `Custom_ErrorDialog` is a renamed copy rather than a redefinition of `ErrorDlg`, since a WixUI library dialog cannot be redefined. Per the MSI spec it keeps `ErrorText` as its first control and all seven `Error*` buttons. MSI popup

signal.title: fix(aggregator): `Stop` no longer leaves a goroutine running
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? `BufferedAggregator.Stop()` now sends its own reply channel on `stopChan` and waits for `run()` to close it, instead of returning as soon as `run()` picks up the stop signal. Also deflaked `TestDemuxFlushAggregatorToSerializer` by replacing a `time.Sleep(250ms)` guess with `assert.Eventually` on `IsInputQueueEmpty()`, which is both faster (10-run mean: ~360ms to ~110ms) and no longer a fixed-duration guess that could be too short on a loaded runner. ### Motivation [tests_macos_gitlab_amd64](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1971012934) panicked in `comp/netflow/topn` with: ``` panic: Log in goroutine after TestTopNScheduling has completed: 2026-08-20 22:37:36 GMT | INFO | (pkg/aggregator/aggregator.go:802 in run) | Stopping aggregator ``` `run()` kept logging and deregistering health after `Stop()` had already returned, so a leaked goroutine could still write through the global logger once a later test rebound it to its own `*testing.T`. Measured under `-race` with a temporary instrumented hook: - before this change, `run()` finished after `Stop()` returned in 500/500 samples (median 263us, p99 767us, max 1.18ms), - after this change, all 500 samples show `run()` completing strictly before `Stop()` unblocks. ### Describe how you validated your changes Ran `dda inv test --race` on `pkg/aggregator/...` and `comp/netflow/topn/...` (241 tests, all pass), confirming the added wait causes no deadlock. ### Additional Notes The delayed log line and `health.Deregister()` have **no production impact** on their own, since the demultiplexer's `flushLoop` already completes its final flush synchronously before `agg.Stop()` is called. The panic is specific to `comp/core/log/mock` binding the global logger to a `*testing.T` that can finish before a leaked goroutine's write. The stop signal uses a request/reply channel (`stopChan chan chan struct{}`), mirroring the `trigger`/`blockChan` pattern already used elsewhere in this file for flush requests.

signal.title: [Backport 7.82.x]  Fix DI proxy dropping when logs_enabled unset
signal.text: Backport 95ac563f4fda703e58a84722440fb9dff8676282 from #54228. ___ ### What does this PR do? Fixes the trace-agent Dynamic Instrumentation proxy so it only drops debugger data when the Logs product is explicitly disabled. Previously, an unset `logs_enabled` was treated the same as an explicit `false`, so DI snapshots were silently dropped. The proxy now forwards unless `logs_enabled` (or the deprecated `log_enabled`) is set to `false` and neither key enables logs, matching how the logs agent itself decides to start. ### Motivation Customers reported that DI snapshots were not reaching the intake even though they had not disabled the Logs product. `core.GetBool("logs_enabled")` returns `false` for both "unset" and "explicitly false", so the proxy dropped snapshots any time the setting was omitted. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests in `comp/trace/config/impl` cover the matrix: both keys unset, each key explicitly `false`, the override, and mixed configurations where one key enables logs while the other is `false`.

signal.title: comp/api: restrict IPC/CMD unix socket to dd-agent
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Restricts the IPC and CMD server Unix socket (`agent_ipc.socket`) on Linux: - `chmod 0770` (was default `0755`) - when the Core Agent runs as root, `chown` the socket to the `dd-agent` user/group when they exist This matches the precedent already set by the runtime security agent gRPC server (`pkg/security/utils/grpc/grpc.go`). ### Motivation Deploying the host profiler under a non-root UID fails with: ``` Error: failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '<https+unix://localhost>/config/v1/' ? ``` When the core agent runs as root in docker, it creates `agent_ipc.socket` as `root:root` with mode `0755`. Connecting to a Unix socket on Linux requires **write** permission, so a subagent running as `dd-agent` (e.g. the host profiler) cannot connect. Other agent sockets (statsd, apm, the runtime security agent) already lock down their permissions; the IPC/CMD socket did not. ### Describe how you validated your changes CI ### Additional notes Behavior matrix: | Agent runs as | `dd-agent` exists | Socket owner | Socket mode | Host profiler (dd-agent) can connect? | |---|---|---|---|---| | root | yes | `dd-agent:dd-agent` | `0770` | ✅ (group write) | | root | no | `root:root` | `0770` | ❌ (no dd-agent user — expected) | | dd-agent | — | `dd-agent:dd-agent` | `0770` | ✅ (owner) |

Check the [Dependency Dashboard](../issues/33469) for more information. --- ### Release Notes <details> <summary>open-policy-agent/opa (github.com/open-policy-agent/opa)</summary> ### [`v1.19.0`](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/releases/tag/v1.19.0) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/compare/v1.18.2...v1.19.0) This release contains a mix of new features and bug fixes. Notably: - A fixed SQL injection vector in the Compile API - Stricter safety checking for Rego assignments (`:=`) - A cgo-free, faster WebAssembly runtime (wazero replaces wasmtime-go) - Startup warnings for unknown configuration options - A new `strings.split_n` built-in function - A REPL line reader that handles pasted input correctly, migrating existing history files ##### Fix SQL injection vector in Compile API: Quote SQL filter field identifiers ([#​8945](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/pull/8945)) The field names in the SQL emitted by the Compile API come from partially evaluated refs, so a policy that selects a dynamic key — such as `input.fruits[input.column]` — puts caller-controlled text in an identifier position. That text was emitted verbatim, which turns ```sql WHERE fruit.name = 'allowed' ``` into ```sql WHERE fruit.name = 'allowed' OR 1=1 -- = 'allowed' ``` and an application appending the filter to its query returns rows the policy denies. Field segments that are not bare identifiers are now quoted at the UCAST-to-SQL boundary, with any embedded quote character escaped. Ordinary column names stay unquoted, so existing filters keep their current shape and remain case-insensitive on Postgres. Authored by [@​thevilledev](https://redirect.github.com/thevilledev) ##### Behavior change: stricter safety for assignment (`:=`) ([#​3546](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/issues/3546)) The assignment operator (`:=`) is documented as "syntactic sugar for `=`, local variable creation, and additional compiler checks," and the safety checker reflects that: after rewriting, `:=` is treated identically to `=` (unification), so an assignment's right-hand side can be made safe by unifying "backwards" through the left-hand side. This means policies like `x := y; x = 7` compile (binding `y` to `7`) even though `y` is never assigned, and `x := y; obj[x]` can silently degrade an expected constant-time lookup into full iteration. This change makes the right-hand-side of `:=` be treated as a read that must be made safe by other expressions, and can no longer be satisfied through the left-hand-side. Affected policies that previously compiled now fail with a `rego_unsafe_var_error`. Reference iteration on the right-hand-side (e.g. `some k; v := obj[k]`) is unaffected. Note: this is a deliberate semantic change, not a fix to match documented behavior — the intended semantics of `:=` in this case were never specified. Authored by [@​sspaink](https://redirect.github.com/sspaink), reported by [@​tsandall](https://redirect.github.com/tsandall) ##### WebAssembly runtime: wasmtime-go replaced with wazero ([#​7557](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/issues/7557)) OPA's WebAssembly runtime — used by the `wasm` evaluation target and the WASM SDK — now runs on the pure-Go [wazero](https://wazero.io/) runtime instead of `bytecodealliance/wasmtime-go`. This removes the cgo dependency from this path, so `wasm`-enabled builds no longer need a C toolchain. Compiled policy modules are now cached process-wide, so repeated VM creation for the same policy skips recompilation. On an Apple M4 Max this makes wasm cold start (compile + instantiate + first eval) about 73% faster, and warm evaluation about 29% faster with \~28% fewer allocations. Authored by [@​srenatus](https://redirect.github.com/srenatus), reported by [@​sspaink](https://redirect.github.com/sspaink) ##### Configuration validation moved to Rego, with warnings on unknown options ([#​8891](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/pull/8891)) Top-level configuration validation and default injection (`default_decision`, `default_authorization_decision`, `labels`) is now expressed as an embedded Rego policy rather than hand-written Go, as is the validation of `server.metrics` and `metrics_export`. The user-visible effect is that unrecognized configuration options are reported instead of being silently ignored. A typo such as `decision_log` instead of `decision_logs` now logs a warning at startup: ```json {"level":"warning","msg":"unknown configuration option \"decision_log\" encountered"} ``` These are warnings, not errors: OPA starts as before, and sections that are intentionally user-extensible are left alone, so extra keys there do not warn. Embedders reading configuration through `config.ParseConfig` can find the same messages on `Config.Warnings`. Authored by [@​sspaink](https://redirect.github.com/sspaink) ##### Add `strings.split_n` built-in function ([#​8344](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/issues/8344)) Policies often need only the first or last few parts of a split string, but the existing `split` built-in always returns every part, so the count has to be worked around with wildcards or a slice. `strings.split_n` takes the first `n` split parts from the front or the back of the string, depending on whether `n` is positive or negative: ```rego result := strings.split_n("a.b.c.d", ".", 2) # result == ["a", "b"] ``` ```rego result := strings.split_n("a.b.c.d", ".", -2) # result == ["c", "d"] ``` If `abs(n)` is larger than the number of parts, all parts are returned. An `n` of `0` returns an empty array. Authored by [@​wonju-dev](https://redirect.github.com/wonju-dev), reported by [@​anderseknert](https://redirect.github.com/anderseknert) ##### Improved REPL line editing, with history file migration ([#​962](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/issues/962)) Pasting a tab-indented snippet into the REPL triggered tab-completion on the pasted tab, corrupting the input (e.g. injecting a completion candidate mid-line and producing a spurious parse error). Fixing that requires bracketed paste, where the terminal wraps pasted text in markers so the line reader inserts it literally instead of treating an embedded tab as a completion request. The previous reader, `peterh/liner`, has no bracketed-paste support and is unmaintained (last release 2021\), so it has been replaced with `reeflective/readline`. The new reader persists history as JSON lines instead of one command per line. Existing history files (`~/.opa_history` by default, or the path given to `--history`) are detected and migrated in place the first time the REPL loads them, so history written by earlier versions of OPA is kept. OPA's own multi-line buffering is unchanged, and `readline`'s native multi-line editing is left disabled to avoid changing REPL behavior. Authored by [@​sspaink](https://redirect.github.com/sspaink), reported by [@​aeneasr](https://redirect.github.com/aeneasr) ##### Runtime, SDK, Tooling - cmd: Avoid intermediate buffer when writing bundle ([#​8909](https://redirect.github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/pull/8909)) authored by [@​anderseknert](https://redirect.github.com/anderseknert) - signal.title: Fix DI proxy dropping when logs_enabled unset
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes the trace-agent Dynamic Instrumentation proxy so it only drops debugger data when the Logs product is explicitly disabled. Previously, an unset `logs_enabled` was treated the same as an explicit `false`, so DI snapshots were silently dropped. The proxy now forwards unless `logs_enabled` (or the deprecated `log_enabled`) is set to `false` and neither key enables logs, matching how the logs agent itself decides to start. ### Motivation Customers reported that DI snapshots were not reaching the intake even though they had not disabled the Logs product. `core.GetBool("logs_enabled")` returns `false` for both "unset" and "explicitly false", so the proxy dropped snapshots any time the setting was omitted. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests in `comp/trace/config/impl` cover the matrix: both keys unset, each key explicitly `false`, the override, and mixed configurations where one key enables logs while the other is `false`.
