Root cause: the suite was added on 2026-08-21 in PR #52410 ("add support for CNM direct send to windows"). Its `Test00FakeIntakeNPM_HostRequests` assertion (`common_1host.go:91`) locks onto the first-seen hostname and requires at least 5 CollectorConnections payloads (30s cadence, ~150s) within a 150s window. On Windows EC2, the VM hostname changes mid-run (rename + reboot → system-probe restart → new cached hostname), so payloads split across two hostname/networkID keys. signal.title: fix(procmgr): anchor in-flight Stop RPCs to SCM shutdown budget
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Ensures Stop RPC child teardown respects the Windows SCM shutdown deadline when a service stop is in progress. - Adds `ShutdownBudget::prefer_service_stop()` / `refresh()` / `for_single_stop()` so RPC stops share the same SCM-anchored budget as ordered shutdown. - Adds `wait_graceful_or_shutdown()` to interrupt graceful stop waits on `shutdown_notify` (Windows). - Applies the budget in `wait_for_stop_since()` and consolidates Windows spawn-resource cleanup on stop. Follow-up to [Codex review on #54731](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54731#discussion_r3831784217). ### Motivation When SCM stop arrives while the supervisor is handling a `Stop` RPC, `handle_command` stays blocked on `proc.stop()` and cannot poll the shutdown future. RPC stops used an unlimited `ShutdownBudget`, so a configured `stop_timeout` larger than the ~175s service budget could keep the service in `STOP_PENDING` past the SCM wait hint before ordered shutdown begins. With default `stop_timeout` (90s) this stays within budget; this closes the gap for large custom timeouts and for SCM stop arriving mid-RPC. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Added unit test `test_prefer_service_stop_without_signal_preserves_fallback` in `pkg/procmgr/rust/src/shutdown.rs`. - Existing shutdown and process stop tests in `shutdown.rs` / `process.rs` cover the refactored paths (CI: `//pkg/procmgr/rust:dd-procmgrd_test`). ### Additional Notes - Windows-only behavior for SCM deadline and `shutdown_notify` interrupt; Unix is unchanged (`service_stop_signal_time()` is always `None`). - **Base branch:** `jose/procmgr-spawn-profiles` (stacked follow-up). Retarget to `main` after #54731 merges if preferred.

signal.title: Update gcc-toolchain to 0.12.1
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Updates gcc-toolchain to 0.12.1 and adjusts patches accordingly. ### Motivation https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54846 has run into linking errors (https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1968744747). The issue has to do with the linker resolving against the actual filesystem root instead of the sysroot's. I think https://github.com/f0rmiga/gcc-toolchain/pull/231 is what fixes this for us in this case, and this version incorporates the change. ### Describe how you validated your changes Green CI, and build passing for https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54846 locally (under linux arm64, at least). ### Additional Notes The core of the issue is that the linker was picking files from the sysroot via `-L%workspace%/{include_prefix}sysroot/lib` etc., which picked up at least one linker script with absolute (sysroot-relative) paths. Given that we're not providing a `--sysroot`, this is trying to link against things in the host, which is obviously wrong and breaks loudly here. Upstream gcc-toolchain has dropped these `-B` and `-L` flags pointing into the sysroot, which removes the problem. I still don't know exactly why that target specifically was the one to hit this error (despite having other targets that link against zstd via cgo).

signal.title: [PoC] Add metricslogs component for local metrics-as-logs debugging
signal.text: ## What this change does Adding `comp/forwarder/metricslogs` component. This component writes metrics as structured JSON lines to the agent's own local log. Other internal agent components can use this component to write metrics as logs, bypassing tags cardinality limits. ## Why we need this change `ebpf-check` emits metrics for each map and each program. This creates too many tag combinations. These combinations overflow the metrics cardinality limits. This component gives a safe way to write this kind of data as a structured log line, not as a tagged metric. ## Important limits This component is for internal use only. Do not use it for customer-facing metrics. This component only writes to the agent's local log. It never sends data over the network. It does not need `logs_enabled`. It does not create billable Log volume. It has no config gate: any caller can use it at any time. ## How the component behaves The caller sends one batch of metrics in one call, through `LogMetrics(metrics []*Metric) error`. The component builds one structured JSON line from the batch and writes it to the local log at Debug level. All metrics in the batch share one log line. An empty batch is a no-op. ## How this was tested - Unit tests cover the component: a normal call with several metrics, and an empty batch. - The full agent binary was built with this change. The build was successful. - The Go linter was run on the new code. The linter found no issues. ## Follow-up work - A separate PR (#55234) adds a `WithLevel` option, so a caller can choose Trace instead of Debug. - Connect the ebpf-check to this component.

signal.title: [DO NOT MERGE] One-off e2e run with ADP enabled by default
signal.text: ## Summary Temporarily flips \`data_plane.enabled\` from \`false\` to \`true\` in the agent's compiled-in config default so that every e2e test in the full suite runs against ADP without requiring per-test changes or test duplication. The change is throwaway — close without merging once the CI run completes. This is the same config knob used by the AMP ADP test helpers (DADP-72, see [Slack thread](https://dd.slack.com/archives/C070PQKLLP5/p1783453441368899)). ## How to kick off the full e2e suite Trigger a new pipeline on this branch and set the CI variable: \`\`\` RUN_E2E_TESTS=on \`\`\` That variable hits the \`if_run_all_e2e_tests\` rule in \`.gitlab-ci.yml\` and flips all e2e jobs from manual to \`on_success\`. ## CI findings (ADP 1.5.1, branch jszwedko/run-ci-adp-enabled) ### Fixed in this PR - **Windows MSI \`status_command_infos\`**: All MSI test variants fail because \`agent_behaviour.go\` asserts the status output contains "DogStatsD". When ADP handles DSD, the \`DogStatsD\` status section is absent (the \`EnabledInternal()\` guard prevents registering the status provider). Fixed by accepting either "DogStatsD" or "Dogstatsd Metric Sample" (always present in the Aggregator section). ### Known pre-existing failures (ADP limitations, tracked in Saluki) - **\`TestReplayWithTagEnrichment\`** — ADP doesn't enrich replayed DSD packets with current tagger state. Tracked in Saluki. ### New failures requiring Saluki fixes - **Container DSD tests (ECS \`TestDogtstatsdUDP\`, \`TestDogtstatsdUDS\`; Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods)**: In container environments (ECS, K8s/Kind), fakeintake is configured as \`DD_ADDITIONAL_ENDPOINTS\` rather than \`dd_url\`. ADP doesn't appear to forward DogStatsD metrics to \`additional_endpoints\`, so no metrics arrive at fakeintake. In VM tests where fakeintake IS \`dd_url\` (primary endpoint), DSD forwarding works. This points to an \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding gap in ADP. - The Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods fail to become Ready — the workload pods mount \`/var/run/datadog/dsd.socket\` as a HostPath volume (type \`Socket\`). With ADP enabled, the core agent's DSD server doesn't start (so no socket is created); ADP must create it but apparently doesn't complete socket setup in time or at the expected path. - Root cause: ADP \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding — active Saluki config migration work (issues #2312–#2316) may be the upstream cause. ### Other failures under investigation - **Anomaly detection tests** — under investigation, may be ADP-independent - **GPU tests** — under investigation ## Test plan - No new tests. The goal is to observe which existing e2e tests break when ADP is the default. - \`new-e2e-amp-adp\` (existing) runs the AMP suite filtered to \`--run "ADP"\` tests; this PR covers the rest. **DO NOT MERGE** — this default flip must not land on \`main\`.

signal.title: Add a lightweight gate for prepared Agent rollouts
signal.text: ### Why A DaemonSet update can delete a working Agent before Kubernetes pulls and starts its replacement. A slow or failed pull can therefore leave the node without an Agent. ### What does this PR do? This PR adds an experimental Linux `agent-rollout-gate` binary to the node Agent images. The Operator can start this binary before each Agent component. The gate waits for a component-specific host lock before it starts the real process. This lets Kubernetes pull and create a replacement Pod while the old Agent still serves. Each component changes ownership independently. A slow `system-probe` shutdown does not block the core Agent or trace Agent. The gate keeps the startup probe unsuccessful while it sleeps. Kubernetes does not run readiness or liveness probes until startup succeeds. After the gate gets the lock, it starts the Agent and uses the original probe and termination behavior. This mechanism does not claim zero-gap telemetry. Agent caches, Cluster Agent assignments, metadata, and process state still start cold after handoff. ### Validation - `dda inv test --targets=./cmd/agent-rollout-gate`: 9 tests passed on macOS. - `dda inv agent-rollout-gate.build`: passed for Linux arm64. - `dda inv linter.go --targets=./cmd/agent-rollout-gate`: 0 issues. - Formatting and Python task compilation: passed. The Linux lock, signal, and probe tests must pass in CI. Experimental-cluster validation starts after the three PoC PRs are reviewed. ### Related PRs - Operator: https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-operator/pull/3355 - Experimental deployment: https://github.com/DataDog/k8s-datadog-agent-ops/pull/9477 The gate-capable Agent image must be deployed with the ordinary rollout before prepared mode is enabled.

signal.title: fix(remoteagentregistry): canonicalize local metric help
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes Core Agent telemetry HELP text canonical when Remote Agent Registry (RAR) merges incoming Prometheus telemetry. The telemetry component records HELP text for metric families it creates in the normal `/telemetry` registry. When RAR receives a remote family with the same name, it uses that local HELP text when constructing the forwarded Prometheus descriptor. Remote-only families retain the remote agent's HELP text. ### Motivation Prometheus requires metric families that share a name to use identical HELP text. A remote agent can currently supply a different description for a metric also emitted by Core Agent, causing the combined telemetry gather to fail. The Core Agent definition is the authoritative local contract. This includes the Core Agent DogStatsD client byte counters added in #54381. The regression coverage verifies that Core Agent's `dogstatsd_client__bytes_sent` HELP wins over incompatible ADP text while retaining the ADP sample and authoritative `emitter` label. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/core/telemetry/impl:impl_test //comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl:impl_test --test_output=errors` - `git diff --check` - Independent spec-compliance and code-quality reviews. `dda inv test --targets=./comp/core/telemetry/impl,./comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl --timeout=120` and `dda inv linter.go --targets=./comp/core/telemetry/impl,./comp/core/remoteagentregistry/impl --timeout=120` were blocked before compilation by an internal dependency-mirror HTTP 403 for `github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/extension/healthcheckextension@v0.158.0`, which is in its mirror cooldown window. ### Additional Notes The canonical HELP catalog deliberately covers metrics created through the telemetry component's counter, gauge, and histogram factory APIs. It excludes `DefaultMetric` and opaque direct `RegisterCollector` registrations, which are not part of RAR's normal telemetry registry merge path.

signal.title: feat(serverless-init): add shared infrastructure for AWS MicroVM cloud service
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds the shared Go infrastructure that AWS MicroVM cloud-service support depends on. This is the first in a stack of PRs that together deliver full MicroVM observability. ### Motivation The Datadog Agent's serverless-init supports multiple cloud platforms (Cloud Run, Container Apps, etc.) via a `CloudService` abstraction. AWS Lambda MicroVMs are a new deployment target where the Agent runs as an init process inside a Firecracker microVM. Each new platform requires small additions in a few central places before the platform-specific code can be wired in cleanly. This PR makes those additions in isolation so the platform-specific MicroVM PR is a clean diff: - **`pkg/metrics/metricsource.go`** — adds `MetricSourceAWSMicroVMEnhanced`, the metric source tag used on all MicroVM enhanced metrics. - **`pkg/serverless/env/env.go`** — adds `MicroVMImageARNEnvVar` (`AWS_LAMBDA_MICROVM_IMAGE_ARN`), the env var the platform injects with the image ARN. - **`pkg/serializer/internal/metrics/origin_mapping.go`** — maps the new MetricSource to its origin string so metrics are routed correctly in the serializer. - **`comp/dogstatsd/server/impl/default_serverless.go` + `enrich.go`** — threads MicroVM origin/tag enrichment through DogStatsD's serverless path. - **`comp/logs-library/processor/json_serverless_init.go`** — adds a JSON log encoder for structured serverless-init logs, needed for MicroVM's log pipeline. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New unit tests cover the origin mapping and DogStatsD enrichment paths. - All changes are additive; no existing behaviour is altered. signal.title: fix(otel-metrics): skip spans with client-computed stats
signal.text: ## What Datadog tracing libraries can emit spans as OTLP while also computing APM stats client-side (CSS). Those spans carry `_dd.stats_computed` as a resource or span attribute. Before this PR, the DDOT connector did not inspect that marker. It converted the spans and recomputed hits, errors, and duration, double-counting stats the tracing library had already produced. After this PR, the connector treats `_dd.stats_computed` as a `ResourceSpans`-level signal. When the marker is truthy on the resource or any span it contains, every span in that `ResourceSpans` is excluded from the connector's concentrator. Other resources in the same OTLP batch remain eligible for Agent-computed stats. ## Why resource scope is correct - Client-side stats are enabled or disabled for the whole ddtrace client; there is no partial per-span enablement. - The ddtrace OTLP path emits `_dd.stats_computed` as a resource attribute. - The Agent and built-in collector processors preserve or copy the resource and its attributes when forwarding, batching, splitting, or regrouping trace data. One marked span is therefore sufficient evidence for its containing `ResourceSpans`, but not for other resources that happen to share the same `ptrace.Traces` payload. ## Changes - Detect `_dd.stats_computed` on both resource and span attributes. - Promote a span-level marker to its containing `ResourceSpans`. - Skip every span belonging to a client-computed resource while retaining unmarked resources. - Return before span indexing and top-level detection when the entire payload is client-computed. - Allocate the computed-resource set only when a marker is found. - Treat absent, empty, or `false` markers as not client-computed; other non-empty values enable the skip. ## Performance The same focused benchmark was run at the PR's base commit and current head on an Apple M4 Max with `GOMAXPROCS=1`. The payload contains 10 resources with 10 spans each. | Scenario | Before PR | After PR | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Client stats enabled | ~281.6 us/op | ~0.82 us/op | ~344x faster | | Client stats disabled | ~282.5 us/op | ~283.7 us/op | +0.4%, within benchmark noise | With client stats enabled, memory falls from 114,808 B/op to 712 B/op and allocations from 855 to 5. With client stats disabled, memory and allocations are unchanged at 114,808 B/op and 855 allocations/op. The added no-marker resource scan measures approximately 0.50 us per 100 spans with zero allocations. That is about 0.18% of the baseline conversion cost, or roughly 5 ns per span for this payload. ## Validation ```text bazel test //pkg/trace/otel/stats:stats_test bazel test //comp/otelcol/otlp/components/connector/datadogconnector:datadogconnector_test ``` Both targets pass. Tests cover marker parsing, resource-level markers, promotion of a span marker to its containing resource, and retaining unmarked resources in the same payload.

signal.title: [CWS-6628] Implement the unshare syscall event
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds a public `unshare` CWS event carrying the requested namespace flags, so detection rules can match the syscall itself rather than the name of the calling binary: ``` unshare.flags & CLONE_NEWNET > 0 unshare.flags & (CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET) > 0 && process.file.name != "docker" ``` New SECL surface: `unshare.flags` (bitmask, `Clone flags` constants) and `unshare.retval`. 12 `CLONE_*` constants are registered. ### Motivation Jira: [CWS-6628](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628) (also filed as [CWS-6778](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778) — duplicates). Requested by the detection guild. Recent Linux LPE exploits call `unshare` **directly** to create a new network namespace and thereby obtain `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. Today CWS can only catch this via `process.executable.name == "unshare"`, which misses every exploit that invokes the syscall from its own code. > [!NOTE] > The Jira description claims this complements an existing `setns` event. There is no `setns` instrumentation in CWS — `setns` appears only in the syscall-number tables used by the syscall-monitor event. This is CWS's first namespace-lifecycle event. Scope is unchanged; the ticket framing is just wrong. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `pkg/security/tests/unshare_test.go` with per-flag rules plus a combined `CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET` case (the actual exploit shape), asserting the exact raw bitmask and `retval`. The `syscall_tester` helper invokes `unshare(2)` **directly** rather than exec'ing `unshare(1)`, since catching direct syscall callers is the point. Verified locally: | Check | Result | |---|---| | eBPF C compiles — kprobe, fentry, syscall-wrapper | all 3 objects rebuilt; `tracepoint/"handle_sys_unshare_exit"` present | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/...` | 1420 passed | | `dda inv security-agent.build-functional-tests` | testsuite + `syscall_tester` build clean | | Codegen idempotent | re-ran generation, byte-identical output | | `dda inv linter.go` on secl, probe, serializers, ebpf | 0 issues | > [!IMPORTANT] > **KMT functional tests have not been run** — they need a real kernel. Since this modifies an event the mount resolver depends on, please run `TestUnshareEvent` **plus the mount, pivot_root and network suites** before merging. `syscall_tester.c:test_new_netns_exec` already calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, so this event will start firing inside existing network tests. ### Additional Notes <details> <summary>Why the public event reuses event ordinal 46, and why that matters</summary> `unshare` was already hooked, but narrowly: the hook bailed out unless `CLONE_NEWNS` was set, and the resulting `unshare_mntns` event was swallowed in userspace after registering the mount-namespace copy (`field:"-"`, never dispatched to rules). That internal event fires **once per cloned mount** — `hook_make_visible`, `hook_attach_mnt`, `hook___attach_mnt`, `hook_attach_recursive_mnt` and `hook_propagate_mnt` each call `handle_new_mount()` for a distinct mount, which tail-calls through to `dr_mount_stage_two_callback` → `send_event`. Correct for mount bookkeeping; wrong for detection, where a rule must fire once per syscall. So the two concerns are now separate event types: - **`EVENT_UNSHARE` (ordinal 46, reusing the old slot)** — public, per-syscall. Full process/cgroup/span context plus the raw flags bitmask, sent once from the exit hook. - **`EVENT_UNSHARE_MNTNS` (newly appended)** — internal, per-mount. Semantics unchanged, still consumed by `handleNewMount` and never dispatched to rules. Keeping the *public* event at ordinal 46 is load-bearing. `probe_ebpf.go` packs enabled events as `1 << (eventType - 1)` into a **`uint64`**, mirrored kernel-side in `helpers/events.h`. `PivotRootEventType` is ordinal 64 — the last representable bit, which is exactly why `LastEventType = PivotRootEventType`. A newly appended public type would be ordinal 69 and therefore permanently unreachable by `is_event_enabled()` and by `applyDefaultFilterPolicies()`. The internal event doesn't care, since internal events are never gated by that mask. </details> <details> <summary>Event volume</summary> Bounded by a single gate: **`is_event_enabled(EVENT_UNSHARE)`** — no event at all when no loaded rule references `unshare.*`. Every `unshare` call is reported once that gate opens, so all 12 exposed `CLONE_*` constants are matchable and the `flags` field carries the full raw bitmask. An earlier revision also filtered kernel-side on `CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID`. That was dropped in review: it silently made rules on the other exposed constants (`CLONE_NEWUTS`, `CLONE_NEWIPC`, `CLONE_NEWTIME`, …) unable to fire. Per-flag volume control belongs in `unshare` approvers, as a follow-up. `CLONE_NEWNS` is always *cached* regardless of the gate, because the mount resolver depends on that hook entry. </details> <details> <summary>Known gap and follow-ups</summary> - In `handle_new_mount` (`mount.h`), if the mount bookkeeping bails early it calls `pop_syscall()`, dropping the cache entry before the exit hook runs — so that particular `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` produces no public event. Narrow degraded path, mirrors existing behaviour, but a real coverage hole for `CLONE_NEWNS` specifically. - ebpfless/ptracer support deferred, as `setrlimit` did. - `setns` instrumentation (the join-side signal) not in scope. - Four existing events (ordinals 65–68: `SampleRefresh`, `SetSid`, `Nop`, `Socket`) are already unreachable by the `enabled_events` mask and silently stay that way. Widening it past 64 bits is separate, cross-cutting work worth filing. </details> [CWS-6628]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [CWS-6778]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: Pedro.cordeiro/macos ec2 snapshot poc
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Introduces a shared pool of macOS EC2 Dedicated Hosts for the E2E test framework, so macOS test runs stop provisioning (and tearing down) a brand-new Dedicated Host + instance every time. - **Pool package** (`test/e2e-framework/resources/aws/ec2/pool`): discovers idle, tagged macOS EC2 instances and manages their lifecycle via lease records stored in S3, using conditional writes (ETag/If-Match) to arbitrate concurrent acquisition: - `Acquire` claims an idle instance from the pool (`AcquireIdleInstance`), or falls back to a per-developer local instance lookup/provisioning path (`LocalProvisionOptions`) outside CI. - Leases track `idle`/`in-use` status, owner, and `leased_at`, and are namespaced per owner to avoid collisions. - `RevertAndRelease` reverts an instance's root volume to the lease's baseline AMI and republishes it as `idle` on teardown; `RevertInPlace` re-reverts and re-publishes as `in-use` for local dev reuse. - `PublishInitialLease` registers a brand-new pool member's first lease out-of-band (used when auto-provisioning on a local cache miss). - **Provisioning wiring** (`test/e2e-framework/resources/aws/ec2/vm.go`): macOS VM creation now imports an existing pool member (pinning `HostID`/`SubnetID`/AMI via `pulumi.Import` + `IgnoreChanges`, and `RetainOnDelete` so Pulumi never destroys pooled instances) instead of always creating a fresh Dedicated Host. On a local cache miss, it provisions a new Dedicated Host/instance through ordinary Pulumi resources and registers it as a new pool member. - **Teardown wiring** (`test/e2e-framework/testing/e2e/suite.go`): `BaseSuite.releasePoolInstanceIfAny` reverts and releases the pool instance backing a suite's environment at teardown, replacing ad hoc destroy-based cleanup for macOS hosts. - **Bypass flag**: `E2E_MACOS_POOL_ENABLED` (default enabled) lets a run opt out of the pool entirely and fall back to the pre-existing per-run Dedicated Host provisioning; it's meant to be removed once the pool is validated and trusted as the default. - CI-run detection now checks the `CI` env var, so local runs consistently take the per-developer local-provisioning path. ### Motivation Every macOS E2E test run previously stood up a new AWS EC2 Dedicated Host that was used once and then torn down — but AWS bills Dedicated Host allocations in 24-hour minimum increments, so each single test run paid for a full day of macOS instance time. A shared pool of pre-baked, leasable hosts amortizes that 24h allocation across many runs via acquire/release against S3-backed lease state. See [WINA-2931](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2931). ### Describe how you validated your changes - Ran `TestMacosInstallScript` locally in CI-mode (`E2E_PIPELINE_ID` forced) and in local-provisioning mode against a live pool, confirming warm-import acquisition and correct root-volume revert/release on teardown. - Ran four simultaneous `TestMacosInstallScript` invocations against a 2-member pool to exercise acquire-retry contention: the two extra runs correctly queued and waited on `pool.Acquire`'s retry loop until a member was released, then all four passed. - Validated the `E2E_MACOS_POOL_ENABLED=false` bypass path falls back to the pre-existing per-run Dedicated Host provisioning unchanged. ### Additional Notes [WINA-2931]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-2931?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: feat(dogstatsd): detect client payload drops
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Detects sustained DogStatsD client-reported payload-byte drops for UDS and UDS-stream clients using telemetry from the normal final aggregation path. When the drop rate exceeds 1%, the Agent reports a per-Agent Agent Health issue containing queue, writer, and unclassified drop totals. The issue resolves after sustained healthy telemetry. This adds two confirmation-period settings: - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.unhealthy_confirmation_window` defaults to `1m` and prevents transient drops from opening an issue. - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.recovery_confirmation_window` defaults to `30m` and prevents intermittent drops from repeatedly resolving and reopening the issue. ### Motivation This builds on #54381, which exposes DogStatsD client byte telemetry through Agent Telemetry/COAT. Detecting sustained drops in the Agent provides consistent behavior across supported clients and surfaces an actionable Agent Health issue without requiring new client payloads or library changes. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Unit tests covering detection, confirmation, recovery, missing telemetry, restart reconciliation, and multi-worker flush ordering - Fakeintake integration test covering ACTIVE and RESOLVED Agent Health reports - Updated the benchmarks ### Additional Notes

signal.title: ci: default to GIT_DEPTH=1, full clone for jobs needing git history
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Sets a repo-wide `GIT_DEPTH: 1` default in `.gitlab-ci.yml` to speed up job checkouts, and adds `GIT_DEPTH: 0` overrides on the jobs whose scripts (or the invoke tasks they call) run history-dependent git operations: - `.gitlab/build/source_test/golang_deps_diff.yml` (`golang_deps_diff` — `git merge-base` via `go-deps.diff`) - `.gitlab/test/e2e/e2e.yml` (`.new_e2e_template` — `git merge-base` for `--impacted` test selection) - `.gitlab/.pre/ci_configuration.yml` (`test_gitlab_compare_to`, `compute_gitlab_ci_config`, `lint_github_actions_shellcheck` — all use `git merge-base`) - `.gitlab/build/binary_build/fakeintake.yml` (`fakeintake_check_version_bump` — `git merge-base` + reading a file at the merge-base commit) - `.gitlab/deploy/internal_kubernetes_deploy/internal_kubernetes_deploy.yml` (`notify-slack` — `git log` over a commit range for the changelog) - `.gitlab/build/lint/technical_linters.yml` (`lint_releasenotes_rst` — `git merge-base`) - `.gitlab/.pre/setup/setup.yml` (`setup_agent_version` — `git describe --tags`, needs full history to find the nearest tag) Jobs that already had an explicit `GIT_DEPTH`/`GIT_STRATEGY` override (`regression_detector.yml`, `static_quality_gate.yml`, `files_inventory_check.yml`, the Windows bazel runner) were left untouched. The Windows `GIT_STRATEGY: "clone"` templates in `deploy/conditions.yml` / `agent7.yml` are unrelated to git history (they work around CIEXE-1152 for cancelled jobs) and don't need `GIT_DEPTH: 0`. ### Motivation Shallow clones reduce checkout time/bandwidth across the pipeline, which runs on every commit/PR. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Validated YAML syntax of all changed files. - Manually traced every git operation (`git merge-base`, `git log` ranges, `git describe --tags`) reachable from CI jobs, including through the invoke tasks they call (`tasks/libs/common/git.py`, `tasks/gotest.py`, `tasks/libs/releasing/version.py`, etc.) to confirm which jobs need full history. - Ran the `gitlab-configuration` pre-push linter (`dda inv linter.full-gitlab-ci -t main --pre-push-linters --fail-fast`) locally — passed with pre-existing warnings unrelated to this change. ### Additional Notes **Known risk, intentionally not addressed here:** the Linux/macOS/Windows unit-test jobs use `--only-impacted-packages` on essentially every dev-branch pipeline (via `FAST_TESTS=true`), which calls `git merge-base` through `tasks/gotest.py:get_impacted_packages` with **no error handling**. Under `GIT_DEPTH=1`, if the merge-base predates the 1-commit shallow window, this would hard-fail the test job rather than gracefully falling back to running all tests. This wasn't addressed in this PR to avoid setting `GIT_DEPTH: 0` on the largest and most CI-time-costly category of jobs, which would defeat much of the purpose of this change. Options going forward: harden the fallback in `get_impacted_packages` (deepen fetch or fall back to "run all tests" on merge-base failure), or scope `GIT_DEPTH: 0` to those jobs if the risk materializes.

signal.title: feat(windows): enforce the config root security check on uninstall too
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Stacked on #55136. Extends that PR's config-root owner check to uninstall and upgrade-removal, which it currently skips, and trusts one more owner: - `EnsureSecureConfigRoot` now runs unconditionally in the MSI's `InstallExecuteSequence`, including on uninstall and removal for an upgrade, instead of being skipped there. It only asserts ownership and never changes anything, so it can't leave a partial uninstall behind. - `DDCreateFolders` now runs on every install/upgrade/repair/uninstall pass instead of only on first install, creating the config root if it's missing. It only resets an existing directory's permissions on a true first install, so upgrade/repair/uninstall never strips access (e.g. ddagentuser's) granted after the directory was first created. - The maintenance dialog's config-root check is now a single check on the Welcome dialog's `Next`, covering Change, Repair, and Remove alike, instead of a separate per-button check that skipped Remove. - `ContainerAdministrator` (the account Windows containers run as by default) is trusted alongside `Administrators`/`SYSTEM` in both the Go and MSI checks. ### Motivation Uninstall-time steps that depend on the config root (e.g. the fleet installer's `prerm` hook) should get the same defense-in-depth guarantee installation already has, instead of only install/upgrade/repair being covered. ### Describe how you validated your changes - New/updated `SecureDirectory` unit tests for the create-if-missing-without-reset behavior used outside first install, and for trusting `ContainerAdministrator`. - Fixed a race in `TestInstallAltDirAndCorruptForUninstall`: the test deleted the Agent's registry key while the service was still running, which could let the running Agent (as `ddagentuser`) recreate the default config directory itself before the fix stopped the service first.
signal.author: clarkb7

signal.title: [Backport 7.81.x]  Windows: don't let registry DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS fallback override explicit install args
signal.text: Backport 32353f859276f5283be48e7abe1a615891312a63 from #54125. ___ ### What does this PR do? Prevents a `getenv()` fallback (registry-derived `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS`, service-derived `DDAGENTUSER_NAME`) from silently overriding an explicit value passed via install args on a Fleet Automation install/upgrade. ### Motivation Follow-up to #53958, addressing a [review concern](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/54081#discussion_r3642641460) that also applies to `main`. `getenv()`'s fallbacks for `AgentUserKeepRights` (registry) and `AgentUserName` (running service) don't know about raw install args (`ctx.WindowsArgs`), a separate path an operator/Fleet task can use to pass these properties explicitly. Since `msi.Cmd()` always places typed properties after raw args on the final command line regardless of option order, a stale fallback value would win over an explicit one, reversing the operator's intent. `AgentUserPassword` has no such fallback and isn't affected. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `TestArgsHaveProperty`: property present/absent/nil args, no false-positive prefix match, covers both `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS` and `DDAGENTUSER_NAME`. - New E2E suite `TestAgentKeepRightsFleetUpgrade` (`test/new-e2e/tests/installer/windows/agent_keep_rights_fleet_test.go`), driving the real Fleet Automation experiment lifecycle (`StartExperiment`/`PromoteExperiment`) against a stable baseline pinned to 7.81.0 (the first release with `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS`), registered in the `new-e2e-installer-windows` CI matrix: - `TestKeepRightsSurvivesFleetUpgrade` — regression test for #53958. - `TestKeepRightsExplicitArgWinsOnFleetUpgrade` — regression test for this PR, using `StartExperimentMSIArgs` to inject an explicit override at experiment time. Both E2E tests passed CI after two fixes to the tests themselves (a log-filename collision from calling `installPreviousAgentVersion()` twice, and pinning the stable baseline version since the pipeline's default "last stable" pointer predates the `DDAGENTUSER_KEEP_RIGHTS` feature) — the underlying fix required no changes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Enables the **v3 metrics intake for series** in DDOT (the `otel-agent` binary). signal.title: compliance/k8sconfig: fix kubelet defaults when --config is used
signal.text: Kubernetes keeps the historical command line default of a few kubelet flags to preserve the command line API, and drops them as soon as the kubelet is started with --config. The configuration file is then loaded with the KubeletConfiguration defaults instead, and only the flags that appear on the command line are applied on top of it. The loader applied the command line defaults in both cases. The two sets of defaults disagree on exactly the three settings the CIS Kubernetes benchmarks care about. A kubelet reading a configuration file that leaves them out runs with the read-only port disabled, anonymous authentication disabled and Webhook authorization, while the loader reported a read-only port on 10255, anonymous authentication enabled and an AlwaysAllow authorization mode. OpenShift and kubeadm both leave readOnlyPort out of their rendered configuration, so their nodes failed "The kubelet read-only port should be disabled" with the port closed. The generator now carries the configuration file default next to the command line one for those three flags, and the loader picks between them by whether the component reads a configuration file. The payload version is bumped so that rules can tell the two apart. Updates CSPDE-1519.

signal.title: [WP] Read OTel thread local context records (OTEP 4947)
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds support for reading span/trace IDs from native applications using the OpenTelemetry Thread Local Context Record format (OTel spec #4947) in the CWS eBPF security module. The implementation adds a new eBPF read path that: Discovers the OTel TLSDESC TLS variable offset (registered by user-space) Dereferences the TLS pointer to locate the OTel Thread Local Context Record This targets native applications using ELF TLSDESC (C, C++, Rust, Java/JNI, .NET/FFI, Python native extensions). ### Motivation The OpenTelemetry specification defines a standard mechanism for SDKs to publish thread-level trace context (trace ID, span ID) through ELF Thread Local Storage so that out-of-process readers like eBPF probes can correlate security events with distributed traces. Supporting this standard allows CWS to automatically pick up span context from any OTel-instrumented native application without requiring Datadog-specific instrumentation. ### Describe how you validated your changes * All modified Go packages (probe/erpc, probe/constantfetch, ebpf/probes, ptracer, probe) build cleanly * The C syscall tester compiles successfully with the new otel-span-open command * Added a functional test (TestOTelSpan) that: * Creates a __thread TLS variable in C, computes its offset from fsbase via arch_prctl(ARCH_GET_FS) * Registers the offset with eBPF via the new REGISTER_OTEL_TLS_OP eRPC operation * Fills an OTel Thread Local Context Record with a known trace ID and span ID in W3C byte order * Triggers an open() syscall and verifies the correct trace/span IDs appear in the captured security event ### Additional Notes

signal.title: compliance/k8sconfig: tell an unreadable file from an empty one
signal.text: The loader stats a configuration file, reads it, then parses whatever it got. A read that fails, typically a permission denied on a root-owned kubeconfig, went to the errors list alone. Parsing an empty read yields an empty configuration, matching a file that really is empty, and the errors list stays out of reach of the rules. So an unreadable file quietly became a file holding nothing. detectManagedEnvironment falls back to the kubelet kubeconfig to recognize an EKS, GKE or AKS control plane when the node labels say nothing, and it walked the three empty maps of a manufactured kubeconfig to conclude that the node was unmanaged. Content that could not be read is now left out rather than parsed, so the detection sees an absent kubeconfig rather than invented evidence. Such a node is still reported as unmanaged: classifying it needs a resource type the rule set would have to define, which is a separate matter. The ownership and permissions from the stat are kept, which also fixes the benchmarks looking at them. They used to see a mode of zero for an unreadable kubelet configuration file and pass. Updates CSPDE-1519.

signal.title: fix(ebpf): synchronize perfUsageCollector.Collect with Manager.Start
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race between `perfUsageCollector.Collect` (reads PerfMap/RingBuffer telemetry fields during a Prometheus Gather tick) and `Manager.Start` (writes those fields during eBPF manager startup). Adds a shared `sync.Mutex` (`TelemetryMu`) in `pkg/ebpf` that both `Start` and `Collect` hold. It lives in `pkg/ebpf` to avoid a circular import (`pkg/ebpf/telemetry` already imports `pkg/ebpf`). ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes No unit test added — the race requires eBPF support to trigger (`Manager.Start` writes to PerfMap/RingBuffer internal fields that can't be constructed in a unit test). The race is eliminated by construction: `Collect` and `Start` now share the same mutex, so they can never access the telemetry fields concurrently.

signal.title: sbom: key the runtime enrichment dedup on bom-ref
signal.text: The enrichment merge rebuilds the component list of the image SBOM it annotates, emitting the first component of each name and normalised version and dropping the rest. Trivy reports one component per install location, so a library version pinned by two lockfiles arrives once per lockfile, each entry with its own bom-ref, and the merge kept one of them. The dependency graph, which the merge carries over as it stands, went on referencing the components that went missing. On the Agent image in the e2e fleet, 362 of its 2673 components share a name and version with another. Deduplicate the components that carry a bom-ref, which is what identifies a component in CycloneDX, and emit the others in turn. A byte-for-byte duplicate shares its bom-ref, so the stored SBOM the guard was added for still collapses.

signal.title: sbom: default runtime usage properties only on OS packages
signal.text: The enrichment merge copies the runtime usage properties onto the components the system-probe report covers, then defaults LastSeenRunning to "0" and HasSetSuidBit and RunningAsRoot to "false" on every other component of the image SBOM. The runtime scanner reads the dpkg, rpm and apk databases, so a "0" on a language package, on the image's operating-system component or on one of Trivy's per-lockfile application components claims the Agent watched a package outside its scope. Default the three properties on the components the report carried and on those whose purl marks them an OS package. The rest keep them absent, which a consumer reads as out of scope. Trivy maps every OS family onto the deb, rpm and apk purl types, so the prefix decides, and the SBOM e2e tests already use the same three.

signal.title: env: warn when a container socket exists but is not reachable
signal.text: Feature detection reports this with log.Infof, but it runs while the configuration is still loading, so the message is buffered and only filtered against the final log level once the logger is installed. On an Agent running at log_level warn it is discarded and never written anywhere. The condition deserves a warning. On Unix socket.IsAvailable calls a socket unreachable only when the dial fails with a permission error, so the Agent user cannot open it and container metrics, container image collection and container image vulnerability scanning are all silently disabled. Windows also counts a pipe that is merely busy, but a pipe the Agent cannot open in half a second is worth surfacing too.
signal.author: 0intro

signal.title: healthplatform: correct the docker permission issue impact
signal.text: The check that raises this issue detects an unreachable Docker socket, so the Agent cannot query the daemon at all and container metrics, container image collection and container image vulnerability scanning all go quiet. The impact named only the log tailing fallback, so an operator chasing missing images would read the issue and dismiss it. Worse, that fallback cannot happen. Socket tailing needs the very socket that is unreachable. Everything named is scoped to Docker. The check only proves that a default Docker socket exists and cannot be opened, not that Docker is the runtime in use, so a containerd or CRI-O node with a stale inaccessible socket keeps reporting all of it through its own collector. Title, Description and the remediation still describe the log directory case that the logs producer raised before 058e777637d removed it, and the remediation ACLs "<socket>/containers", which helps nobody whose dd-agent user is not in the docker group. Correcting those means replacing the embedded scripts, so they are left for a separate change.
signal.author: 0intro

signal.title: fix(rtloader): do not crash when formatting lone-surrogate Python exceptions
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a crash in rtloader when formatting a Python check exception whose message or traceback contains a Unicode lone surrogate (for example `\ud800`). `_fetchPythonError()` in `rtloader/three/three.cpp` converted traceback and exception strings with strict `as_string()`. Lone surrogates cannot be encoded as UTF-8, so conversion returned `NULL`, and appending that to a `std::string` caused a SIGSEGV in the core Agent process. This PR: - Adds `as_string_lossy()` in `rtloader/common/stringutils.c`, which encodes Unicode with UTF-8 `backslashreplace` for diagnostic paths. - Routes all exception formatting in `_fetchPythonError()` through a safe helper that skips on allocation failure. - Adds rtloader regression tests for lone-surrogate exceptions in `run_check` and `discover_config`. Strict `as_string()` behavior is unchanged for tags, metrics, events, and other hot paths. ### Motivation Reported by the rtloader vuln audit (`agent-vuln-hunt`, finding `rtloader-lone-surrogate-exception-crash`). A Python integration can raise an exception whose text embeds monitored-service data containing a lone surrogate (for example JSON `{"statusstring":"\ud800"}`). That should surface as a check error, but instead crashed the entire Agent on every scheduled run. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //rtloader/test/rtloader:rtloader_test` - `bazel test //rtloader/test/rtloader:rtloader_test --test_arg=-test.run='LoneSurrogate' --test_output=all` New tests: - `TestRunCheckLoneSurrogateException` - `TestDiscoverConfigRaisesLoneSurrogate` Both assert the Agent gets a Python error containing `\ud800` instead of crashing. ### Additional Notes - Release note: `releasenotes/notes/rtloader-lone-surrogate-exception-78250a6675432d3a.yaml` (`fixes`) - This closes the reported availability issue only. Other `as_string()` call sites already handle `NULL` without crashing and they may still drop or reject unencodable strings on non-exception paths.

signal.title: [Backport 7.82.x]  fix(windows): don't lock out the domain agent user account on upgrade
signal.text: Backport 5cf80f4c717f401d4af45d9ba42fb7c390d5fe13 from #55130. ___ ### What does this PR do? Makes the Windows MSI set `dd-procmgr-service`'s start type to **disabled** when the Agent user password is not available, and back to **demand start** once it is available again. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3052 #incident-59268 `dd-procmgr-service` created and runs as `ddagentuser` in 7.82.0 and, unlike the earlier services that hit this same class of bug (security-agent, DDOT, PAR), it **runs by default**. On a manual MSI upgrade that does not re-provide `DDAGENTUSER_PASSWORD` and has no LSA secret — the case for hosts first installed with **7.65 or earlier**, since only 7.66+ began storing it: 1. `InstallServices` creates the service with a domain account and an **empty password**. 2. `ConfigureServiceUsers` sees no password and passes `null` to `SetCredentials`, which leaves the empty password in place. 3. The service fails to log on (Event 7000/7038, Security 4625 substatus `0xC000006A`). 4. Failure actions are `restart` ×3 with `RestartServiceDelayInSeconds = 60`, but **`ResetPeriodInDays = 0`** makes the SCM reset the failure counter immediately, so it applies the *first* action forever and never exhausts the three restarts. Hence Event 7031 reporting *"It has done this 1 time(s)"* on every iteration, and an **unbounded 60-second retry loop**. 5. Five failed logons **lock out the account in about 4 minutes**, unattended, on a single host — and because it is a domain account, the Agent then fails to start on **every host sharing it**. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests** — new `CustomActions.Tests/Service/ProcmgrStartTypeTests.cs`, 8 cases: domain-without-password → `Disabled`; domain-with-password, **local-without-password**, gMSA and LocalSystem → `Manual`; `ERROR_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` swallowed; any other failure propagates; and no other service's start type is touched. **E2E, domain** — new `testUpgradeWithoutStoredPasswordSuite` in `tests/windows/domain-test` installs **7.65.2-1** with a domain account and password, upgrades **without** a password, then asserts that `dd-procmgr-service` start type is `SERVICE_DISABLED`, that the core Agent is healthy and payloads reach the fakeintake, and — as a positive control — that re-installing *with* the password restores `SERVICE_DEMAND_START` and the service starts. The existing `testUpgradeSuite` does not catch this, because it installs last stable (7.82.x), which already stores the LSA secret. **E2E, non-domain** — one assertion added to `install-test`'s `TestUpgrade`, which is the exact local-account analogue (default local `ddagentuser`, upgraded without a password), asserting the service **stays enabled**. **Manual QA — reproduced the bug, then verified the fix against it** Run on a domain VM (`WIN-Q4KDLA2CBJF.test.local`, domain account `TEST\ddagentuser`), as an A/B against an identical baseline. *A — unpatched build (7.82.2, unpatched).* Installed Agent **7.65.2** (pre-dates the LSA secret store, matching real affected hosts), then upgraded to 7.82.2 without re-supplying the password. Reproduced the exact incident signature: - System **7000 / 7031 / 7038** every 60s, each reporting *"done this 1 time(s)"* forever — the `ResetPeriodInDays = 0` behavior described above - Security **4625** sub-status `0xC000006A` from `services.exe` - **account locked out in ~4 minutes**, matching the incident report *B — this PR* (build from pipeline `132180801`, commit `c9e8439f`). Reset to the identical clean baseline and repeated the same no-password upgrade: - `dd-procmgr-service` came up **Disabled** instead of retry-looping - **zero** logon-failure events, `badPwdCount` stayed **0**, no lockout across a 5+ minute observation window - `datadogagent` kept running normally *Positive control.* Reinstalled the fixed build **with** the password supplied — `dd-procmgr-service` flipped back to **Manual** (demand start) and started successfully. ### Additional Notes **Why the MSI and not `pkg/fleet/installer`** (per `.claude/rules/msi.md`): For now it is a simpler fix to do in the MSI. Though doing it in the `pkg/fleet/installer` is possible and could be done instead. **Why disabling is safe:** every service uses `StartOn = null` / `StopOn = null`, `ConfigureServices` runs `When.After Step.InstallServices`, and `StartDDServices` runs later — so the service is disabled *before any logon attempt exists*. A disabled procmgr does not break the core Agent: `startDependentServices` only logs a warning when a dependent service fails to start. **Re-enabling is done by this custom action, not by MSI.** Services are *not* deleted and recreated on upgrade. Verified from the MSI logs of the E2E run: `DeleteServices` never executes, and after `RemoveExistingProducts` the `StopDDServices` pass still finds `datadogagent`, `datadog-trace-agent`, `datadog-process-agent`, `datadog-system-probe` and `datadog-security-agent` already present. That is also *why* the underlying bug is limited to newly added services — existing ones keep their stored credentials, which is exactly what would break fleet-wide if MSI rewrote them from the `ServiceInstall` table on every upgrade. So a disabled start type **does persist across upgrades**, and the `else` branch setting `Manual` is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: it is the only thing that brings procmgr back. Confirmed in the reinstall log: `ConfigureProcmgrStartType. Setting dd-procmgr-service start type to Manual`. This matters for #54735 / #54731: when procmgr moves to LocalSystem, that call must be **replaced with an unconditional enable, not deleted**. `passwordUnavailable` describes the Agent user, not the account the service runs as, so leaving it would disable a service that no longer needs a password — but deleting it outright would strand every host this fix disabled in a permanently disabled state. **Behavior change to be aware of:** while procmgr is disabled, DDOT / PAR / ADP do not run. **Rollback record is currently ommited:** For now we are just rolling back with the service disabled. As the service could be unhealthy in the previous state. So we are just leaving it disabled for now. **Not in this PR, follow-ups:** 1. An `agent status` warning when procmgr is disabled for this reason. 2. #54735 / #54731 run procmgr as LocalSystem with spawn profiles, removing the ddagentuser logon entirely. this MSI workaround can be relaxed once they land. 3. Should we add support for rollback Intended for backport to `7.82.x` for 7.82.3. Every production file touched is byte-identical between `main` and `origin/7.82.x`, so the cherry-pick should be conflict-free.

signal.title: [Backport 7.83.x]  Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signal.text: Backport f776f333c334087d4b4c2f66b7f5dbaf4c051df6 from #55014. ___ ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process can not resolve secret handles and expects to receive them from the core agent already resolved ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.

signal.title: sbom: warn when container image scanning has no container runtime
signal.text: Container image SBOMs come from images that workloadmeta discovers through the container runtime. With no runtime the collectors stay disabled, no image entity is ever created, and the check reports itself healthy while emitting only the host SBOM. A customer spent a week on a correct configuration because nothing said the images were never found. Warn once at configuration time. The gate is sbom.container_image.enabled, which defaults to false, rather than container_image.enabled, which defaults to true and would warn on nearly every host without containers. The check is only scheduled when sbom.enabled is true, so setting sbom.container_image.enabled on its own stays as silent as before. Only Docker, containerd and CRI-O build image SBOMs, so the runtime test names those three rather than calling IsAnyContainerFeaturePresent. That helper also answers true for Kubernetes, ECS, Cloud Foundry and Podman, and a Kubernetes node whose runtime socket is not mounted is precisely the case this warning exists for.

signal.title: Bump Bazel to 9.2.0  for remote cache and Windows fixes
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Bump the pinned Bazel version from 9.1.1 to 9.2.0 and refresh `MODULE.bazel.lock` accordingly. ### Motivation Bazel 9.2.0 ships fixes this repo has been working around over the past month. #### Windows issues Our contributions: - bazelbuild/bazel#29984, which should remove the need for temporary countermeasures we had to come up with: - DataDog/datadog-agent-buildimages#1212 (alas ineffective), - DataDog/datadog-agent-buildimages#1215 (effective), - #52500, - bazelbuild/bazel#30182, which should remove the need for: - #52061, - #53591. #### Caching issues - bazelbuild/bazel#29791, - bazelbuild/bazel#29868, - bazelbuild/bazel#29885, - bazelbuild/bazel#30193, a caveat mentioned in: - #53356. #### Others Also worth noting, though not tied to a specific incident here: - bazelbuild/bazel#29807, - bazelbuild/bazel#29898, - bazelbuild/bazel#30194. ### Describe how you validated your changes `bazel version` reports 9.2.0 after `bazelisk` re-bootstraps. `bazel build //pkg/config/schema/...` completes successfully. `bazel shutdown` followed by `bazel mod deps --lockfile_mode=refresh` leaves `MODULE.bazel.lock` unchanged. ### Additional Notes None of the .bazelrc UAC/8dot3 workarounds (DataDog/datadog-agent-buildimages#1215, #52500, #52061, #53591) are removed here. Each needs its own re-verification on Windows before being reverted as follow-ups.
signal.author: rdesgroppes

signal.title: Also stop the coverage job from thrashing Bazel analysis cache
signal.text: ### Motivation "Bazel analysis cache thrashing on `main` (containerized job)" keeps alerting after #54963 ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1963914110)): all 49 occurrences of the last 24 hours come from `bazel:coverage:linux-amd64`, which now flips `cover_format`, `--collect_code_coverage` and `--instrumentation_filter`. The last one `bazel coverage` derives from the target patterns, some 400 package regexes that a post-test command cannot replay. ### What does this PR do? Skip `test2json` and UTOF where their `bazel run` cannot match the test invocation, which is only the coverage job: its tests are a **subset** of `bazel:test:linux-amd64`, still reporting them, while its JUnit tar needs no Bazel and its coverage profile only `bazel info`, which analyzes nothing. Guard the remaining `bazel run` with `--noallow_analysis_cache_discard`, turning a future divergence into a failure of the job that introduces it, rather than a warning nobody reads until a monitor fires hours later on `main` pipelines. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv bazel.process-test-results --result-json=` runs no Bazel and still packages JUnit, while a non-empty one keeps converting logs. With the server left in the coverage configuration, the guarded command exits 2 on "analysis cache would have been discarded", and stays silent after `bazel test --config=gorace`. ### Additional Notes The guard is safe for the four `bazel:test:*` jobs: `INSTALL_DIR` and `AGENT_FLAVOR` are set by packaging jobs only, so `omnibazel_flags` injects nothing there, and neither monitor has reported a flip in those jobs since #54963.

signal.text: ## Stack - Base: #55153 (`nubtron/remote-queries-intake-poc`) - This draft: test-only deterministic relay proof ## Summary - drive exact 8 MiB and 32 MiB producer streams through the actual relay - verify bounded chunking, aggregate hashing, receipt-only output, and backpressure - cover rejection-before-accept and lost-response-after-accept idempotent retries ## Validation - 135 focused package tests passed after the production lint fix was merged - synthetic M3/M5 proof passed all cases - lint and reliabilint passed - signed commits independently reviewed ## Deployment Test-only local proof tooling; no production deployment.

signal.title: fix(lint_windows-x64): move `cwdLogLimiter` out of shared file
signal.text: ### Motivation Despite #55076 and #55162, `lint_windows-x64` still fails, this time on the system-probe go linter step ([example](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/jobs/1971344465)): ``` Linter failures: pkg\network\sender\event_consumer.go:96:5: var cwdLogLimiter is unused (unused) var cwdLogLimiter = logutil.NewLogLimit(20, 10*time.Minute) ^ 1 issues: * unused: 1 system-probe Go linter result is 1 system-probe go linter failed 1 ``` `event_consumer.go` builds under `linux || (windows && npm)`, but `cwdLogLimiter` is only read from `event_consumer_linux.go`, whose `_linux.go` suffix restricts it to `GOOS=linux`: the `windows && npm` build declares the limiter and never uses it. ### What does this PR do? Move the `cwdLogLimiter` declaration, and its now-unused `time` and `logutil` imports, from `event_consumer.go` into `event_consumer_linux.go`, next to its only caller. ### Describe how you validated your changes `dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/network/sender/...`

signal.title: [VULN-95338] Remove curl from cluster-agent container
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Stop adding curl to the cluster-agent container. This is theoretically a no-op change, as the agent does not use the system provided curl directly, nor should any of the integrations we ship. In practice, however, people ssh-ing to the container might expect curl to be there. Or, user installed integrations might. OTOH, users making their own containers with more integrations can install the curl they feel safe with as part of that. ### Motivation Vex scan https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/VULN-95338 ### Describe how you validated your changes - CI - Scan should clear in a few days - we have to merge and wait

signal.title: fix(windows): don't lock out the domain agent user account on upgrade
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Makes the Windows MSI set `dd-procmgr-service`'s start type to **disabled** when the Agent user password is not available, and back to **demand start** once it is available again. ### Motivation https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3052 #incident-59268 `dd-procmgr-service` created and runs as `ddagentuser` in 7.82.0 and, unlike the earlier services that hit this same class of bug (security-agent, DDOT, PAR), it **runs by default**. On a manual MSI upgrade that does not re-provide `DDAGENTUSER_PASSWORD` and has no LSA secret — the case for hosts first installed with **7.65 or earlier**, since only 7.66+ began storing it: 1. `InstallServices` creates the service with a domain account and an **empty password**. 2. `ConfigureServiceUsers` sees no password and passes `null` to `SetCredentials`, which leaves the empty password in place. 3. The service fails to log on (Event 7000/7038, Security 4625 substatus `0xC000006A`). 4. Failure actions are `restart` ×3 with `RestartServiceDelayInSeconds = 60`, but **`ResetPeriodInDays = 0`** makes the SCM reset the failure counter immediately, so it applies the *first* action forever and never exhausts the three restarts. Hence Event 7031 reporting *"It has done this 1 time(s)"* on every iteration, and an **unbounded 60-second retry loop**. 5. Five failed logons **lock out the account in about 4 minutes**, unattended, on a single host — and because it is a domain account, the Agent then fails to start on **every host sharing it**. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests** — new `CustomActions.Tests/Service/ProcmgrStartTypeTests.cs`, 8 cases: domain-without-password → `Disabled`; domain-with-password, **local-without-password**, gMSA and LocalSystem → `Manual`; `ERROR_SERVICE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` swallowed; any other failure propagates; and no other service's start type is touched. **E2E, domain** — new `testUpgradeWithoutStoredPasswordSuite` in `tests/windows/domain-test` installs **7.65.2-1** with a domain account and password, upgrades **without** a password, then asserts that `dd-procmgr-service` start type is `SERVICE_DISABLED`, that the core Agent is healthy and payloads reach the fakeintake, and — as a positive control — that re-installing *with* the password restores `SERVICE_DEMAND_START` and the service starts. The existing `testUpgradeSuite` does not catch this, because it installs last stable (7.82.x), which already stores the LSA secret. **E2E, non-domain** — one assertion added to `install-test`'s `TestUpgrade`, which is the exact local-account analogue (default local `ddagentuser`, upgraded without a password), asserting the service **stays enabled**. **Manual QA — reproduced the bug, then verified the fix against it** Run on a domain VM (`WIN-Q4KDLA2CBJF.test.local`, domain account `TEST\ddagentuser`), as an A/B against an identical baseline. *A — unpatched build (7.82.2, unpatched).* Installed Agent **7.65.2** (pre-dates the LSA secret store, matching real affected hosts), then upgraded to 7.82.2 without re-supplying the password. Reproduced the exact incident signature: - System **7000 / 7031 / 7038** every 60s, each reporting *"done this 1 time(s)"* forever — the `ResetPeriodInDays = 0` behavior described above - Security **4625** sub-status `0xC000006A` from `services.exe` - **account locked out in ~4 minutes**, matching the incident report *B — this PR* (build from pipeline `132180801`, commit `c9e8439f`). Reset to the identical clean baseline and repeated the same no-password upgrade: - `dd-procmgr-service` came up **Disabled** instead of retry-looping - **zero** logon-failure events, `badPwdCount` stayed **0**, no lockout across a 5+ minute observation window - `datadogagent` kept running normally *Positive control.* Reinstalled the fixed build **with** the password supplied — `dd-procmgr-service` flipped back to **Manual** (demand start) and started successfully. ### Additional Notes **Why the MSI and not `pkg/fleet/installer`** (per `.claude/rules/msi.md`): For now it is a simpler fix to do in the MSI. Though doing it in the `pkg/fleet/installer` is possible and could be done instead. **Why disabling is safe:** every service uses `StartOn = null` / `StopOn = null`, `ConfigureServices` runs `When.After Step.InstallServices`, and `StartDDServices` runs later — so the service is disabled *before any logon attempt exists*. A disabled procmgr does not break the core Agent: `startDependentServices` only logs a warning when a dependent service fails to start. **Re-enabling is done by this custom action, not by MSI.** Services are *not* deleted and recreated on upgrade. Verified from the MSI logs of the E2E run: `DeleteServices` never executes, and after `RemoveExistingProducts` the `StopDDServices` pass still finds `datadogagent`, `datadog-trace-agent`, `datadog-process-agent`, `datadog-system-probe` and `datadog-security-agent` already present. That is also *why* the underlying bug is limited to newly added services — existing ones keep their stored credentials, which is exactly what would break fleet-wide if MSI rewrote them from the `ServiceInstall` table on every upgrade. So a disabled start type **does persist across upgrades**, and the `else` branch setting `Manual` is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces: it is the only thing that brings procmgr back. Confirmed in the reinstall log: `ConfigureProcmgrStartType. Setting dd-procmgr-service start type to Manual`. This matters for #54735 / #54731: when procmgr moves to LocalSystem, that call must be **replaced with an unconditional enable, not deleted**. `passwordUnavailable` describes the Agent user, not the account the service runs as, so leaving it would disable a service that no longer needs a password — but deleting it outright would strand every host this fix disabled in a permanently disabled state. **Behavior change to be aware of:** while procmgr is disabled, DDOT / PAR / ADP do not run. **Rollback record is currently ommited:** For now we are just rolling back with the service disabled. As the service could be unhealthy in the previous state. So we are just leaving it disabled for now. **Not in this PR, follow-ups:** 1. An `agent status` warning when procmgr is disabled for this reason. 2. #54735 / #54731 run procmgr as LocalSystem with spawn profiles, removing the ddagentuser logon entirely. this MSI workaround can be relaxed once they land. 3. Should we add support for rollback Intended for backport to `7.82.x` for 7.82.3. Every production file touched is byte-identical between `main` and `origin/7.82.x`, so the cherry-pick should be conflict-free.

signal.title: add support so DDOT attaches grpc status code tags(rpc.grpc.status_code)
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? This PR adds support so DDOT attaches grpc status code tags(rpc.grpc.status_code). As described in this [ticket](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTELS-685), rpc.grpc.status_code tags were reported to be lost in trace metrics for the DDOT routing method and were showing up as N/A. Now, the grpc status codes are shown properly. The screenshot shows the behaviour after the changes. As well, this ticket adds support for rpc.response.status_code from the latest convention and to interpret it as a gRPC status code only if rpc.system.name is grpc. If rpc.system.name is grpc, it is able to interpret different rpc.response.status_code values: If rpc.system.name is jsonrpc, it is not able to interpret rpc.response.status_code values: Also, this ensures that jsonrpc systems are still able to interpret regular rpc.grpc.status_code values: ### Motivation ### Describe how you validated your changes Tested it locally by running the Otel collector with a sample app service to either pass rpc.response.status_code with an grpc rpc system, confirming it is interpreted as gRPC status code. With a non grpc rpc system, confirmed it is not interpreted. An then ran both systems passing rpc.response.status_code to confirm it shows up for both. ### Additional Notes
